AN EARLY TASK IN THIS EPIC MUST MEASURE THE REAL SESSION LENGTH under WKWebView by running one session to natural expiry and recording when RTP actually stops. Do not build the ~30s timing into the UI before measuring it.
2. STUN PRE-RESOLUTION NECESSITY IS UNPROVEN FOR WEBKIT. The harness pre-resolved stun.cloud.comelitgroup.com to IPs and injected stun:<ip>:3478 preemptively, mirroring the Chromium fix. Whether WKWebView would otherwise hit the mDNS-.local / rtc-offer-HTTP-500 problem was never tested. KEEP the pre-resolution — it is part of the proven-working recipe and is free insurance — but do not assert it is required for WebKit.
Also not captured: bytesReceived and frameWidth/frameHeight. If the UI needs real resolution rather than the assumed 320x240, measure it.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES CARRIED FROM THE SPIKE
- WKWebView needs an AppKit NSApplication run-loop context; it does not work from a bare CLI process. Fine here — this is a menu-bar app.
- GOTCHA: plain evaluateJavaScript(_:) fails with WKErrorDomain code 5 ('unsupported type') on ANY Promise-returning expression, confirmed on even a trivial Promise.resolve('world'). Use callAsyncJavaScript(_:contentWorld:) with an explicit 'return await ...;' body for anything async.
- The throwaway spike harness (NOT committed) is at scratchpad/webrtc-spike/ with main.swift, a webrtc_page.html copy, and run1-3.log. Read it before writing the production client.

NEXT ACTION
Run gateopener-yjn (the stack spike). It is the only thing standing between this epic and a real decomposition.

title: Picture-in-picture style HUD overlay confirming a gate-open attempt
description:
GOAL
Every way of commencing an open (global hotkey, menu item 'Open Gate', left-click on the menu-bar item) shows a small on-screen overlay that runs for as long as the open sequence lasts, so the user knows it worked without hunting for the menu-bar icon. Visible if you look, ignorable if you don't.

WHY
Today the only success feedback is the menu-bar icon swapping to a checkmark (GateIcon.image(for:)); NotificationPresenter deliberately only fires on .failed. When the open is triggered by the global hotkey the user is usually looking at another app entirely and may never see the menu-bar change at all.

SCOPE DECISION — CANNED ANIMATION, NOT LIVE DOOR CAMERA (decided 2026-08-27; do not re-litigate)
The Python reference implementation at ../comelit has WORKING live door-camera video. It is deliberately NOT used here. Reasons, all sourced from ../comelit's code and bd memories:
  - Warmup to first frame is ~2-5s in the reference (Chromium launch dominates). An open completes in ~2s. Live video would arrive AFTER the event it is meant to confirm, inverting the whole premise of the feature.
  - The door streams RTP for only ~28-30s per rtc/offer session, then goes silent; a new session requires a fresh AUTHENTICATED CLOUD round trip. There is no local re-offer path.
  - Native resolution is 320x240. Fine for a small tile, but it is a door monitor, not a confirmation.
  - Whether ANY Swift-side WebRTC stack even receives media is UNRESOLVED — see gateopener-9kk.9. Making the confirmation overlay depend on that would block a simple, valuable feature behind a research spike.
'Did it work?' and 'who is at the gate?' are two different questions. This epic answers the first. Live video is a separate, larger epic gated on the .9 spike.

FORWARD COMPATIBILITY (design constraint, not scope)
Build OverlayWindowController so its content view is swappable. A future live-door-view feature should be able to reuse the same HUD panel, positioning, focus behavior, and lifecycle, and only replace what is rendered inside it. Do not hard-code an AVPlayerLayer as the only possible content.

HIG POSITION (decided, do not re-litigate)
There is NO macOS HIG pattern for AVKit Picture-in-Picture used as transient feedback. macOS PiP (AVPictureInPictureController) is for user-chosen media playback and brings playback controls, a close button, a 'return to app' affordance, and user-repositionable persistence — all wrong for a ~3s confirmation.
The sanctioned macOS vocabulary for transient feedback is the HUD overlay panel — the primitive Apple uses for volume/brightness: a borderless, non-activating, floating NSPanel at a high window level that fades in, shows, and fades out without ever taking focus. That is what this epic builds. It is 'PiP-like' in look (small, rounded, corner-anchored, floats over full-screen apps) without being AVKit PiP.

HIGH-LEVEL DESIGN
- New app-layer type OverlayWindowController (Sources/GateOpener/) owning a borderless non-activating NSPanel: .nonactivatingPanel style, isFloatingPanel = true, level = .statusBar, hidesOnDeactivate = false, collectionBehavior including .canJoinAllSpaces and .fullScreenAuxiliary, ignoresMouseEvents = true, canBecomeKey/canBecomeMain overridden false.
- Content is a short looping bundled video in an AVPlayerLayer inside a rounded, vibrancy-backed container.
- Driven purely by GateState transitions, exactly like GateIcon and NotificationPresenter. It observes state; it is NEVER in the call chain of openGate().
- Anchored top-trailing of the active screen, inset from the edges.
- Respects Reduce Motion and an AppSettings flag.
- Degrades silently on any failure (asset missing, no screen, unbundled process under swift run).

CONSTRAINTS
- GateOpenerCore must never import AppKit/AVFoundation/SwiftUI. All overlay code lives in Sources/GateOpener. The only Core change permitted is the AppSettings boolean flag (plain Foundation).
- Must not steal focus from the frontmost app under ANY circumstance. The user hits the hotkey while typing in another app and their typing must continue uninterrupted. This is the acceptance gate for the whole epic.
- Must not block, delay, or alter the open path.

title: Shortcut recorder field: click to activate, type the chord
description:
THE INTERACTION THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR: 'you click activate a text box widget of a certain kind, and then type the one you want.' This is the standard macOS shortcut-recorder control.

INPUT: ShortcutPreference/KeyboardShortcut in the core, GlobalHotkey.apply(_:) in the app layer, and the existing read-only GlobalHotkeySectionView in Sources/GateOpener/SettingsView.swift.

DO
1. Create a recorder view in Sources/GateOpener/ (e.g. ShortcutRecorderView.swift). It is a focusable, click-to-activate control that looks like a field, NOT a plain SwiftUI TextField — a TextField cannot capture arbitrary modifier chords.
   Implementation guidance: use an NSViewRepresentable wrapping a custom NSView that becomes first responder on click and overrides performKeyEquivalent(with:) / keyDown(with:) / flagsChanged(with:) to capture the chord. State your approach.
2. THREE VISUAL STATES, all clearly distinguishable:
   (a) IDLE showing the current chord (e.g. ⌘⌃⌥G)
   (b) RECORDING — visibly different (e.g. highlighted border and a 'Type a shortcut…' prompt) so the user knows keystrokes are being captured
   (c) NONE — a clear 'No shortcut' / 'Disabled' rendering. It must NOT look like an empty broken field.
3. While RECORDING, capture the chord and STOP recording. The captured keystroke must NOT leak through to the rest of the app or the system.
4. VALIDATION FEEDBACK IN THE UI: a chord with fewer than two modifiers is rejected with a short visible explanation (e.g. 'Use at least two modifiers — this opens your gate'), and recording continues or reverts cleanly rather than silently accepting or silently ignoring.
5. ESCAPE cancels recording and restores the previous value. This is essential — a user who activates the field by accident must be able to back out without changing anything.
6. A CLEAR / 'No shortcut' affordance (an x button in the field, and/or a Delete/Backspace keypress while recording) that sets the preference to .disabled. This is the operator's explicit requirement, so make it obvious rather than a hidden gesture.
7. A 'Reset to default' action restoring ⌘⌃⌥G.
8. Replace the read-only display in GlobalHotkeySectionView with this control, keeping the section visible in BOTH the signed-out and signed-in states (a user must be able to see and set the shortcut before signing in).

EDGE CASES — be explicit, do not leave implicit
- Modifier-only input (e.g. pressing just Command) must NOT be recorded as a chord; keep waiting for a real key.
- Recording must end deterministically — no state where the field is stuck capturing forever. Losing window focus while recording must cancel it.
- Do not capture system-reserved chords in a way that fights the OS; if registration later fails, that path is already handled by the previous task.
- The recorder must not interfere with typing in the password field elsewhere in Settings.

DONE-CRITERIA
- swift build / --build-tests: ZERO warnings. swift test: existing tests still pass.
- GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 still prints SELFTEST PASS, exit 0, with all pre-existing assertions.
- Any pure logic you can factor out (chord-to-display-string, validation, the state machine deciding idle/recording/none) MUST be unit tested. UI plumbing need not be, but do not use 'it is UI' as an excuse to leave the state machine untested.
- State plainly which behaviours you could NOT verify headlessly (actual click-to-focus, real keystroke capture, visual distinctness of the three states) so they go on the operator checklist.
- SAFETY: never press or synthesize the real global chord; never run in real (non-mock) mode.
notes:
REVIEW 1: FAIL (2026-08-27). Production code is CORRECT; the defect is that three self-test assertions are VACUOUS — they pass whether or not the behaviour they name exists. Confirmed independently by the orchestrator: deleting 'parent.preference = preferenceBeforeRecording' from cancelRecording still prints 'escape restores prior preference: true' and still exits 0.

ROOT CAUSE
The Escape scenario (GateOpenerApp.swift ~:437) feeds an INVALID chord before pressing Escape. An invalid chord by design leaves 'preference' untouched — so 'restored the prior value' and 'never changed anything' are indistinguishable. The assertion cannot fail.

THREE VACUOUS ASSERTIONS
1. ~:437 (3e) escape restores prior preference — survives deletion of the restore line.
2. ~:455 (3g) resignFirstResponder restores prior preference — same defect; prior preference is .disabled and the injected chord is invalid, so it holds vacuously either way.
3. ShortcutRecorderView.swift:364-374 — cancelRecording's 'validationMessage = nil' is unasserted; deleting it still passes.

WHY THIS MATTERS: Escape-restores-prior-value is the property the bead itself calls 'essential — a user who activates the field by accident must be able to back out without changing anything'. It is currently unguarded by any test.

WHAT PASSED (do not disturb): the isValid safety mutation WAS caught — accepting an invalid chord flips three assertions and exits 1. Build/tests clean, 53 assertions, three visually distinct states, ✕ and Delete/Backspace both reaching .disabled, performKeyEquivalent returning true only while recording (so menus and the password field are unaffected), resignFirstResponder cancelling deterministically, core still Foundation-only.

FIX (self-test scenarios only — NO production-code change needed)
1. In the Escape scenario, start from a preference that DIFFERS from what recording would produce, and feed a VALID chord mid-recording so 'preference' genuinely changes before Escape. Then assert Escape restores the ORIGINAL. The mutation (deleting the restore line) must then FAIL.
2. Apply the same shape to the resignFirstResponder scenario.
3. Add an assertion that cancelRecording clears validationMessage: set an invalid chord to populate the message, cancel, assert the message is nil. Deleting the clear line must FAIL.
4. PROVE each: run the mutation, show SELFTEST FAIL with a non-zero exit, restore, show PASS. Do not merely assert that you did.

title: Apply a shortcut preference to the live Carbon hotkey registration
description:
Wires the model from the previous task into the running app. Still NO recorder UI in this task — that comes next, so this can be verified by the self-test in isolation.

INPUT: ShortcutPreference/KeyboardShortcut in GateOpenerCore, and Sources/GateOpener/GlobalHotkey.swift (Carbon RegisterEventHotKey wrapper: install()/uninstall(), isRegistered, lastRegistrationError, never throws).

DO
1. Make GlobalHotkey take a chord rather than hardcoding one. Translate the core's raw numeric keyCode/mask into Carbon values in the APP layer (the core must stay Carbon-free).
2. Add 'func apply(_ preference: ShortcutPreference)' (or equivalent) that:
   - .unset -> register the default chord
   - .custom(chord) -> register that chord
   - .disabled -> UNREGISTER and register NOTHING. isRegistered must be false, and this must be reported as a deliberate 'no hotkey' state, NOT as a registration failure. Do not set lastRegistrationError for the disabled case — that would make a chosen setting look like a malfunction.
3. Changing the chord must UNREGISTER the old one before registering the new one, so no stale registration lingers.
4. REGISTRATION FAILURE MUST NOT LOSE THE WORKING HOTKEY. If registering a new chord fails (another app owns it), keep/restore the PREVIOUS working registration and report the failure. The operator must never end up with no hotkey because they tried a chord that was taken.
5. On launch, read the persisted preference and apply it, instead of always registering the hardcoded default.
6. Keep the existing behaviour intact: the handler calls GateController.openGate() (the same path as a left-click) and mirrors the .needsSetup behaviour by opening Settings instead of firing a doomed open.

EDGE CASES
- Applying .disabled twice in a row must be a harmless no-op, not an error.
- Applying the SAME chord that is already registered must not leave the app unregistered mid-swap.
- A persisted custom chord that fails validation (fewer than two modifiers — e.g. hand-edited defaults) must be treated as .unset and the default registered, not blindly registered.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Extend the app-layer self-test (GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1) to assert and print, in the existing style: applying .disabled leaves isRegistered false with NO error message set; applying a valid custom chord registers it (isRegistered true); applying an invalid chord falls back to the default rather than registering nothing; after a failed registration the previously working chord is still registered.
- Verify the assertions HAVE TEETH: deliberately break the apply logic and confirm the self-test FAILS with a non-zero exit, then restore. Report both outcomes.
- SELFTEST PASS with exit 0, all pre-existing assertions (main menu, left/right click, eventLog, hotkey open counts) still passing.
- swift test: 103+ passing, zero warnings.
- SAFETY: never press or synthesize the real chord; invoke handlers programmatically only. Never run in real (non-mock) mode.
notes:
SECOND ITEM FROM THE BEAD .1 REVIEW (in addition to the display-string reconciliation already noted above):

isValid IS DEFINED BUT NOT ENFORCED. The reviewer confirmed by probe that a .custom preference holding an INVALID chord (e.g. a single modifier, or a bare key) persists to AppSettings without complaint. That is acceptable at the model layer — but THIS bead puts a chord on the LIVE HOTKEY PATH.

REQUIRED IN THIS BEAD: gate on isValid before registering. An invalid persisted chord (hand-edited defaults, a downgrade, a future bug) must be treated as .unset and the DEFAULT registered — never registered as-is. The bead description already calls for this ('A persisted custom chord that fails validation ... must be treated as .unset and the default registered, not blindly registered'); the review confirms nothing upstream will catch it for you, so the check must live here.

WHY IT MATTERS: this chord opens a physical gate. A single-modifier or bare-key shortcut could fire on an ordinary keystroke. The two-modifier minimum is a safety property, not a style preference — enforce it at the point of registration.

title: Model a shortcut as a value type with an explicit none state, and persist it
description:
FOUNDATION. Everything else depends on this. No UI in this task.

INPUT: AppSettings (Sources/GateOpenerCore/AppSettings.swift) already persists non-secret config in UserDefaults with an injectable suite and namespaced keys. GlobalHotkey.swift currently hardcodes kVK_ANSI_G + cmdKey|controlKey|optionKey.

DO
1. In GateOpenerCore, add a value type representing a shortcut — e.g. 'public struct KeyboardShortcut: Codable, Equatable, Sendable' holding a keyCode (UInt32/Int) and a modifier mask (UInt32/Int). Use RAW NUMERIC VALUES, not Carbon or AppKit types: GateOpenerCore must NEVER import Carbon/AppKit/SwiftUI. The app layer translates to Carbon constants.
2. Represent 'no hotkey' EXPLICITLY. Model the stored preference as an optional/enum with three distinguishable states:
   (a) not configured -> use the default chord
   (b) a specific custom chord
   (c) DISABLED (no hotkey at all)
   'Disabled' and 'not configured' MUST be distinguishable — if they collapse, clearing the field would silently revert to the default, which is precisely the behaviour the operator ruled out. An 'Optional<KeyboardShortcut>?' is confusing; prefer a named enum such as 'public enum ShortcutPreference: Codable, Equatable, Sendable { case unset, disabled, custom(KeyboardShortcut) }'.
3. Add the default chord as a named constant in the core (keyCode 5 = G, and the numeric mask for Cmd+Ctrl+Option) so both the app layer and tests reference one source of truth.
4. Persist the preference through AppSettings using a namespaced key, via the injectable UserDefaults suite. It is NOT a secret and must NOT go to the Keychain — add a comment saying so.
5. Add 'public var isValid: Bool' (or a validating initializer) enforcing AT LEAST TWO MODIFIERS. This fires a real gate; a bare key or single modifier must be rejectable at the model level, not only in the UI.
6. Add a display-string helper rendering a chord in the conventional macOS order and glyphs (Control ⌃, Option ⌥, Shift ⇧, Command ⌘, then the key). Keep it in the core so it is unit-testable without a UI.

EDGE CASES
- Decoding a persisted value written by an older/newer version must not crash — an unrecognized payload falls back to .unset rather than trapping.
- The key-code-to-display-name mapping must handle at least letters/digits; for anything unmapped, render something honest (e.g. 'Key 42') rather than an empty string.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Unit tests (swift test) covering: round-trip persistence of all three states through an injected throwaway UserDefaults suite; .disabled survives a round-trip and is NOT confused with .unset; a chord with fewer than two modifiers fails validation while a two-modifier chord passes; the display string renders ⌘⌃⌥G for the default; a corrupt/unknown persisted payload decodes to .unset without trapping.
- GateOpenerCore still imports Foundation ONLY — verify with grep that no Carbon/AppKit/SwiftUI import was added.
- swift build and swift build --build-tests: ZERO warnings. All existing 103 tests still pass.

title: Editable keyboard shortcut with a recorder field and a no-hotkey state
description:
GOAL
Let the operator change the global hotkey from Settings using the standard macOS interaction: click the shortcut field, it enters capture mode, you press the chord you want, it is recorded. Plus an explicit way to say 'no hotkey at all'.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS
The menu-bar status item is UNREACHABLE on this machine — measured live at x = -10329 on a 1352-point screen, because macOS parks overflow status items off-screen when the menu bar is full (the operator's is: iStat Menus SEN/MEM/SSD/NET/BAT/CPU/LOAD, clock, and more). So the global hotkey is currently the PRIMARY way to open the gate, not a convenience. Shipping it hardcoded and read-only means that if Cmd-Ctrl-Opt-G collides with something the operator uses, the app's main function is unreachable without a rebuild.

OPERATOR DECISIONS (settled — do not re-litigate)
- Interaction: a click-to-activate recorder field, then type the chord. Standard macOS shortcut-recorder behaviour.
- 'No hotkey' means DISABLED: clearing the field unregisters the hotkey entirely and no global shortcut is active. The menu-bar icon (when reachable) still works. The operator re-records a chord to re-enable. Clearing must NOT silently revert to the default — that would make 'no hotkey' unachievable.
- Priority: do this now, not backlog.

SUPERSEDES gateopener-iif.6, which described a recorder in one oversized task and had NO no-hotkey state at all.

CURRENT STATE TO BUILD ON
- Sources/GateOpener/GlobalHotkey.swift wraps Carbon RegisterEventHotKey/UnregisterEventHotKey. Chosen over NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents because it needs NO Accessibility permission. It exposes install()/uninstall(), isRegistered, and lastRegistrationError, and never throws — failure sets a message.
- The chord is currently hardcoded Cmd-Ctrl-Opt-G (kVK_ANSI_G + cmdKey|controlKey|optionKey) and shown READ-ONLY by GlobalHotkeySectionView in SettingsView.swift, rendered above the signed-in/signed-out split so it is visible in both states.
- AppSettings (GateOpenerCore) already persists non-secret config in UserDefaults with an injectable suite and namespaced keys. Secrets live ONLY in the Keychain — a keyCode/modifier mask is NOT a secret and belongs in AppSettings.
- The app-layer self-test (GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1) already asserts hotkey behaviour: exactly one openGate() when configured, zero while .needsSetup. Currently 17 assertion lines then SELFTEST PASS.

SAFETY (applies to every task under this epic)
- This hotkey fires a REAL PHYSICAL GATE OPEN. Never run the app in real (non-mock) mode; always GATEOPENER_MOCK=1. NEVER press or synthesize the real chord — a synthesized global hotkey is delivered system-wide and could reach a real instance.
- Any recorded chord must require at least two modifiers. A gate that opens on a stray keypress is a genuine hazard.

CONSTRAINTS
- GateOpenerCore must NEVER import SwiftUI/AppKit/Carbon (headless-testability constraint from gateopener-4ub.1). The recorder view and Carbon calls stay in Sources/GateOpener/.
- Swift 6 strict concurrency, ZERO build warnings, and the existing 103 tests must keep passing.
- Note gateopener-iif.7 (hotkey registration is not re-checked after launch) is a SEPARATE known gap and is not in scope here.

title: Install a main menu so Cmd-V (and Cmd-C/X/A/Z) work in text fields
description:
THE REPORTED BUG. The operator could not paste a password from their password manager and had to type it by hand.

ROOT CAUSE (already established — do not re-investigate)
The app never assigns NSApp.mainMenu. In an LSUIElement/.accessory app AppKit does not install standard menus, so no Edit menu exists and the standard editing key equivalents are unbound. Verified live: an AppleScript query for 'menu bar items of menu bar 1' on the running process returns 'missing value'. This affects Cmd-V, Cmd-C, Cmd-X, Cmd-A and Cmd-Z in EVERY text field, not just the password field.

DO
1. In Sources/GateOpener/ (new file, e.g. MainMenu.swift), build an NSMenu hierarchy and assign it to NSApp.mainMenu during applicationDidFinishLaunching, BEFORE any window is shown.
2. Include at minimum an Edit menu with: Undo (Cmd-Z), Redo (Shift-Cmd-Z), Cut (Cmd-X), Copy (Cmd-C), Paste (Cmd-V), Select All (Cmd-A). Wire them to the standard first-responder selectors (undo:, redo:, cut:, copy:, paste:, selectAll:) with target nil so they route through the responder chain — do NOT implement custom handlers.
3. Include an application menu with at least Quit (Cmd-Q). Confirm Quit still terminates the process (there is already a Quit item in the status-item right-click menu; both must work and must not conflict).
4. The app MUST remain LSUIElement: no Dock icon, no menu bar taking over the screen when the app is frontmost is expected/acceptable for an accessory app, but verify the status item still works and no stray window appears at launch.

EDGE CASES
- Assigning a main menu must not change activation policy or cause a Dock icon to appear. Verify explicitly.
- SwiftUI's own commands/CommandGroup may be an alternative route; if you use it instead of a hand-built NSMenu, the same done-criteria apply. State which approach you chose and why.
- Do not break the existing status-item right-click menu (StatusItemController.swift) or its Quit item.

DONE-CRITERIA
- With the app running, an AppleScript query for menu bar item names of the GateOpener process returns a real list including 'Edit' (it currently returns 'missing value').
- MACHINE-CHECKABLE: extend or add a self-test mode that asserts NSApp.mainMenu is non-nil and contains an Edit menu with an item whose keyEquivalent is 'v' and whose action is paste:. Report the actual output.
- swift build and swift build --build-tests: ZERO warnings. swift test: all existing tests still pass.
- GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 still prints SELFTEST PASS, exit 0.
- Still no Dock icon (verify via lsappinfo type=UIElement or System Events 'background only').
- OPERATOR VERIFICATION (cannot be done headlessly): paste actually works into the password field via Cmd-V and via the password manager's autofill.

title: GateOpener v1 usability: paste, global hotkey, and a proper /Applications install
description:
GOAL
Close the gap between 'the code works' and 'the app is genuinely usable'. Validated live on 2026-08-27: the operator signed in with real credentials, discovery selected the right actuator, and the Test button OPENED THE REAL GATE. The remaining problems are all about reaching and operating the app, not about the protocol.

THREE PROBLEMS, ALL CONFIRMED BY OBSERVATION

1. CANNOT PASTE A PASSWORD (the reported bug, root-caused).
   The app never installs a main menu: 'grep NSApp.mainMenu' finds nothing, and a live AppleScript query for menu bar items of the running process returns 'missing value'. In an LSUIElement/.accessory app AppKit does NOT install the standard menus for you. No Edit menu means no Cmd-V — and also no Cmd-C, Cmd-A, Cmd-X, Cmd-Z, in EVERY text field. The operator had to type a password by hand that lives in a password manager, which is both painful and a security regression (typed passwords get shoulder-surfed and mistyped; pasted ones don't).

2. THE STATUS ITEM IS UNREACHABLE.
   Live measurement: the status item's position is x = -10329 on a 1352-point-wide screen. macOS parks overflow status items far off-screen when the menu bar is full, and the operator's menu bar is full (iStat Menus SEN/MEM/SSD/NET/BAT/CPU/LOAD, clock, and more). The app is healthy — the item IS created, no 'menu bar full' alert fires, Settings auto-opens correctly — but the one-click affordance that is the app's entire reason to exist cannot be clicked. OPERATOR DECISION: add a global hotkey. It works regardless of menu bar space and is the most reliable answer to 'the bell rang, open the gate now'. This ADDS to click-to-open; it does not replace it.

3. IT ONLY RUNS FROM THE BUILD DIRECTORY.
   GateOpener.app currently sits in the repo checkout. SMAppService.register() (Launch at Login) is expected to fail outside /Applications, and the app should live where a real app lives. OPERATOR DECISION: provide an install script that the OPERATOR runs (copying into /Applications may require admin rights; the agent must not do that silently).

NON-GOALS
- No changes to the protocol, auth, retry, or gate-selection logic. That stack is validated against real hardware and must not be disturbed.
- Not fixing the pre-existing follow-ups under epic gateopener-4ub (.13/.15/.16/.20/.21/.22); they stay there.

CONSTRAINTS THAT STILL APPLY
- GateOpenerCore must NEVER import SwiftUI/AppKit/Observation (headless-testability constraint from gateopener-4ub.1).
- The app opens a PHYSICAL GATE: never run it in real (non-mock) mode for testing; use GATEOPENER_MOCK=1. Only the operator triggers real opens.
- Swift 6 strict concurrency, zero build warnings, and the existing 103 tests must keep passing.

title: GateOpener: macOS menu-bar app for one-click Comelit gate opening
description:
GOAL
A native macOS menu-bar app (MenuBarExtra) whose entire job is: when the doorbell rings while I am working, open the gate with one click, reliably, with no fuss.

WHY
The existing Python webapp in ../comelit works but requires a running server, a browser tab, and attention. A menu-bar app is always present, zero-latency to reach, and survives reboots. Scope at v1 is DELIBERATELY just 'open the gate' — no video, no intercom.

DECIDED (by the operator, do not re-litigate)
- Stack: Swift 6 + SwiftUI MenuBarExtra. Native app, no Python runtime. Auth/API logic is REIMPLEMENTED in Swift (URLSession + CryptoKit), not shelled out to the Python code.
- Credentials: username+password in the macOS Keychain. Tokens cached and refreshed.
- Endpoint: discovered on first login, auto-select the LOCK_GENERIC/PowerController actuator, cache the endpoint id, allow override in Settings.
- Trigger: LEFT-CLICK the menu-bar icon fires the gate IMMEDIATELY (no menu, no confirmation). Right-click (or a menu affordance) reaches Settings/About/Quit.
- Reliability: retry with backoff on transient failure; clear success/failure feedback via the icon itself.
- License: MIT. Public GitHub eventually, but NOT pushed at the start — local-only.

PROTOCOL FACTS ALREADY REVERSE-ENGINEERED (reuse, do not rediscover)
Reference implementation: /Users/ebowman/src/comelit/comelit/auth.py and client.py (validated live).
- BASE https://api.comelitgroup.com
- CLIENT_ID kgDV0WRlQcSF4jPsz887lOTPyVVtP7Oh
- REDIRECT_URI https://app.comelitgroup.com/oauth_redirect/comelit
- User-Agent: ktor-client
- Login is OAuth2 Authorization-Code + PKCE, 2 steps: POST /o-auth-2/auth (JSON) -> Location header with ?code=, then POST /o-auth-2/token (form, grant_type=authorization_code).
- PKCE verifier is a plain uuid4 STRING; challenge = base64url(sha256(verifier)) with padding stripped.
- access_token lives 604800s (7 days); refresh_token grant works.
- Discovery: GET /servicerest/devicecom/endpoints/discovery?aptId=<aptId>
- OPEN: PUT /servicerest/devicecom/endpoint/<urlencoded endpointId>/power body {"value":true} -> HTTP 202. NEVER send {"value":false} (500s). Actuators are momentary/write-only; there is NO read-state (GET is 404).
- The cloud transiently returns HTTP 500 on the open command — the official app sends it twice. Retry is MANDATORY, not optional.
- Known-good gate endpoint suffix: VIP#OD#SB100001.1 'Entrance lock' [LOCK_GENERIC].
- IGNORE VIP#OD#SBIO0255.0 'Generic Actuator': it returns 202 but has NO physical effect. Must never be presented as the gate.
- Operator's aptId: 577fcdbf-5abd-4439-a572-e512f83683de (discoverable, do not hardcode as the only path).

title: Experiment: Tailscale subnet router on the home LAN so a remote laptop reaches the door's host candidate
description:
NEEDS HUMAN (tailnet admin + a shell on the home LAN box). Hypothesis from memory gateopener-remote-video-relay-path-no-frames: if the remote laptop can route to 192.168.1.0/24, WebKit's ICE check from the laptop's Tailscale host candidate (100.x) to the door's host candidate 192.168.1.131 succeeds and the pair becomes local=prflx remote=host, exactly the working home-Mac path, bypassing the door's relay. Zero app changes.
STEPS: 1. On 'streamy' (Linux, 192.168.1.4, on the tailnet and the LAN): sudo tailscale up --advertise-routes=192.168.1.0/24 (keep existing flags; enable IP forwarding per Tailscale docs). 2. Approve the route in the Tailscale admin console. 3. On the remote laptop: tailscale up --accept-routes (or the Mac app's 'Use Tailscale subnets'), then ping 192.168.1.131 from the laptop. 4. Relaunch GateOpener there, View door, then capture with /usr/bin/log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.gateopener"' --last 10m --info --style compact | grep -E 'selected pair|candidate pair|video stats|terminal' | tail -8 and paste into this bead. EXPECTED: selected pair remote(type=host), framesDecoded>0 within ~8s. If the pair stays relay, check that WebKit gathered a host candidate on the utun interface (a 'local candidate: type=host' count of 4+) and that the door accepted a check from the 100.x or SNAT address. RISK: Tailscale MTU 1280; the door's ~1200-byte RTP packets fit, but if frames still never assemble, compare packetsLost from kgx.11.
DONE: pasted capture shows remote(type=host) and framesDecoded>0, or a documented negative result with the pair/stats lines.

comments.author: Eric Bowman
comments.text: Update 2026-09-09: the laptop is behind an always-on GlobalProtect full tunnel (utun12, mtu 1400). Tailscale would run INSIDE that tunnel; if the firewall mangles UDP, Tailscale falls back to DERP over TCP 443, which still works but adds latency. Check whether installing Tailscale on that laptop is permitted at all before trying; if not, see the home-TURN bead.

title: getVideoStats: add packetsLost, nackCount, pliCount, firCount, keyFramesDecoded, frameWidth/Height for the video inbound-rtp
description:
WHY: the remote-laptop log (memory gateopener-remote-video-relay-path-no-frames) shows video packetsReceived growing with framesReceived=0 over the door's relay. To split 'keyframe never arrived and the door ignores PLI' (packetsLost~0, pliCount growing, keyFramesDecoded=0) from 'large packets dropped on the path' (packetsLost growing with gaps), the stats line needs those counters.
STEPS: 1. Resources/door-video.html getVideoStats(): for the video inbound-rtp report add packetsLost, nackCount, pliCount, firCount, keyFramesDecoded, frameWidth, frameHeight, jitter (all numeric, default 0); keep every existing field and key name unchanged. 2. macOS DoorVideoSession: no parsing change needed (framesDecoded is still read); confirm the 'video stats' diag line prints the new fields since it logs the raw JSON. 3. Core: no change. 4. JS syntax check of the extracted script with node --check.
DONE: swift test passes; build-app.sh exit 0; node --check passes; a LAN 'View door' (human-only) shows the new fields in the log.

title: Gate-open overlay: a failed video session must self-dismiss (hold, fade) and never strand the curtains
description:
INPUT: Sources/GateOpener/OverlayWindowController.swift -- handleOpening(), handleResolved(holdDuration:), handleIdleOrNeedsSetup(), handleOpenVideoState(_:), teardownOpenVideoSession(), fadeOutThenHide(); Sources/GateOpener/GateOpenVideoView.swift (player state); memory gateopener-f8w-root-cause-gate-open-path-overlaywindowcontro.
THE BUG (confirmed by code reading, 2026-09-09): open resolves at ~2s while the video session is in flight, so handleResolved returns early; GateState then auto-resets to .idle and handleIdleOrNeedsSetup also returns early; when the video session later fails, handleOpenVideoState(.failed) only calls teardownOpenVideoSession(). Nothing ever hides the panel, and the panel ignores mouse events. The curtains stay up until the next open.
STEPS:
1. In handleOpenVideoState(.failed(message)): after teardownOpenVideoSession(), if the GateState has already resolved (track a `lastResolvedHold: Duration?` set in handleResolved when it returns early because a session was in flight, cleared in handleOpening), schedule the same hold-then-fade handleResolved would have scheduled (reuse its pendingResolveTask path; do not duplicate fade code). If the gate open has NOT resolved yet, do nothing extra -- handleResolved will run normally now that openVideoSession is nil.
2. Same treatment for .ended arriving on a session that never streamed (handleOpenVideoSessionEnded already hides; verify it handles the pre-streaming case and add the same guard if not).
3. Before hiding, briefly show the failure reason: install a DoorVideoConnectingView(text: message) as content for the hold duration only when the message is "Door camera busy" or "Door camera not responding" (short, actionable); for other messages keep the curtains and just fade. Flag: this is a UX choice; keep it minimal and reversible.
4. Diag for the half-open-curtains mystery: when teardownOpenVideoSession() runs, log at notice level (category "overlay") the canned player's `rate` and `currentTime` if the current content is a GateOpenVideoView, so the next strand tells us whether playback stopped mid-clip.
5. Extract the decision "what to do on video failure given (gateResolved, sessionAcceptedOffer)" into a tiny pure Core type with tests (e.g. `OverlayFailureDecision.decide(gateAlreadyResolved: Bool) -> .scheduleFade | .awaitGateResolution`). Mutation-check it.
DONE-CRITERIA: `swift test` passes with the new tests; `bash scripts/build-app.sh` exit 0; summary includes a step-by-step trace of the sequence open->succeeded(2s)->idle(5s)->video failed(20s) showing which method hides the panel and when. Manual verification is HUMAN-ONLY (open the gate once with video enabled while a phone holds a View-door session; the panel must fade within ~2s of the failure): state it was not performed.

title: macOS DoorVideoSession: cooldown wait, single 12s offer, door-busy fail-fast, no blind retry, stop-aware loop
description:
INPUT: Sources/GateOpener/DoorVideoSession.swift (start(), putOfferWithRetry(), putOffer(), watchForFirstFrame(), stop()); Core DoorVideoBusyPolicy + DoorVideoSessionRegistry from the previous bead; VideoDiagnosticsStage (add lines, keep existing formats).
STEPS:
1. In start(), immediately before the offer PUT: `let wait = DoorVideoSessionRegistry.shared.waitBeforeOffer()`; if > .zero, record diag "door cooldown: waiting Xs" (new VideoDiagnosticsStage.cooldownWait(seconds:)), keep state .connecting, `try await Task.sleep(for: wait)` honouring cancellation/hasStopped (return silently if stopped).
2. Replace putOfferWithRetry's policy: ONE attempt, requestTimeout 12s (URLRequest.timeoutInterval = 12; the URLSession used must not have a shorter timeout -- check `session` config). Classify the result with DoorVideoBusyPolicy.classify (map URLError.timedOut -> .timedOut, other URLError -> .other). If shouldRetry (only .network) retry ONCE after 500ms with a NEW sessionId; otherwise throw. Every attempt still records VideoDiagnosticsStage.offerAttempt with the same format as today (n/of/outcome/latency); add the classification word to the failure outcome string, e.g. "500 door-busy", "timeout".
3. Map outcomes to state: .doorBusy -> .failed(message: "Door camera busy"); .unauthorized -> .failed("Sign-in required"); .timedOut -> .failed("Door camera not responding"); .network/.serverError -> keep "Could not reach door camera". Also throw the outcome so callers can distinguish (extend DoorVideoSessionError with `.offer(OfferOutcome)` or similar).
4. On .accepted call DoorVideoSessionRegistry.shared.recordSessionAccepted(); on EVERY terminal transition (.ended, .failed after an accepted offer, stop() after an accepted offer) call recordSessionEnded(). A failure BEFORE the offer was accepted must NOT record an end (it did not occupy the door). Put this in the existing finalizeDiagnostics() choke point or a sibling `finalizeSession()` called from the same places.
5. The retry/cooldown paths must check `hasStopped` before every await continuation and never record diag after finalize (existing `finalized` guard).
6. Tests: the Swift session cannot be unit-tested headlessly (WKWebView), so put the outcome->message mapping in Core (`DoorVideoBusyPolicy.failureMessage(for:)`) with tests, and add a Core test that recordSessionEnded is only expected after acceptance by testing a small pure helper `DoorVideoSessionRegistry.shouldRecordEnd(offerAccepted: Bool)` -- or state clearly that this rule is enforced by code review only. Do NOT drive the app UI.
DONE-CRITERIA: `swift test` passes; `bash scripts/build-app.sh` exit 0; grep shows no remaining `maxAttempts: 2` / 5s offer timeout; a code-path walkthrough in the summary covers: busy door (500) -> "Door camera busy" within ~2s with no second PUT; timed-out PUT -> no second PUT; cooldown wait logged when a session ended <15s ago. Manual hardware check is HUMAN-ONLY: state it was not performed.

title: Core: DoorVideoBusyPolicy (cooldown + offer-outcome classification) and DoorVideoSessionRegistry
description:
INPUT: memory comelit-rtc-offer-500-means-door-busy; Sources/GateOpenerCore/GateClient.swift (RetryPolicy, for style only); Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests conventions.
OUTPUT: two Core types with tests. No app-target changes in this bead.
STEPS:
1. Sources/GateOpenerCore/DoorVideoBusyPolicy.swift: `public enum DoorVideoBusyPolicy` with `public static let cooldown: Duration = .seconds(15)` and `public static func waitBeforeOffer(lastSessionEnded: Date?, now: Date) -> Duration` returning .zero when nil or when now - lastSessionEnded >= cooldown, else the remaining time. Also `public enum OfferOutcome { case accepted, doorBusy, unauthorized, serverError(Int), timedOut, network }` and `public static func classify(httpStatus: Int?, transportError: OfferTransportError?) -> OfferOutcome` where `public enum OfferTransportError { case timedOut, other }`: 200 -> accepted; 500 -> doorBusy; 401/403 -> unauthorized; other 4xx/5xx -> serverError(status); nil status + timedOut -> timedOut; nil status + other -> network. And `public static func shouldRetry(_ outcome: OfferOutcome) -> Bool` returning true ONLY for .network (never for .timedOut -- the PUT may have succeeded server-side and consumed the door -- and never for .doorBusy, which needs the cooldown, not a fast retry). Document each rule in a doc comment citing the memory.
2. Sources/GateOpenerCore/DoorVideoSessionRegistry.swift: `@MainActor public final class DoorVideoSessionRegistry` with `public static let shared`, `public private(set) var lastSessionEnded: Date?`, `public func recordSessionEnded(at: Date = Date())`, and `public func recordSessionAccepted(at:)` (an accepted offer also counts as the start of a busy window; store it in `lastSessionAccepted`). Provide `public func waitBeforeOffer(now: Date = Date()) -> Duration` that takes the LATER of lastSessionEnded and lastSessionAccepted+30s-as-an-estimate? NO -- keep it simple and explicit: waitBeforeOffer uses lastSessionEnded only; lastSessionAccepted is recorded for diagnostics. Flag in the doc comment that a still-STREAMING session elsewhere is not detectable from this process.
3. Tests in Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/DoorVideoBusyPolicyTests.swift: nil -> zero; ended 20s ago -> zero; ended 5s ago -> 10s (assert within 1ms); ended 15s ago exactly -> zero; classify for each status/transport combo; shouldRetry true only for .network (assert false for .timedOut and .doorBusy explicitly). Registry test: recordSessionEnded then waitBeforeOffer(now: +5s) == 10s. Mutation check (memory gateopener-vacuous-assertion-failure-mode): make shouldRetry return true for .doorBusy and confirm a test fails; restore.
DONE-CRITERIA: `swift test` passes with the new tests (report the count); mutation check reported; no changes outside Sources/GateOpenerCore and Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests.

title: macOS DoorVideoSession records diagnostics: diag handler, stage log, persist on terminal state, mirror to Logger
description:
WHY: on macOS Resources/door-video.html already emits diag() lines (candidate types/families, ICE/connection/signaling transitions, remote answer candidates, selected pair) but nobody registers the "diag" WKScriptMessageHandler, so they are lost; and the Swift side never records which stage failed. After this bead a failed macOS session leaves a complete, shareable, address-free record.

INPUT: Sources/GateOpener/DoorVideoSession.swift (macOS), iOS/App/Video/DoorVideoSession.swift lines ~250-280 and ~1076+ (DiagScriptMessageForwarder pattern and what iOS records), VideoDiagnostics in GateOpenerCore (previous bead).

STEPS:
1. In macOS DoorVideoSession.init, register a `DiagScriptMessageForwarder`-style weak forwarder on the WKUserContentController under name "diag" (copy the iOS pattern, including removing the handler in stop()/deinit to break the retain cycle). Every message body String is appended to a `VideoDiagnostics` instance owned by the session. Acceptance: a unit-free manual check via `log show` after a session shows "iceConnectionState=" lines.
2. Record from Swift, in start(): a "session start" line with app version/build and macOS version; "token ok"/"token failed: <case>"; "endpoint <id-suffix-only>" (never the full endpoint id, it embeds the apartment id); "stun resolved N addresses" (count only); "offer ready: N candidates"; each rtc/offer attempt with status or error and latency ms; "answer applied"; in watchForFirstFrame each CHANGED video-stats line and the terminal reason ("streaming after Xs" / "no video after 20s" / "failed: <message>" / "stopped by caller"). Also extend window.getVideoStats() in door-video.html to include iceConnectionState and connectionState so the stats line alone shows whether ICE connected (keep the existing fields unchanged; the iOS session parses the same JSON -- verify its parsing still works).
3. Mirror every appended line to `Self.logger.notice("diag: \(line, privacy: .public)")` so `log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.gateopener"'` also carries the full record without opening the app.
4. On every terminal state (.streaming is NOT terminal; .ended/.failed and stop() are) call `persist(to: UserDefaults.standard)` so the last session's log survives relaunch for the Settings section in the next bead.
5. Extract the pure "stage recorder" (which lines to emit for which event) into a small Core type or function with unit tests in Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests, e.g. `VideoDiagnosticsStage` mapping events to lines, so the line format is tested even though WKWebView cannot be exercised headlessly. Include a test that the endpoint id is truncated to its VIP#... suffix and that no line contains a full endpoint id.

EDGE CASES: start() called twice; stop() before page load (continuation resumed; must not append after persist); the page posting diag before ICE servers are injected; messages that are not String (ignore).

DONE-CRITERIA: `swift test` passes with new tests; `make build` (or the app build script) produces the app; running the built app, choosing View door and then `log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.gateopener"' --last 5m --info` shows diag lines including at least one "local candidate:" and one "iceConnectionState=" line; no line contains a bearer token or the full endpoint id.

title: Move VideoDiagnostics recorder from the iOS target into GateOpenerCore
description:
WHY: macOS needs the same release-build diagnostics recorder iOS got in gateopener-672.27, and the type has no UIKit dependency (Foundation + UserDefaults only), so it belongs in Core where both apps can use it.

INPUT: iOS/App/Video/VideoDiagnostics.swift (public final class VideoDiagnostics: append(_:), persist(to:), static loadLast(from:), byte-capped text) and iOS/Tests/VideoDiagnosticsTests.swift. Consumers: iOS/App/Video/DoorVideoSession.swift, iOS/App/SettingsView.swift.

STEPS:
1. `git mv iOS/App/Video/VideoDiagnostics.swift Sources/GateOpenerCore/VideoDiagnostics.swift`; keep the API byte-for-byte identical (same class name, same UserDefaults key so an existing iOS install keeps its last log). Ensure it imports only Foundation. Acceptance: `swift build` succeeds.
2. `git mv iOS/Tests/VideoDiagnosticsTests.swift Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/VideoDiagnosticsTests.swift`; change `@testable import` to GateOpenerCore. Acceptance: `swift test --filter VideoDiagnosticsTests` passes with the SAME number of tests as before the move (count them first and state the number in the summary).
3. Add `import GateOpenerCore` where the two iOS consumers need it (they may already import it). Regenerate the Xcode project if project.yml drives it (`make xcodeproj`) and check the iOS target no longer lists the moved files. Acceptance: `make ios-build` (or `xcodebuild build -project GateOpener.xcodeproj -scheme GateOpener-iOS -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator'`) compiles. If no simulator/toolchain is available in this environment, say so explicitly in the summary rather than claiming success.
4. Do NOT change behaviour, and do NOT touch the macOS DoorVideoSession in this bead.

EDGE CASES: the class is `public` already but its members may be `internal`; anything the iOS app touches must be public after the move. Mutation check per memory gateopener-vacuous-assertion-failure-mode: temporarily break the byte cap and confirm the moved test fails, then restore.

DONE-CRITERIA: `swift test` passes including the moved tests; iOS target compiles or the summary states precisely why it could not be verified; git shows renames, not delete+add; no source line other than imports/access modifiers changed in VideoDiagnostics.swift.

title: Analyse both captures, name the failing stage, file the root-cause fix bead
description:
INPUT: the baseline report+signature (working Mac) and the failing report+operator answers (failing laptop), both as bd comments on their capture beads. Read Sources/GateOpener/DoorVideoSession.swift, Resources/door-video.html and the memories gateopener-live-video-architecture and gateopener-ios-video-cellular-nat64 first.

OUTPUT: a bd comment on THIS bead with a verdict, and one new child task of the epic describing the fix with numbered steps and done-criteria. Planning-quality analysis only; do not change code in this bead.

STEPS:
1. Environment diff table: app version/build, macOS version, LAN vs remote, VPN/utun and exit node, DNS resolvers, firewall/stealth, STUN resolution results, cloud HTTP reachability/latency. Call out every row that differs.
2. Walk the pipeline stages in order and mark the FIRST stage where the failing log diverges from the baseline: (1) no log lines at all -> View door never reached DoorVideoSession.start() or logging is not persisted; (2) session failed with "Sign-in required"/"Could not get access token"/"Door camera not found" -> auth/discovery; (3) "offer SDP ready ... N ICE candidates" with N=0 or only one family -> gathering/STUN; (4) rtc/offer attempts failing (quote status/error) -> signaling; (5) offer succeeded but video stats stay packetsReceived=0 for 20s then "No video received" -> ICE or media path (indistinguishable on macOS today; say so); (6) packetsReceived>0 but framesDecoded=0 -> decode.
3. For the identified stage write the most likely root cause AND the second-most likely, each with the specific evidence line that supports it, and what single extra observation would separate them.
4. File the fix bead under the epic (`bd create ... --parent <epic>`, p2) with concrete steps against named files/symbols; if the fix is an environment change on the failing laptop rather than code (e.g. VPN exit node, firewall), still file a bead whose deliverable is the operator instruction plus an in-app detection/message so the next user gets feedback. If stage (5) is the verdict and the two causes cannot be separated from the data, make the fix bead depend on the macOS diagnostics port bead (diag handler) and state that the operator must re-capture with the new build.

DONE-CRITERIA: verdict comment names exactly one stage from the list with quoted evidence; a fix bead exists as a child of the epic with numbered steps and done-criteria; `bd ready` shows the fix bead or shows what blocks it.

comments.author: Eric Bowman
comments.text: Reviewer finding on the kgx.2 baseline (2026-09-08): on the WORKING Mac the door's answer offered FOUR remote candidates (srflx x2, host, and a RELAY udp/v4), and ICE selected local=prflx <-> remote=host for the whole session, i.e. the door's host candidate was reachable directly. The sharper question for the failing laptop is therefore: does it fall back to the door's srflx/relay candidates, or never reach any pair? Also: the selected-pair bytesReceived stat reads 0 throughout even while decoding fine, so do not treat it as evidence of no traffic. Absolute timestamps in the kgx.2 signature are uniformly 60ms early; the relative t+ offsets are correct.

comments.author: Eric Bowman
comments.text: VERDICT (2026-09-09): stage (5)/(6) -- signaling and ICE succeed; the selected pair is the door's RELAY because the laptop is behind a symmetric NAT (srflx port differs per STUN server); over the relay, video packets trickle in (~5/s) but framesReceived stays 0 for 20s and audio never arrives, so no keyframe is ever assembled. Root cause: door video is not usable over the door's relay leg from symmetric-NAT networks; it works on cone-NAT (home Mac, LAN host pair) and on 5G (srflx<->srflx). Fix beads filed: gateopener-kgx.11 (stats instrumentation to split keyframe-loss vs large-packet loss) and gateopener-kgx.12 (Tailscale subnet-router experiment so remote laptops reach the door's host candidate). See memory gateopener-remote-video-relay-path-no-frames.

title: Failing capture: operator runs video-diag.sh on the FAILING laptop and pastes the report
description:
NEEDS HUMAN: the operator is at the failing laptop and relays by copy/paste. This bead is the hand-off protocol.

INPUT: scripts/video-diag.sh from the script task.

STEPS FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR:
1. Give the operator the script contents in ONE fenced code block plus a single command to save and run it, e.g. paste into `cat > ~/video-diag.sh <<'EOF' ... EOF` then `bash ~/video-diag.sh > ~/Desktop/video-diag.txt; cat ~/Desktop/video-diag.txt`. The script is copied by hand, so keep it self-contained (no repo paths, no sourcing).
2. Ask the operator to ALSO answer, in their own words: is the failing laptop on the same Wi-Fi/LAN as the door station or elsewhere; is any VPN on; how long between choosing View door and the panel disappearing; what text, if any, the panel showed at the end.
3. When the report arrives, attach it verbatim as a bd comment on this bead and the operator's answers as a second comment.

DONE-CRITERIA: both comments exist; the report's LOG section contains at least one "door-video" line from the failed attempt, OR the comment explicitly records that the log was empty and the operator confirmed the attempt happened within the 30-minute window (in which case the analysis bead must treat "no log lines at all" as the primary symptom).

comments.author: Eric Bowman
comments.text: Operator pasted the failing laptop's log on 2026-09-09 (builds 142 and 152, two View-door sessions). Key lines: 18-21 local candidates with a different srflx port per STUN server (symmetric NAT); remote answer candidates srflx,srflx,host,relay; ICE connected <1s; selected pair local=prflx remote=relay; bytesReceived 22KB (0.1.4) / 105KB (0.1.5) over 20s; candidate pairs: 1 (relay only); video stats packetsReceived=214 framesReceived=0 framesDecoded=0 audio=0; terminal 'no video after 20s'. Full analysis in memory gateopener-remote-video-relay-path-no-frames.

title: Baseline capture: run video-diag.sh on the WORKING Mac after a successful View door
description:
NEEDS HUMAN: someone must trigger "View door" on the working Mac (chedda, this session's machine). Do NOT press the gate-open hotkey -- that physically opens the gate. Only the "View door" menu item. If nobody is at the working Mac, try `osascript` on the status item menu but expect it to fail (the status item is known to sit off-screen and AX queries against an accessory app are unreliable, see memory gateopener-lsuielement-app-gotchas); in that case leave the bead open with a comment saying it awaits the operator.

INPUT: scripts/video-diag.sh from the parent's script task.

STEPS:
1. Run `log stream --predicate 'subsystem == "com.gateopener"' --info --style compact` in the background writing to the scratchpad, trigger View door, wait until the panel disappears (~35s), stop the stream.
2. Run `bash scripts/video-diag.sh` and save the output.
3. Attach the FULL report as a bd comment on this bead (`bd comment <id> -f <file>` or paste), plus a second comment titled "BASELINE SIGNATURE" listing, with timestamps relative to the first line: offer ICE candidate count, rtc/offer attempt result and latency, the first "video stats" line with framesDecoded>0 and how many seconds after the offer it appeared, and the terminal "session ended: <reason>" line.
4. If the LOG section is empty even though the panel showed video, that is itself a finding (unified log not persisting notice-level lines for this app): record it, and fall back to the log stream capture from step 1 for the signature.

DONE-CRITERIA: the bead has two comments as described; the signature comment names all four data points or explains which are missing and why.

BASELINE SIGNATURE

Session start (t=0): 2026-09-08 14:40:16.508 IST — diag: session start: app 0.1.3 (136), macOS Version 26.6.2 (Build 25G83)

(a) Offer ICE candidates: 6 total (offer ready: 6 candidates, at t+2.814s / 14:40:19.322).
    Local candidate types/families logged during gathering (t+2.586s..2.612s, 14:40:19.094-19.120):
      - type=host proto=udp family=v4 port=54088
      - type=host proto=udp family=v4 port=57809
      - type=host proto=udp family=v4 port=62075
      - type=srflx proto=udp family=v4 port=54088
      - type=srflx proto=udp family=v4 port=57809
      - type=srflx proto=udp family=v4 port=62075
    (3 host + 3 srflx, all udp/IPv4 — no relay/TURN candidates offered, no IPv6.)

(b) rtc/offer attempt result: attempt 1/2 succeeded, status=200, latencyMs=2348, at t+5.162s (14:40:21.670).

(c) First video-stats line with framesDecoded>0: at t+7.729s (14:40:24.237) —
      {"video":{"packetsReceived":17,"framesDecoded":5,"framesReceived":5},"audio":{"packetsReceived":0},"iceConnectionState":"connected","connectionState":"connected"}
    That is 4.915s after offer ready (t+2.814s) and 2.567s after rtc/offer success (t+5.162s).
    ICE/connection state at that moment: iceConnectionState=connected (reached t+5.612s / 14:40:22.120), connectionState=connected (reached t+6.177s / 14:40:22.685) — both already connected before frames decoded.
    Selected candidate pair (first "selected pair" line, t+8.178s / 14:40:24.686, ~0.45s after the framesDecoded>0 stats line — no earlier selected-pair line precedes it):
      local(type=prflx family=unknown) remote(type=host family=unknown) state=succeeded bytesReceived=0
    This local=prflx/remote=host/succeeded pairing repeats unchanged on every subsequent selected-pair log line (every ~2s) through t+38.253s.

(d) Terminal lines:
      t+7.731s (14:40:24.239): diag: terminal: streaming after 7.7s
      t+38.253s (14:40:54.761): com.gateopener:door-video-frame — door video frame plateau detected; reporting session ended
      t+38.253s (14:40:54.761): diag: terminal: stopped by caller
    (Session ran ~38s total from session-start log line to stop; video was actively streaming/decoding frames for that entire window per the app's own "streaming after 7.7s" report.)

ENVIRONMENT FACTS (from the report header):

- App: Running: yes (pid 27310), process path /Applications/GateOpener.app/Contents/MacOS/GateOpener, process start Tue Sep 8 14:41:06 2026.
  NOTE: "Installed at /Applications/GateOpener.app" reports 0.1.2 (86) — the Info.plist/bundle version on disk — but the unified-log line for THIS session says the running app reported itself as "app 0.1.3 (136)" at runtime. The install-location check and the live diag: session start line disagree; the live session-start line is authoritative for what actually ran (0.1.3/136), matching the task's stated build. Also note pid mismatch: script's "Running" check found pid 27310, but the log lines for this session are tagged GateOpener[26381:...] — i.e. the process captured by the OS-level check (27310) was NOT the same pid that emitted this log session (26381), consistent with the app having been relaunched between the log session and the script run.
- macOS: ProductVersion 26.6.2, BuildVersion 25G83.
- Default route interface: ipsec0 (IPsec VPN), NOT en0. `route -n get default` shows interface: ipsec0, flags <UP,DONE,CLONING,STATIC,GLOBAL>.
- utun/VPN interfaces present: utun4 (100.80.181.50 / fd7a:115c:a1e0::c434:b533 — Tailscale range), utun11 (10.6.0.41 — matches ipsec0's 10.6.0.41, i.e. the IPsec tunnel). 3 utun interfaces total. en0 also has an address (192.168.1.64) but is not the default route.
- Tailscale: connected — "* (Connected) ... Tailscale 2 [VPN:io.tailscale.ipn.macsys]"; tailscale status shows this Mac (chedda) at 100.80.181.50, "no exit nodes found".
- DNS resolvers (scutil --dns, de-duplicated nameserver lines): 100.100.100.100, 103.86.96.100, 127.0.0.1, 192.168.1.1, 103.86.99.100, fd7a:115c:a1e0::53 — a mix of Tailscale MagicDNS (100.100.100.100), local resolver (127.0.0.1), LAN router (192.168.1.1), IPv6 Tailscale DNS, and two 103.86.9x.100 resolvers (likely IPsec-VPN-pushed DNS).
- Firewall: disabled (State = 0), stealth mode off, block-all disabled.
- STUN resolution: both resolvers agree — dscacheutil (system resolver) and dig both returned the same 5 addresses for stun.cloud.comelitgroup.com: 192.248.183.213, 107.191.49.108, 45.63.60.228, 95.179.217.134, 139.180.214.132 (dig lists them in different order but same set). No resolution failure or mismatch between resolvers.
- Cloud curl result: https://api.comelitgroup.com/ reachability check — http=200, total=0.312816s, connect=0.063198s. Reachable, fast.

VPN DEFAULT ROUTE FLAG (per prior reviewer comment on this bead): CONFIRMED — the working Mac's default route was ipsec0 (IPsec VPN) at the time of this baseline capture, exactly as flagged in the 2026-09-08 13:27 comment. Despite this VPN default route being active, the session succeeded end-to-end: offer/answer exchanged, ICE reached connected, frames decoded (framesDecoded=5 by t+7.7s), and video streamed for ~38s before a normal plateau-triggered end. So on this Mac, an ipsec0 default route did NOT by itself prevent video from working — worth flagging to the analysis bead (gateopener-kgx.4) since it rules out "VPN default route" alone as a sufficient explanation for the second Mac's failure, though it may still be a contributing/necessary-but-not-sufficient factor depending on what differs on the second Mac (e.g. STUN reachability, candidate types actually usable, TURN/relay availability — note no relay candidates appeared in the offer here, and the selected pair was prflx/host, not a TURN relay pair).

title: Paste-able macOS video diagnostic script (scripts/video-diag.sh)
description:
INPUT: nothing beyond the repo. The script must run on a Mac that has ONLY the installed GateOpener.app (no repo, no Xcode, no Homebrew) because the operator will paste it into Terminal on the failing laptop. Use only tools in a stock macOS install: bash/zsh, log, sw_vers, defaults or PlistBuddy, ifconfig, route, scutil, dig, curl, socketfilterfw, pgrep, ps, sqlite3 (optional, tolerate failure).

OUTPUT: scripts/video-diag.sh (executable, bash, `set -u` but NOT `set -e` -- every section must run even if a previous one fails). It prints a single plain-text report to stdout with clearly delimited sections (=== SECTION NAME ===) so the operator can paste it into a bd comment. Also print, at the very top, a 3-line usage banner telling the operator: (1) quit and relaunch GateOpener, (2) choose "View door" from the menu bar item and wait until the panel disappears, (3) run this script within 30 minutes and paste everything.

STEPS:
1. Section APP: path of the running GateOpener process (ps -o comm= for pgrep -x GateOpener; say "not running" if none), CFBundleShortVersionString and CFBundleVersion read from /Applications/GateOpener.app/Contents/Info.plist and from the running process's bundle if different, process start time (ps -o lstart=). Acceptance: on this Mac it prints "0.1.2 (86)" for /Applications.
2. Section OS: sw_vers output.
3. Section NETWORK: every interface with an inet or inet6 address other than loopback/link-local, the default route interface and gateway (route -n get default), a count and list of utun interfaces with their addresses, DNS resolvers (scutil --dns, the nameserver lines only, de-duplicated), and `scutil --nc list` for VPN services. If /usr/local/bin/tailscale or /Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale exists, print `tailscale status --self --peers=false` and `tailscale exit-node list` (tolerate failure). Acceptance: on this Mac it shows en0 192.168.1.64, utun4 100.80.181.50, gateway 192.168.1.1.
4. Section FIREWALL: /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --getglobalstate --getstealthmode --getblockall. Also `--listapps | grep -i gate` (tolerate empty).
5. Section STUN: `dig +short stun.cloud.comelitgroup.com` and `dig +short @192.168.1.1 ...` is NOT required; instead print resolution via the system resolver (dscacheutil -q host -a name stun.cloud.comelitgroup.com) AND via dig, so a split-DNS/VPN resolver difference is visible.
6. Section CLOUD: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'http=%{http_code} total=%{time_total}s connect=%{time_connect}s\n' --max-time 10 https://api.comelitgroup.com/` (any HTTP status is fine; the point is reachability and latency). Never send credentials.
7. Section LOG: `log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.gateopener"' --last 30m --info --style compact`, followed by `log show --predicate 'process == "GateOpener"' --last 30m --info --style compact | tail -200` as a fallback in case a build without the subsystem is installed. Print a line "LOG LINES: <n>" with the count for the subsystem query so an empty capture is obvious rather than silent.
8. Section REDACTION: pipe the whole report through a filter that replaces anything matching `[Bb]earer [A-Za-z0-9._-]+` and any `eyJ[A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,}` with `[REDACTED]`. Also print a footer reminding the operator the report contains local IP addresses and hostnames.
9. Add a Makefile target `video-diag` that runs the script, and a short paragraph in README.md under a "Troubleshooting door video" heading with the three operator steps and the paste command (`bash scripts/video-diag.sh > ~/Desktop/video-diag.txt`).

EDGE CASES: no GateOpener installed (print "not installed" and continue); `log show` returning only its header lines (LOG LINES must be 0, not 2); tailscale absent; dig absent (fallback to dscacheutil only); IPv6-only or no default route.

DONE-CRITERIA: `bash scripts/video-diag.sh` on this Mac exits 0 and prints every section listed above; `bash -n` passes; if shellcheck is installed it reports no errors; the output contains no "bearer"/"eyJ" strings (grep -ci must be 0); the LOG section reports a count.

title: Video diagnostics in Release: log ICE candidate types, selected pair and failure stage; share from Settings
description:
BUG REPORT (operator, 2026-09-06): in-app door video does not work outside the house / off the LAN (works on the LAN). Assessment: on the LAN media is direct phone<->door UDP; off-LAN it needs STUN srflx or Comelit TURN relay. Both Mac and iOS configure STUN only (stun:<ipv4>:3478 pre-resolved), no TURN credentials. Two candidate causes: (1) no usable relay path without TURN credentials; (2) on IPv6-only cellular (NAT64) the IPv4-literal STUN/door candidates are unreachable. TestFlight builds are Release, so the DEBUG --video-harness is compiled out and we are blind on the device.

STEPS
1. In Resources/door-video.html record (guarded so macOS is unaffected): our local candidates as they are gathered (type host/srflx/relay, protocol, address family), the remote answer candidate lines (types only), iceGatheringState/iceConnectionState/connectionState transitions with timestamps, and after connection the selected candidate pair from getStats (local/remote candidate types and address families). Expose as window.__diag (array of lines, capped at 200).
2. iOS DoorVideoSession: add a public `diagnostics: [String]` collected via a "diag" WKScriptMessageHandler (or polled from window.__diag at end), plus Swift-side lines: STUN resolution result (IPs, count), offer PUT status/latency, state transitions, and the terminal reason (stall/timeout/failed). Persist the last session log to the app-group defaults (key videoDiagnostics, capped ~16KB) in RELEASE builds too.
3. SettingsView: a "Video diagnostics" row showing the last session summary (terminal reason, selected pair) with a Share button (ShareLink) of the full text so the operator can send it back.
4. Also record the network path type at session start (NWPathMonitor: wifi/cellular, supportsIPv4/IPv6) in the log.
5. Tests: Core-free; add an iOS test that the diagnostics store caps size and round-trips. `make ios-build`/`make ios-test` green.
DONE: a TestFlight build where one off-LAN attempt produces a shareable log naming candidate types, selected pair, and failure stage.
notes: Follow-up fix bead depends on the diagnostics result: either TURN credentials (find how the official app gets them: REST endpoint or app constant) or IPv6/NAT64 handling (use hostname-form STUN URLs on IPv6-only paths, or resolve AAAA too).
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: release diagnostics + share, no IP leakage, 16KB cap mutation-checked

title: Simulator builds must be signed so keychain-access-groups apply (errSecMissingEntitlement -34018 on unsigned builds)
description:
INPUT: `make ios-build` and all simulator install/launch steps so far pass CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO. Discovered in 672.8: with no code signature the keychain-access-groups entitlement is not applied, so KeychainCredentialStore(accessGroup:) fails on the very first save with KeychainError.saveFailed(status: -34018) (errSecMissingEntitlement). Consequence: sign-in can never reach Comelit on the simulator, and every later screen bead (672.9, .10, .12) cannot be verified with real state.
OUTPUT: simulator builds carry the entitlements.

STEPS
1. Makefile: keep `ios-build` (generic simulator, CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO) as the fast compile gate. Add `ios-sim-build` that builds for a concrete simulator destination (name from SIM_DEVICE, default "iPhone 17 Pro") WITH signing enabled: omit CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO and pass CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-" (ad-hoc, "Sign to Run Locally") so entitlements are embedded; the simulator honours ad-hoc signatures. Add `ios-sim-run` that boots the device if needed, uninstalls, installs the built .app and launches ie.boboco.GateOpener, printing the pid. Both in .PHONY.
2. Verify: after `make ios-sim-run`, `codesign -d --entitlements :- <built .app>` shows both keychain-access-groups and application-groups; launch with `--signin-debug-attempt nobody@example.invalid wrong` and confirm the inline message is NOT the generic fallback caused by -34018 (add a temporary #if DEBUG file log of the error type if needed, remove afterwards). Report the observed error type from the live OAuth attempt (expected: ComelitError.invalidCredentials → "Wrong username or password", or a network error).
3. If ad-hoc signing does not embed entitlements, fall back to automatic signing with DEVELOPMENT_TEAM (already in project.yml) for the simulator destination — Xcode signs simulator builds with the local "Apple Development" identity without a provisioning profile; document which worked.
4. README (iOS section, may not exist yet — add a short note under "Build & Test" in CLAUDE.md or README): explain that CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO builds cannot use the keychain.

EDGE CASES: do not weaken KeychainCredentialStore (no silent fallback to a no-access-group store). Do not touch Sources/.

DONE: `make ios-sim-run` launches a signed build whose entitlements list both groups; the debug sign-in attempt yields a credentials/network message rather than the -34018 fallback; summary states the exact message and error type observed.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: entitlements embedded in __TEXT,__entitlements, live sign-in shows invalidCredentials

title: OPERATOR CHECK on real hardware: sign-in, actuator pick, open with video, widget, Control Center, locked, airplane-mode queue
description:
Human-only acceptance pass against the real gate. Record each item as pass/fail with notes in this bead; file a bug bead for every failure.

1. Fresh install → SignInView; sign in with real credentials (Password AutoFill should offer them) → lands on MainView with the correct gate name.
2. Settings → Default gate shows 'Entrance lock' selected (not 'Generic Actuator'); Refresh works; switch selection and back.
3. Tap Open: the button changes instantly; gate physically opens within ~2-3s; haptic + 'Opened HH:MM'; video panel shows 'Connecting…' then live door video ~4-6s after the tap and disappears on its own ~30s later.
4. Tap Open twice quickly: exactly one physical open, video not restarted.
5. 'View door' shows video without opening the gate.
6. Add the Home Screen widget; press its button from the Home Screen: gate opens, widget shows 'Opening…' then 'Opened HH:MM'; the app is NOT launched. Tap the widget body → app opens WITHOUT opening the gate.
7. Add the control to Control Center and to the Action Button; press each with the phone UNLOCKED → gate opens. Lock the phone; press from the Lock Screen → gate opens (setting default ON). Turn the setting OFF, lock, press → 'Unlock iPhone to open the gate'.
8. Airplane mode on; tap Open in the app → 'Waiting for network…'; airplane mode off within 45s → gate opens automatically once. Repeat but wait >45s → 'No network' and NO open when the network returns.
9. Background: tap Open then immediately swipe the app away/home → gate still opens.
10. Kill the app, wait a day, open it again: no re-login prompt; the first open is fast (prewarm).

DONE: all ten items recorded; failures filed as beads with the observed behaviour.
notes: BUILD 4 (uploading 2026-09-06): adds the cellular video fix (672.28: NAT64-aware STUN list — hostname form + synthesized IPv6 + IPv4 literals) and release-build Video diagnostics (672.27: Settings > Video diagnostics > Share log / Copy). OPERATOR TEST: on CELLULAR (Wi-Fi off), open the gate or tap View door; if video still fails, Settings > Video diagnostics > Share the log and send it back — it names candidate families, the selected ICE pair and the failure stage. Also re-check on the LAN that video still works after the STUN list change.
close_reason: Operator verified on device (builds 2-6): sign-in, actuator, Open, widget, Control Center, Action Button, in-app video on LAN and 5G (View door autoplays as of build 6).

title: OPERATOR: create the App Store Connect record and run the first TestFlight upload
description:
Human-only step; the implementer must NOT attempt it.

1. On appstoreconnect.apple.com create a new app: platform iOS, bundle id ie.boboco.GateOpener (register it in the developer portal first if -allowProvisioningUpdates did not already), name 'GateOpener' (or a variant if taken), SKU gateopener-ios, primary language English.
2. Ensure the App Group group.ie.boboco.GateOpener and the Keychain Sharing capability are enabled on both identifiers (app + .widget) in the developer portal; automatic signing usually does this during the archive-only run.
3. Run ./testflight.sh ios and wait for processing; add the internal TestFlight tester; install on the operator's iPhone.
4. Record the outcome (build number, any signing/portal error text) in this bead's notes and close it.

notes: UPDATE 2026-09-05: bundle ids ie.boboco.GateOpener and ie.boboco.GateOpener.widget are now REGISTERED via the ASC API with the APP_GROUPS capability enabled. The App Group itself (group.ie.boboco.GateOpener) CANNOT be created via the public API (/v1/appGroups is 404) - create it in Xcode (Signing & Capabilities, automatic signing) or on developer.apple.com Identifiers, and attach it to both ids. Then create the ASC app record (My Apps > + > New App, iOS, bundle id ie.boboco.GateOpener). Then run ./testflight.sh ios --archive-only, then ./testflight.sh ios.
