title: WidgetKit extension: interactive Home Screen widget + Lock Screen widget driven by OpenGateIntent
description:
INPUT: project.yml, OpenGateIntent, WidgetSnapshotStore/SharedContainer, ../FlöDo/project.yml extension-target shape.
OUTPUT: iOS/Widget target 'GateOpenerWidget' (app-extension, bundle id ie.boboco.GateOpener.widget, embedded in the app) with a one-tap open button that never launches the app and never touches the network.

STEPS
1. project.yml: add target GateOpenerWidget: type app-extension, platform iOS, sources iOS/Widget + iOS/Shared + Sources/GateOpener/GateControllerObservable.swift if AppEnvironment needs it (prefer not), dependencies: package GateOpenerCore; settings: PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER ie.boboco.GateOpener.widget, GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE YES, INFOPLIST_KEY_NSExtension... (NSExtensionPointIdentifier com.apple.widgetkit-extension — use an explicit Info.plist if xcodegen cannot express it), CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS iOS/Widget/GateOpenerWidget.entitlements (same app group + keychain access group as the app), SKIP_INSTALL YES. Add it as an embedded dependency of GateOpener-iOS. Update make ios-build to build the app scheme, which builds the embedded extension.
2. iOS/Widget/GateOpenerWidgetBundle.swift (@main WidgetBundle) and GateWidget.swift: StaticConfiguration; supportedFamilies [.systemSmall, .systemMedium, .accessoryCircular, .accessoryRectangular]. TimelineProvider reads WidgetSnapshot from the app-group defaults and returns a single entry with policy .never (the app/intent reload timelines explicitly). Placeholder/snapshot entries render a sensible idle state for the gallery.
3. Views: systemSmall = the gate name + one large Button(intent: OpenGateIntent()) filling most of the widget with an SF Symbol and 'Open'; systemMedium adds the last-outcome line ('Opened 14:02', 'Failed: …', 'Opening…', 'Sign in required'); accessoryCircular = a Button(intent:) with the symbol only; accessoryRectangular = symbol + gate name + outcome. Phase-dependent tint: opening/queued amber, succeeded green (for the ~3s the snapshot shows it), failed red. Use .containerBackground for iOS 17+.
4. Tapping anywhere that is NOT the button uses widgetURL(gateopener://main) which merely opens the app to MainView (register the URL scheme in the app target; the app must NOT auto-open on this URL).
5. needsSetup snapshot: the button is disabled and the widget says 'Open GateOpener to sign in'.
6. Verify in the simulator: build, install, add the widget via the widget gallery (or use xcrun simctl + WidgetKit developer preview if available) — at minimum the extension must build and the previews (#Preview with each family) render.

EDGE CASES: The provider must never block (reads defaults only). If SharedContainer.sharedDefaults() is nil (missing entitlement) render an 'App Group missing' diagnostic so the failure is visible, not blank.

DONE: make ios-build green including the extension; screenshots of systemSmall and systemMedium previews attached; summary lists the entitlement contents of both targets side by side (they must match on app group + keychain group).
notes: FOLLOW-UP from 672.7 review: AppEnvironment.publishSnapshot() writes the snapshot but does not call the timelineReloader (the private init never stores it). Fix in this bead: store timelineReloader and call it from publishSnapshot() so a foreground re-publish refreshes the widget.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: extension builds/embeds, entitlements match, Info.plist regression-checked, URL scheme never opens the gate

title: OpenGateIntent (AppIntents) shared by app and widget: runs the open in the extension, publishes snapshots
description:
INPUT: AppEnvironment.make() (iOS/Shared, UIKit-free), GateController.requestOpen()/openGate(), WidgetSnapshotStore, WidgetCenter.
OUTPUT: iOS/Shared/OpenGateIntent.swift — one AppIntent every one-tap surface (widget button, Control Center, Action Button, Siri/Shortcuts) invokes, with openAppWhenRun = false so the app is never launched.

STEPS
1. struct OpenGateIntent: AppIntent { static let title: LocalizedStringResource = "Open Gate"; static let description = ...; static let openAppWhenRun = false; func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult & ProvidesDialog }. No parameters in v1 (the default gate from AppSettings is used; a gate parameter is a later enhancement).
2. perform(): let env = AppEnvironment.make(); if controller.state == .needsSetup → write snapshot needsSetup, reload timelines, return .result(dialog: "Sign in to GateOpener first"). Else write snapshot opening + reload, then AWAIT the open (use the async openGate() here, not requestOpen(): the extension process must stay alive until the result; queued/offline is folded into the retry budget in the intent context — if unreachable, fail fast with 'No network' rather than queuing, because the extension cannot wait 45s). Then write the terminal snapshot + reload and return a dialog 'Gate opened' / the short failure message.
3. Time budget: the intent must finish within ~20s (widget intents are killed around 30s). The existing RetryPolicy worst case is ~15s — keep it. Wrap in a Task with a 25s timeout that fails with 'Timed out' rather than being killed silently.
4. Also declare an AppShortcutsProvider (iOS/App only) exposing OpenGateIntent with phrases like "Open the gate with \(.applicationName)" so Siri/Action Button work.
5. Mark the intent so the SAME type identifier is used by app and extension (both compile iOS/Shared; ensure no duplicate-symbol or missing-intent-in-metadata error by checking Metadata.appintents is generated for both targets).
6. Errors: keychain errSecInteractionNotAllowed → dialog 'Unlock iPhone to open the gate' and snapshot failed with that message (the lock-screen setting task depends on this mapping).

EDGE CASES: The intent may run concurrently with the app open — GateController instances are per-process so the physical single-flight guarantee is per process; document this limitation in the summary (a cross-process lock via the app-group defaults 'openingSince' timestamp older than 10s = stale is an acceptable addition if cheap).

DONE: make ios-build green for app AND the widget target once it exists (if the widget target does not exist yet, build the app only and say so); an iOS unit test (fake controller) asserts perform() writes opening then succeeded snapshots in order and returns the success dialog; a second test asserts needsSetup short-circuits with ZERO open calls.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: 275 tests green, flow guards/timeout/keychain mapping mutation-checked, intent verified on sim

title: Show door video during and after an open on the iOS main screen; View Door on demand
description:
INPUT: MainView slot for video; DoorVideoSession/DoorVideoView; AppSettings.autoShowDoorVideoOnOpen; memory double-click-during-door-video-warm-up-the (epic gateopener-ufk) for the retention rule.
OUTPUT: The open flow shows the door camera when it can, without ever delaying the open.

STEPS
1. In MainView (or a small coordinator object owned by the app), when requestOpen() is invoked and autoShowDoorVideoOnOpen is true: start the video session CONCURRENTLY with the open (same instant, separate Task) — never await video before the open, never await the open before video. The video panel appears immediately in the reserved slot with 'Connecting…' (expect ~4-6s to first frame; the open itself completes in ~2s and its own success feedback must not wait for video).
2. Panel lifecycle: remains visible while streaming; disappears (animated) when the session ends (~28-30s) or fails; a small X lets the operator dismiss it early (calls stop()).
3. Repeat taps: a second requestOpen() during warm-up or streaming must NOT restart the video session (retention rule) — assert this in an iOS unit test with a fake session factory (count of start() calls == 1 across two taps).
4. Add a secondary 'View door' button (plain, below the status line) that starts a video session WITHOUT opening the gate; pressing it while a session is live is a no-op.
5. When a video panel is visible, tapping the big Open button still opens the gate (video never steals the primary affordance).
6. Landscape is not supported (portrait only per project.yml); the panel uses 16:9 at full width.

EDGE CASES: The open failing does not tear down a streaming video (the operator may want to see what is happening). A session failure (.noCamera) hides the panel silently — no error alert; the open outcome is what matters.

DONE: make ios-build green; the fake-session unit test passes and fails if the retention check is removed; simulator screenshot of the panel in the Connecting state attached to the summary.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: sync tap path, retention via Core policy, panel UI verified on sim; retention unit test in 672.18

title: iOS DoorVideoSession: WKWebView door-camera view (token stays in Swift, STUN pre-resolved, liveness end)
description:
INPUT: Read memory gateopener-live-video-architecture and gateopener-yjn-spike-result-wkwebview-webkit-s-own FIRST. Sources/GateOpener/DoorVideoSession.swift (macOS, 675 lines) is the reference: camera endpoint resolution, resolveStunIPs via getaddrinfo, injectIceServers, startNegotiation/applyAnswer, putOffer with retry, and Core's DoorVideoLiveness + DoorVideoSessionRetention. Resources/door-video.html is shared verbatim.
OUTPUT: iOS/App/Video/DoorVideoSession.swift + DoorVideoView.swift (UIViewRepresentable) that shows live door video inside the app. Unlike macOS, the iOS window is key, so the <video> element is displayed DIRECTLY — no canvas JPEG polling.

STEPS
1. Add Resources/door-video.html to the iOS app target's resources in project.yml (do not copy the file; reference the shared one).
2. Port DoorVideoSession to iOS: same public surface shape (start() async, stop(), state: connecting/streaming/ended/failed with an onStateChange callback), same token discipline — the rtc/offer PUT is issued from Swift with TokenManager.accessToken(); the bearer token is NEVER injected into page JS. Reuse the existing putOfferWithRetry semantics (bounded retry, same timeouts).
3. WKWebViewConfiguration: allowsInlineMediaPlayback = true; mediaTypesRequiringUserActionForPlayback = []; allowsPictureInPictureMediaPlayback = false. Without the first two iOS refuses inline autoplay and the view stays black — state this in a comment. Load door-video.html via loadFileURL(_:allowingReadAccessTo:) from the bundle.
4. Liveness/end detection: add a WKScriptMessageHandler channel ('frame') that door-video.html's requestVideoFrameCallback loop posts to at most ~2 times per second (throttle in JS: post only if ≥ 500ms since last post — edit door-video.html minimally and keep the macOS captureFrameJpeg path intact). Swift feeds those timestamps to Core's DoorVideoLiveness (or an equivalent 'no new frame for N seconds' detector reusing its constants); session ends on liveness stall or a 35s hard timeout, NEVER on ICE state. On end, stop the peer connection (evaluate a JS teardown) and blank the view.
5. Apply DoorVideoSessionRetention from Core: a start() request while a session is connecting/streaming retains it; only ended/failed/nil sessions are replaced.
6. Audio: the session is recvonly and the <video> is muted in the HTML; keep it muted (no door audio in v1) and set AVAudioSession category .ambient so the app never interrupts the operator's music.
7. DoorVideoView: UIViewRepresentable hosting the session's WKWebView with an overlay 'Connecting…' ProgressView while state == connecting and a short 'Camera unavailable' label on failed.

EDGE CASES: If no camera endpoint is discovered, start() sets state failed(.noCamera) immediately without any network call. Backgrounding the app while streaming → stop() (WebRTC will be suspended anyway). callAsyncJavaScript for anything Promise-returning (see memory). Do NOT experiment with the offer shape — the plain recvonly recipe is proven.

DONE: make ios-build green; a debug-only harness (launch argument --video-harness) that starts a session and logs state transitions; the implementer cannot verify against hardware in the simulator — the summary must say exactly that, and a separate operator-check bead covers the real device.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: recipe/token discipline/liveness verified; device check is 672.21

title: iOS main screen: one giant Open button with instant feedback, haptics, and no confirmations
description:
INPUT: GateController.requestOpen() (non-blocking, queued/opening/succeeded/failed states) via the observable wrapper and BackgroundOpenRunner.
OUTPUT: iOS/App/MainView.swift — the screen the app launches straight into once configured. It exists to be tapped once while distracted.

STEPS
1. Layout: the gate name at top (secondary text); one full-width, thumb-height (≥ 120pt) button in the lower half of the screen labelled with the gate name / 'Open Gate'; a single status line under it. No navigation bar clutter: a small gear button (top-right) leads to Settings. Dark-mode and Dynamic Type must work.
2. Tap → BackgroundOpenRunner.requestOpen() and return immediately; the button visibly changes within one frame to the .opening / .queued appearance (no waiting for a network response). State appearance: idle = accent colour; queued = amber with 'Waiting for network…'; opening = animated progress ring around the button with 'Opening…' (a real open takes ~2s; the 15s worst case must still look alive); succeeded = green check with 'Opened' + time; failed = red with the short message and the same button re-enabled as 'Try again'. Auto-return to idle follows GateController's existing 3s reset.
3. Haptics: UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(.heavy) on tap; UINotificationFeedbackGenerator .success on succeeded, .error on failed. Prepare generators on appear.
4. No confirmation dialog anywhere on this path. A second tap during queued/opening is a no-op visually acknowledged by a light haptic only.
5. Keep the screen awake while opening (UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled true from tap until terminal state), reset afterwards.
6. Leave a clearly-marked slot (a VStack region above the button) for the video panel task; do not implement video here.

EDGE CASES: If state becomes .needsSetup (sign-out or lost credentials) the root view swaps to SignInView. VoiceOver: the button's accessibilityLabel is 'Open <gate name>' and its accessibilityValue is the status text.

DONE: make ios-build green; simulator screenshot attached to the summary (xcrun simctl io booted screenshot) showing idle and opening states with the MockGateOpening or a fake controller injected via a debug launch argument; the tap-to-visual-change latency is not gated on any await.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: sync tap path, state-driven UI, haptics, sim screenshots verified

OUTPUT: iOS/App/SignInView.swift shown whenever state == .needsSetup.

title: iOS composition root: AppEnvironment wiring Core with app-group defaults, keychain access group, reachability, background task
description:
INPUT: Core provides KeychainCredentialStore(accessGroup:), AppSettings(defaults:), ComelitAPI, TokenManager, GateClient, GateController(requestOpen/queued, reachability:), WidgetSnapshotStore, SharedContainer; the Mac app's GateOpenerApp.swift shows the wiring order.
OUTPUT: iOS/Shared/AppEnvironment.swift — one factory usable from BOTH the app and the widget extension (so it must not import UIKit at the top level) — plus the iOS-only glue for reachability, background tasks and widget refresh.

STEPS
1. iOS/Shared/AppEnvironment.swift: @MainActor final class AppEnvironment { static func make() -> AppEnvironment } constructing: defaults = SharedContainer.sharedDefaults() (fall back to .standard and log loudly if nil — means the entitlement is missing); appSettings = AppSettings(defaults:); credentialStore = KeychainCredentialStore(accessGroup: SharedContainer.keychainAccessGroup, accessibility: from a stored setting, default afterFirstUnlock); api = ComelitAPI(); tokenManager = TokenManager(...); gateClient = GateClient(tokenResolver:...); reachability = NWPathMonitorReachability (step 2); controller = GateController(gateClient:tokenManager:credentialStore:appSettings:reachability:); snapshotStore = WidgetSnapshotStore(defaults:). Expose them as lets.
2. iOS/Shared/NWPathMonitorReachability.swift: ReachabilityProviding backed by Network.NWPathMonitor on a utility queue; isReachable = path.status == .satisfied; callbacks forwarded as-is (GateController hops to main). Start the monitor on init, cancel on deinit.
3. Snapshot publishing: in AppEnvironment.make(), subscribe controller.onStateChange and on every change write WidgetSnapshot.from(state:gateName: appSettings.selectedEndpointName, now: Date()) to snapshotStore then call WidgetCenter.shared.reloadAllTimelines() (WidgetKit is available in both app and extension; import it in this file only). Also write a snapshot once at construction so a fresh install shows needsSetup.
4. iOS/App/BackgroundOpenRunner.swift (app target only, imports UIKit): wraps a call to controller.requestOpen() so that UIApplication.shared.beginBackgroundTask is begun when state enters .opening/.queued and ended when state returns to idle/succeeded/failed/needsSetup. Guard against double-ending. Expiration handler ends the task.
5. Foreground hook (app target): on scenePhase == .active call Task { await tokenManager.prewarm() } and re-write the snapshot.
6. Reuse Sources/GateOpener/GateControllerObservable.swift (already in the target from the project task) to expose an @Observable state to SwiftUI; if it has macOS-only assumptions, copy it into iOS/App with the minimum edits and say so.

EDGE CASES: AppEnvironment.make() may be called from the intent while the device is locked — keychain reads must go through the access-group store and never prompt. Never instantiate UIApplication from iOS/Shared.

DONE: make ios-build green; a debug run on the iOS simulator launches to the placeholder view without crashing (implementer runs xcrun simctl boot + launch, or xcodebuild test-without-building with a trivial smoke test) and the snapshot key appears in the app-group defaults (verify with a small debug print or the test in the later app-tests task).
notes: DECISION (672.6): Sources/GateOpener/GateControllerObservable.swift is NOT iOS-safe (it holds a GlobalHotkey, which imports AppKit+Carbon). It is NOT compiled into the iOS target. Write iOS/App/GateControllerObservable.swift: a small @Observable @MainActor wrapper mirroring the Mac one state-forwarding (subscribe controller.onStateChange, publish state), with no hotkey parts.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: ios-build green, snapshot verified in app-group plist on fresh sim install

title: GateController: non-blocking requestOpen() with offline queue, TTL, and coalescing
description:
INPUT: GateController.openGate() is async and idempotent against concurrent calls; there is no offline handling — an open attempted with no network just burns the retry budget and fails.
OUTPUT: A fire-and-forget entry point that never blocks the caller, holds the request while offline, fires it the instant connectivity returns, and coalesces repeated taps.

STEPS
1. In Sources/GateOpenerCore add public protocol ReachabilityProviding: Sendable { var isReachable: Bool { get }; var onChange: (@Sendable (Bool) -> Void)? { get set } } (or an AsyncStream<Bool> — pick one, document it). Provide AlwaysReachable (default) so existing Mac behaviour is unchanged and existing tests pass without edits.
2. Add GateState case queued to GateState. Update every exhaustive switch in Sources/GateOpener (macOS app) to treat .queued like .opening (icon/overlay/status text) — grep 'case .opening' to find them. GateControllerObservable and NotificationPresenter included.
3. Add to GateController: init params reachability: any ReachabilityProviding = AlwaysReachable(), queueTTL: Duration = .seconds(45). Add public func requestOpen() (NOT async). Semantics: if reachable → start openGate() in a Task exactly as today. If not reachable → state = .queued, remember the request timestamp, and subscribe to reachability; when it flips true within TTL → run the open; when TTL elapses first → transition(to: .failed(message: "No network")) via the existing auto-reset path. A second requestOpen() while .queued or .opening is a no-op (coalesce: one physical open per burst). Cancelling: signOut() drops any queued request.
4. Use the injected sleep/clock seam already present (GateControllerSleep) for the TTL timer so tests never wait.
5. Tests in GateControllerTests.swift with a FakeReachability: (a) reachable → requestOpen leads to .opening then .succeeded and exactly ONE gateClient.open call; (b) unreachable → .queued and ZERO open calls; then flip reachable → exactly one open call; (c) unreachable, TTL elapses → .failed("No network"), zero open calls, and a later flip to reachable does NOT fire the stale request; (d) three requestOpen() calls while queued → one open call after flip; (e) signOut while queued → no open after flip. Each test must fail if the corresponding production branch is deleted.

EDGE CASES: Reachability callbacks may arrive on any thread — hop to the main actor before touching state. A flip to true followed immediately by false must still fire the request (fire on the first true). Do not change RetryPolicy defaults (requestTimeout stays 3s).

DONE: swift test green (new tests + all existing); swift build of the macOS app green; summary states the exact public API added and every Mac-app file touched for the new enum case.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: 241 tests green, mutation-checked TTL/coalescing/token paths

title: Core: SharedContainer identifiers + WidgetSnapshot codec/store for app↔widget state
description:
INPUT: Nothing shared exists between an app and a widget extension today.
OUTPUT: Foundation-only Core types that both iOS targets use to (a) locate the shared container and (b) publish/read the widget's display state.

STEPS
1. Add Sources/GateOpenerCore/SharedContainer.swift: public enum SharedContainer { public static let appGroupId = "group.ie.boboco.GateOpener"; public static let keychainAccessGroup = "Y5SB82BPYL.ie.boboco.GateOpener"; public static func sharedDefaults() -> UserDefaults? (UserDefaults(suiteName: appGroupId)) }.
2. Add Sources/GateOpenerCore/WidgetSnapshot.swift: public struct WidgetSnapshot: Codable, Equatable, Sendable { public enum Phase: String, Codable, Sendable { case needsSetup, idle, queued, opening, succeeded, failed }; gateName: String?; phase: Phase; message: String?; updatedAt: Date } plus public static func from(state: GateState, gateName: String?, now: Date) mapping every GateState case (needsSetup→needsSetup, idle→idle, opening→opening, succeeded→succeeded with message nil, failed(message)→failed carrying the message). If a queued GateState case exists by the time this is implemented, map it to .queued; otherwise leave the enum case present for the queue task to use.
3. Add public final class WidgetSnapshotStore: Sendable { init(defaults: UserDefaults, key: String = "widgetSnapshot"); func write(_:) ; func read() -> WidgetSnapshot? } using JSONEncoder/Decoder with .iso8601 dates. Reading a corrupt value returns nil (never throws). Write is synchronous.
4. Tests (Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/WidgetSnapshotTests.swift) using UserDefaults(suiteName: UUID) and removePersistentDomain in tearDown (see memory about stray test plists): round-trip every phase; from(state:) mapping for every GateState case including the failed message; corrupt data → nil; read on empty → nil.

EDGE CASES: The store must not import WidgetKit (Core stays Foundation-only); reloading widget timelines is the app layer's job. Keep the JSON key stable — it is a cross-process contract.

title: KeychainCredentialStore: optional access group, accessibility class, never synchronizable
description:
INPUT: Sources/GateOpenerCore/CredentialStore.swift KeychainCredentialStore(service:) builds kSecClassGenericPassword queries with service+account only.
OUTPUT: The store can be shared between the iOS app and its widget extension via a keychain access group, and items are readable while the device is locked-after-first-unlock, with the macOS app's behaviour and existing tests unchanged.

STEPS
1. Add public enum KeychainAccessibility: Sendable { case afterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly, whenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly } with an internal var secAttr: CFString mapping to kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly / kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly.
2. Extend init to init(service: String = defaultService, accessGroup: String? = nil, accessibility: KeychainAccessibility = .afterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly). Existing call sites compile unchanged.
3. Extract query construction into an internal, pure, testable static func makeBaseQuery(service:account:accessGroup:) -> [String: Any] and static func makeAddAttributes(accessibility:) -> [String: Any]. baseQuery includes kSecAttrAccessGroup ONLY when accessGroup != nil. Add attributes on save include kSecAttrAccessible = accessibility.secAttr and kSecAttrSynchronizable = kCFBooleanFalse. The update-on-duplicate path must also update kSecAttrAccessible (so toggling accessibility re-saves correctly).
4. Add public func rewriteAccessibility(to:) throws that loads credentials and tokens, deletes them, and re-saves them with the new accessibility (used by a later 'allow while locked' setting). If nothing is stored it is a no-op.
5. Tests in Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/CredentialStoreTests.swift: (a) makeBaseQuery omits kSecAttrAccessGroup when nil and includes the exact string when set; (b) makeAddAttributes maps both accessibility cases to the correct CFString and sets synchronizable false; (c) an integration round-trip with a UUID service (as existing tests do) still passes; (d) rewriteAccessibility round-trips stored values. Each assertion must FAIL if the production line is removed — check by temporarily deleting the kSecAttrAccessGroup line and confirming a red test, then restore.

EDGE CASES: On macOS, an access group requires the app to be signed with that entitlement; the DEFAULT must remain nil so the Mac app and swift test are unaffected. errSecMissingEntitlement on iOS must surface as a KeychainError with the OSStatus, not crash.

title: Make GateOpenerCore build for iOS (Package.swift platforms + guard macOS-only self-update code)
description:
INPUT: Package.swift declares only .macOS(.v14); Sources/GateOpenerCore/UpdateInstaller.swift (and possibly UpdateSwapScript.swift / UpdateFetcher.swift) use Process(), which does not exist on iOS.
OUTPUT: GateOpenerCore compiles for iOS 18 and macOS 14 from the same package with no behaviour change on macOS.

2. Find every symbol unavailable on iOS in Sources/GateOpenerCore (grep for Process, NSWorkspace, FileHandle usage that is macOS-only, posix_spawn, NSAppleScript). Wrap the macOS-only self-update runtime pieces (UpdateInstaller's Process-based swap execution, UpdateSwapScript, and anything else that fails to compile) in #if os(macOS) ... #endif at the smallest granularity that compiles. title: Core test: a sequential second openGate() after the first resolves issues a second open
description:
WHY: the epic's contract is "a second click re-issues the gate open (idempotent) but never restarts the video". The gate half is already true — GateController.openGate() (Sources/GateOpenerCore/GateController.swift ~:178-205) joins a CONCURRENT in-flight open via openTask, but once that task completes openTask is nil and state is .succeeded (3s auto-reset to .idle, autoResetDelay ~:143), so a later call performs a fresh open. Nothing tests that. Existing test concurrentOpenGateCallsResultInExactlyOneUnderlyingOpenCall (Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/GateControllerTests.swift ~:223) covers only the concurrent case.

STEPS
1. Read GateControllerTests.swift to reuse its fixture (MockGateOpening or equivalent with openCallCount, the controller factory, any clock/scheduler injection used to avoid real sleeps).
2. Add `@Test func sequentialOpenGateCallsEachIssueAnUnderlyingOpen()`: call `await controller.openGate()`, assert state is .succeeded and openCallCount == 1; WITHOUT waiting for the auto-reset to .idle call `await controller.openGate()` again; assert openCallCount == 2 and state is .succeeded. If the auto-reset uses a real Task.sleep(3s) and the test would race it, the second call must be issued immediately after the first returns — document in a comment why no wait is inserted. Do not add sleeps to the test.
3. Add `@Test func openGateWhileOpeningIsJoinedNotDuplicated()` ONLY if not already covered by the concurrent test — read it first; if it already asserts exactly this, skip and say so.
4. Do NOT change GateController.swift. If the sequential test fails against current code, STOP and report the observed behaviour instead of modifying the controller — that would be a design finding for the orchestrator.
5. `swift test --filter GateControllerTests` passes; paste the summary.

DONE WHEN: the new sequential test exists, passes without sleeps or flakiness (run it 3 times), and GateController.swift is unchanged.

title: OverlayWindowController: retain a connecting/streaming open-video session on a repeat open
description:
INPUT: the retain/replace policy landed by the sibling Core task (DoorVideoSessionRetention / DoorVideoSessionPhase in Sources/GateOpenerCore). Target file: Sources/GateOpener/OverlayWindowController.swift — handleOpening() (~:421), startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled() (~:446), teardownOpenVideoSession() (~:548), handleOpenVideoState() (~:497), plus DoorVideoSession.state (Sources/GateOpener/DoorVideoSession.swift:~127, public private(set)).

STEPS
1. Add a small mapping from DoorVideoSessionState to DoorVideoSessionPhase. Put it as an extension in Sources/GateOpener/DoorVideoSession.swift (e.g. `var phase: DoorVideoSessionPhase`), exhaustive switch, dropping the ended/failed payloads.
2. In startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled(): compute `let decision = DoorVideoSessionRetention.decision(forExistingPhase: openVideoSession?.phase)` (adjust to the API name the Core task actually shipped — read it, do not guess). If .retain: log at notice level "a new open arrived while this open's video session is <phase>; retaining it" and RETURN without calling teardownOpenVideoSession(), without creating a new session or DoorVideoFrameView, and without reassigning onStateChange/onSessionEnded. If .replace: existing behaviour (teardown, then build a new session) — keep the existing "replacing it" log line but only emit it when openVideoSession != nil.
3. In handleOpening(): the unconditional `setContent(Self.makeCannedAnimationContent())` must NOT run when the session is being retained AND the frame view is already the installed content (i.e. session phase is .streaming). When the retained session is still .connecting the canned animation is already showing, so re-setting it is harmless but pointless — simplest correct rule: only call setContent(canned) when the retention decision is .replace. Compute the decision once in handleOpening() and pass it (or the boolean) into startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled() rather than evaluating it twice with a state change in between. cancelPendingResolve(), alphaValue = 1 and show() still run on every opening (they are idempotent and keep the panel visible).
4. Do NOT touch DoorVideoFrameView.startPolling()/sessionStartedAt — the ~30s window stays anchored to the first session by design (see epic).
5. Check handleResolved(holdDuration:) (~:584) and handleIdleOrNeedsSetup() (~:624): they already guard on openVideoSession == nil; confirm a retained session keeps those guards effective for the SECOND open's .succeeded/.failed/.idle transitions too (it should, since openVideoSession is unchanged). State this explicitly in your report.
6. Update the doc comment above startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled() to describe the retain rule.
7. `swift build` must succeed. Run the full `swift test`. Also run the mock self-test if it is cheap (`GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 swift run GateOpener` — see GateOpenerApp.swift ~:257/:455) and report whether it still passes; it exercises the canned-animation path, not video.

EDGE CASES
- Second open arrives while openVideoSession is .failed (e.g. 20s no-first-frame deadline fired): decision is .replace -> tear down and start a fresh session. That is the desired retry.
- Second open arrives while openVideoSession is .ended but handleOpenVideoSessionEnded()->hide() has not yet run: .replace; the teardown inside startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled() must leave the panel visible (do not call hide()).
- Second open with autoShowDoorVideoOnOpen off or no factory: openVideoSession is nil -> .replace -> falls through to the existing early guards; behaviour identical to today.

DONE WHEN: a second GateState.opening while openVideoSession.state is .connecting or .streaming leaves the same DoorVideoSession and DoorVideoFrameView instances in place (no stop(), no new WKWebView, no content swap to the canned animation), logs "retaining", and .ended/.failed/nil still replaces; build and full test suite pass; the summary quotes the final shape of handleOpening() and startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled().

title: Core: pure retain-or-replace policy for an existing door-video session, with tests
description:
INPUT: Sources/GateOpenerCore/DoorVideoLiveness.swift is the pattern to copy (pure logic in Core, exhaustively tested in Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/DoorVideoLivenessTests.swift). The app-layer enum DoorVideoSessionState (Sources/GateOpener/DoorVideoSession.swift:~21) has cases idle, connecting, streaming, ended(reason:), failed(message:) and is NOT visible from Core.

STEPS
1. Add Sources/GateOpenerCore/DoorVideoSessionRetention.swift containing:
   a. `public enum DoorVideoSessionPhase: Sendable, Equatable { case idle, connecting, streaming, ended, failed }` — a payload-free mirror of the app-layer state so Core stays independent of the app target.
   b. `public enum DoorVideoSessionRetention: Sendable, Equatable { case retain, replace }`.
   c. `public static func decision(forExistingPhase phase: DoorVideoSessionPhase?) -> DoorVideoSessionRetention` (put it on DoorVideoSessionRetention or a small `DoorVideoSessionPolicy` enum namespace — pick one and say which in the summary). nil (no session) -> .replace; .idle -> .replace; .connecting -> .retain; .streaming -> .retain; .ended -> .replace; .failed -> .replace. Use an exhaustive switch, no default clause, so adding a phase later fails to compile.
   d. Doc comment on the function explaining WHY: a new open arriving while the video is connecting/streaming must not discard the multi-second warm-up; ended/failed is the case where a second click should retry. Reference the epic id.
2. Add Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/DoorVideoSessionRetentionTests.swift using swift-testing (`import Testing`, `@Test`, `#expect`) matching the style of DoorVideoLivenessTests.swift. One @Test per phase plus one for nil — six tests minimum. Consider a parameterised @Test(arguments:) over all cases; either is fine.
3. Run `swift build` and `swift test --filter DoorVideoSessionRetention` and paste the pass summary in your report.

DONE WHEN: the file exists in Core, the switch is exhaustive, all six input cases are covered by passing tests, full `swift test` still passes, and no file under Sources/GateOpener was touched.

title: Move RTPCounters + rtpCountersShowProgress to GateOpenerCore and unit-test them
description:
PROBLEM: DoorVideoFrameView.rtpCountersShowProgress(previous:current:) (Sources/GateOpener/DoorVideoFrameView.swift, added in a24bcb7) is a pure function deliberately factored out for testability, but it lives in the app target (GateOpener), which has NO test target — only GateOpenerCoreTests exists (structural gap = gateopener-4ub.22; this task is the narrow fix for this one function, NOT a substitute for 4ub.22).

FIX (numbered):
1. Create Sources/GateOpenerCore/DoorVideoLiveness.swift containing: (a) public struct RTPCounters: Equatable, Sendable { public let framesReceived: Int; public let packetsReceived: Int; public init(...) } moved verbatim from DoorVideoFrameView; (b) a public enum or caseless namespace (e.g. DoorVideoLiveness) with static func rtpCountersShowProgress(previous: RTPCounters?, current: RTPCounters) -> Bool, body moved VERBATIM — do not change semantics in this task (the gap-baseline change is a separate, dependent task).
2. In DoorVideoFrameView.swift: delete the nested RTPCounters struct and static func; update the two call/reference sites (pollOnce() and the lastRTPCounters property type) to use the Core types. Keep the existing doc comments, moved alongside the code.
3. Add Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/DoorVideoLivenessTests.swift covering, minimum: (a) previous nil + current all-zero -> false; (b) previous nil + current nonzero (each counter independently) -> true; (c) strict increase in framesReceived only -> true; (d) strict increase in packetsReceived only -> true; (e) both flat -> false; (f) decrease in one counter with the other flat -> false (stats-reset case); (g) one counter decreases while the other increases -> true (current OR semantics — assert the AS-IS behavior).
4. MUTATION CHECK (required by gateopener-vacuous-assertion-failure-mode): temporarily invert the > to >= in the moved function, confirm at least one test FAILS, then revert. State in the completion summary which test caught it.

title: Deflake retryingTestsCompleteFastNoRealSleeping: assert on injected sleep, not wall-clock
description:
PROBLEM: Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/GateClientTests.swift:615-631 asserts elapsed < 500ms wall-clock after a 3-attempt retry run with RetryPolicy.noDelay(). Under parallel load it measured 571ms locally and 747ms on the GitHub CI runner (run 33422028259), failing CI on main. The intent is 'the client never really sleeps in tests', which wall-clock proves only probabilistically.

FIX (numbered):
1. In GateClientTests.swift, rewrite retryingTestsCompleteFastNoRealSleeping to construct a RetryPolicy (see Sources/GateOpenerCore/GateClient.swift:69-129 — public init with injectable sleep closure, invoked at :541) whose sleep closure RECORDS each requested Duration into a Sendable-safe accumulator (e.g. an actor or a Mutex-protected array) instead of sleeping.
2. Drive the same scripted 3x-HTTP-500 failure as today (RequestScript(statuses: [500,500,500]), maxAttempts 3) and assert deterministically: (a) the open() call throws; (b) the recorded sleep calls number exactly 2 (one between each pair of attempts, none after the final attempt); (c) each recorded Duration is > .zero (proves real backoff WOULD have slept — the property the old comment wanted).
3. DELETE the elapsed < 500ms wall-clock assertion entirely. Do not replace it with a looser threshold — any wall-clock bound reintroduces the flake class.
4. Keep the test name or rename to reflect the new mechanism (e.g. retriesRouteAllDelaysThroughInjectedSleep) — implementer's choice, but update the MARK comment at :613 to match.

EDGE CASES: the sleep closure must be @Sendable (matches the stored property type at GateClient.swift:100); use maxAttempts: 3 explicitly so assertion (b) does not silently drift if the default changes.

DONE-CRITERIA: swift test passes fully AND the rewritten test passes 20 consecutive runs under load (run 'for i in {1..20}; do swift test --filter <newTestName> || break; done' alongside a parallel 'swift build -c release' to simulate load) with zero failures; no wall-clock duration assertion remains in the test.

title: Self-replacing swap and Check for Updates
description:
INPUT: a verified DMG. OUTPUT: the self-replacing swap — the irreversible step.

READ THE REFERENCE CAREFULLY AND FOLLOW IT. A running .app cannot overwrite itself; the trick is a detached shell script that waits for the app to exit.

DO
1. Write a short /bin/sh script to NSTemporaryDirectory(), mode 0755.
2. Launch it DETACHED: `nohup ... >>/tmp/gateopener-update.log 2>&1 &` via /bin/sh -c, passing the DMG path, getpid(), the install dir, and the bundle name. EVERY interpolated path MUST go through a shQuote helper — these are paths from the filesystem and the bundle, and an unquoted space or quote here corrupts an rm -rf.
3. Then NSApp.terminate(nil).
4. The script: spin on `kill -0 $PID` until the parent is gone, then `hdiutil attach -nobrowse -noverify -plist`, parse the mount point out of the plist, `rm -rf` the old bundle, `cp -R` the new one into place, `hdiutil detach`, `open` the result.
5. Install dir and bundle name come from Bundle.main.bundleURL, so this works from /Applications or a build directory without special-casing. Do not hardcode /Applications.
6. Plist parsing: the reference shells out to python3. Keep that rather than grepping /Volumes — the reference explicitly calls the grep approach fragile. If python3 is unavailable, fail loudly rather than falling back to something unreliable.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY
Everything that can fail must fail BEFORE anything is destroyed:
- verify() throws -> the app stays intact.
- script write or launch fails -> throw launchFailed, the app stays intact.
- Once `rm -rf` runs, the ONLY recovery is /tmp/gateopener-update.log. So every step before it must fail loudly and visibly.
Do not reorder these. Do not "optimise" by unmounting or deleting earlier.

WHY cp -R IN PLACE, NOT A FRESH INSTALL — do not change this
Same path + same Developer ID identity means TCC grants, login-item registration, and THE KEYCHAIN ACL GRANT survive the upgrade. This project lost days to keychain re-prompts from an unstable signing identity (gateopener-sal); an updater that broke the grant every upgrade would reintroduce exactly that. Preserving it is a feature, not an accident.

DO
7. Wire a minimal user-facing path: a "Check for Updates…" menu item that fetches the manifest, compares, and offers to install. Keep the UI plain — an NSAlert is fine. DROP all the GPGuard Enterprise scaffolding: no custom UTI, no CFBundleDocumentTypes, no NSOpenPanel, no "it's been N days" nag. This repo is public so the app can just URLSession-GET the manifest and DMG.
8. Never take keyboard focus in a way that breaks the overlay guarantee. An update alert is a deliberate user-initiated interaction so it may activate — but do not disturb the overlay panel's orderFrontRegardless-only behaviour.

TESTING — be honest about what you cannot test
A real end-to-end self-replacement needs a genuinely notarized DMG and will terminate the app. Test what you can in isolation: shQuote correctness (spaces, quotes, backslashes, newlines), script generation given known inputs, and the ordering guarantee that nothing destructive is attempted when verify() throws. For the live swap, state plainly whether you performed it and against what artifact. DO NOT claim an end-to-end upgrade you did not observe.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT create a remote, run gh, or push.
- Do not weaken verify(); it gates this entire path.

DONE-CRITERIA
- shQuote is tested against adversarial paths.
- Nothing destructive runs when verification fails — proven by test.
- The script's generated text is asserted for known inputs.
- "Check for Updates..." exists and reports "up to date" correctly against a manifest whose version is not newer.
- swift build; swift test; SELFTEST PASS.
- An explicit statement of what was and was not verified end to end.

title: Port verify(): streaming sha256 plus notarization check
description:
INPUT: UpdateManifest/SemanticVersion. OUTPUT: UpdateInstaller.verify() — the security boundary.

THE REFERENCE IS EMPHATIC: "Keep verify() exactly as-is; it is the whole security story." Port it faithfully. Do not simplify, do not skip a check, do not make either check optional.

DO
1. Port UpdateInstaller.verify(dmgURL:manifest:) into Sources/GateOpener. It MUST throw unless BOTH hold:
   a. Streaming SHA-256 of the DMG matches manifest.dmgSHA256. Read in 1 MiB chunks — NEVER load the whole DMG into memory. A DMG is tens of MB and this runs in a menu-bar app.
   b. `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature <dmg>` exits 0 — i.e. the DMG is Developer-ID signed AND notarized. Developer ID signing alone does not satisfy this.
2. Make it testable without a real signed artifact, as the reference does: both parts `nonisolated static`, and the notarization check INJECTED AS A CLOSURE so tests can substitute it. This is why the reference says the policy unit-tests without shelling out.
3. Tests must cover: matching digest + notarization ok -> success; digest MISMATCH -> throws (even when notarization passes); notarization FAILS -> throws (even when the digest matches); both fail -> throws. The two checks are independent gates and neither may be sufficient alone.
4. Each assertion must be non-vacuous — it must fail if the corresponding check is removed. State how you confirmed it.
5. Use a real temporary file of known content for the digest tests so the streaming path is genuinely exercised, including a file larger than one 1 MiB chunk so chunk-boundary handling is actually tested.

CARRIED FORWARD FROM THE c33.5 REVIEW — handle these here, they are NOT handled in the model
1. `dmgURL` is typed as `String` in UpdateManifest, deliberately, since Core is a pure model. URL VALIDATION IS THEREFORE THIS BEAD'S JOB. Before fetching or verifying anything, the URL must parse as a URL and MUST be https — reject http and any other scheme outright. A manifest is fetched over the network; an attacker who could serve a manifest naming an http:// DMG would otherwise get a plaintext downgrade on the very artifact that is about to replace the running app.
   Consider also pinning the host to the expected GitHub releases host derived from the repo, and say what you decided. Do not silently accept an arbitrary host just because the digest matches — the digest only proves the file matches what the MANIFEST said, and the manifest is the thing an attacker would control.
2. A version component >= 2^63 overflows Int and makes SemanticVersion return nil, which correctly fails closed but means the updater would SILENTLY stop offering updates forever. Not a defect, but if you surface any user-facing "up to date" message, make sure an unparseable-version case is distinguishable in logs from a genuine no-update, so this is diagnosable rather than mysterious.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT implement the swap/install step here — that is the next bead, and it is the irreversible one. This bead is verification only.
- No networking here either.
- Do NOT create a remote, run gh, or push.

DONE-CRITERIA
- verify() throws on digest mismatch, on notarization failure, and on both.
- The digest path is streaming and provably handles a >1 MiB file.
- Tests pass and are non-vacuous by the stated method.
- swift build; swift test; SELFTEST PASS.

title: Port UpdateManifest and fail-closed SemanticVersion, with tests
description:
INPUT: the reference implementation's UpdateManifest.swift (manifest model + tolerant SemanticVersion). OUTPUT: the same, ported into GateOpenerCore with tests.

DO
1. Port UpdateManifest and SemanticVersion into Sources/GateOpenerCore (they are pure model/logic — no AppKit, no networking — so they belong in Core and are unit-testable there). GateOpenerCore must gain NO new import beyond Foundation.
2. UpdateManifest decodes {latestVersion, notes, dmgURL, dmgSHA256} and exposes `isNewer(than:)` comparing against the running app's CFBundleShortVersionString.
3. SemanticVersion MUST FAIL CLOSED, exactly as the reference specifies:
   - accepts 1-4 dot-separated integers
   - treats missing trailing components as 0, so 1.4 == 1.4.0
   - returns nil for ANYTHING else
   - an unparseable version on EITHER side means "no update available"
   Never prompt to upgrade to something you cannot order. This is a correctness requirement, not a nicety: a malformed manifest must never trigger an install.
4. Write thorough tests. This is pure logic with sharp edges, so cover: equal versions, strictly newer, strictly older, 1.4 vs 1.4.0 equality, 4-component versions, leading zeros, empty string, non-numeric components, negative numbers, absurdly long input, and nil-on-either-side. Assert that unparseable input yields "no update", never a crash and never an accidental upgrade.
5. NON-VACUOUSNESS: each assertion must fail if the corresponding rule is inverted. State how you confirmed it (see bd memory gateopener-vacuous-assertion-failure-mode for why this repo insists).

CONSTRAINTS
- No networking in this bead. Model and comparison logic only; fetching is a later bead.
- GateOpenerCore stays Foundation-only — no AppKit/SwiftUI/AVFoundation/Observation.
- Do NOT create a remote, run gh, or push.

DONE-CRITERIA
- swift test passes with the new tests (130 at filing, plus yours).
- `grep -n "import" Sources/GateOpenerCore/UpdateManifest.swift` shows only Foundation.
- Fail-closed behaviour proven by test for every malformed-input case listed above.

title: Release target: manifest generation and gh release publish
description:
INPUT: a notarized, stapled DMG. OUTPUT: a Makefile release target that generates the manifest and publishes both assets.

*** REQUIRES AN OPERATOR PREREQUISITE: a GitHub remote must exist. `git remote -v` is currently EMPTY. Agents MUST NOT run `gh repo create`, add a remote, or push. If no remote exists when this bead runs, STOP and tell the operator. ***

DO
1. Add a `release` target to the Makefile, following the reference Makefile.release-excerpt.
2. PRECONDITIONS FIRST — each turns a bad release into an early `exit 1`, and they are the cheap part of the value here:
   - VERSION non-empty (read from the BUILT bundle's Info.plist, per the version bead — never a shell literal)
   - working tree clean
   - tag v$(VERSION) does not already exist
   - the DMG exists and is notarized (spctl check passes)
   Fail with a clear message naming which precondition failed.
3. Derive host/owner/repo from `git remote get-url origin`, NOT hardcoded, so a fork or rename works without editing. Handle both ssh (git@github.com:OWNER/REPO.git) and https forms.
4. Generate the manifest with the digest computed from THE ARTIFACT JUST BUILT, so it can never describe a different binary:
     SHA=$$(shasum -a 256 "$(DMG_PATH)" | awk '{print $$1}')
   Manifest JSON: {latestVersion, notes, dmgURL, dmgSHA256}. `notes` is the release page URL.
5. THE MANIFEST FILENAME MUST BE STABLE ACROSS RELEASES (e.g. appcast.json) — that is what makes the /releases/latest/download/<name> redirect work. The DMG filename is versioned; the manifest name is NOT. Getting this backwards silently breaks update discovery, so assert it.
6. Publish both assets:
     gh release create "v$(VERSION)" --title "GateOpener v$(VERSION)" --generate-notes "$(DMG_PATH)" "$(MANIFEST_PATH)"
7. Document the whole flow in the README: build -> dmg -> notarize -> release, and what the operator must have set up (Developer ID, notary profile, gh auth).

CONSTRAINTS
- The target may RUN gh release create — that is its purpose — but ONLY when invoked deliberately by the operator. It must never run as a side effect of `make` or `make all`, and never from an unattended agent loop. Guard it so a bare `make` cannot publish.
- Do NOT create the remote or push branches; only `gh release create` against an existing remote.
- Do not weaken the notarization or signing steps.

DONE-CRITERIA
- `make release` dry-runs cleanly (or fails on a named precondition) with no remote configured — verify the failure message is helpful.
- The manifest's dmgSHA256 matches `shasum -a 256` of the DMG actually uploaded.
- The manifest filename is stable and the DMG filename is versioned.
- README documents the release flow.
- A bare `make` cannot publish anything.

title: Notarize and staple the DMG
description:
NO NEW KEY IS NEEDED — resolved 2026-08-28. The operator pointed at ../FlöDo, which already has working App Store Connect API credentials, and I verified them against Apple's notarization service:
    xcrun notarytool history --key ~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_<ID>.p8 --key-id <ID> --issuer <ISSUER>
returned "Successfully received submission history" including a real prior submission (MCPMaestro-1.12.0.dmg, status Accepted, 2026-08-27). So this Apple account has already notarized DMGs with this exact key.
WHERE THE PIECES LIVE (operator's machine, NOT this repo, and they must never be copied into it):
  - Private keys: ~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_7ZG885QRGL.p8 and AuthKey_JQR4S423V4.p8
  - Key ID and Issuer ID: exported as API_KEY_ID and API_ISSUER_ID in ../FlöDo/.env (gitignored there)
The only remaining operator step is a ONE-TIME convenience: storing a named keychain profile so scripts need no key paths.

OPERATOR STEP — run once, then tell the agent it is done:
    cd ../FlöDo && set -a && source .env && set +a && \
    xcrun notarytool store-credentials "GateOpenerNotary" \
      --key "$HOME/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_${API_KEY_ID}.p8" \
      --key-id "$API_KEY_ID" --issuer "$API_ISSUER_ID"
Verify with: xcrun notarytool history --keychain-profile "GateOpenerNotary"
(If the operator would rather not create a profile, the script must also accept --key/--key-id/--issuer via env vars. Support both; do not force the profile.)

CARRIED FORWARD FROM THE c33.2 REVIEW — check this early
The DMG's code-signing identifier is currently derived from the filename and TRUNCATES at the first dot: `codesign -dv GateOpener-0.1.0.dmg` reports `Identifier=GateOpener-0`. Harmless for a DMG in itself, but notarization is stricter than local signing. If notarytool rejects or warns about the identifier, pass an explicit stable one (e.g. `codesign --identifier ie.boboco.GateOpener.dmg ...`) in scripts/make-dmg.sh rather than leaving it filename-derived. Check this BEFORE burning a submission round trip — notarization is slow and each rejected attempt costs minutes.

AGENT WORK
INPUT: scripts/make-dmg.sh producing a signed DMG.
OUTPUT: scripts/notarize-dmg.sh that submits, waits, staples, and verifies.

WHY NOTARIZATION IS MANDATORY, NOT OPTIONAL
UpdateInstaller.verify() requires `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature` to exit 0. That passes ONLY for NOTARIZED artifacts — Developer ID signing alone FAILS it. Skipping notarization would gut half the security model and leave an updater that installs whatever the network hands it. It also stops Gatekeeper warning every downloader.

DO
1. Write scripts/notarize-dmg.sh matching the existing scripts' conventions (set -euo pipefail, REPO_ROOT derivation, header comment, clear failures). Read scripts/build-app.sh first and match its style.
2. Credential resolution, in this order, so it works for a contributor without the operator's setup:
   a. NOTARY_PROFILE env var (default "GateOpenerNotary") used via --keychain-profile
   b. else NOTARY_KEY / NOTARY_KEY_ID / NOTARY_ISSUER env vars used via --key/--key-id/--issuer
   c. else fail with the operator instructions above and exit non-zero — NOT a raw notarytool error.
3. Submit and wait: `xcrun notarytool submit "$DMG" ... --wait`.
4. On success staple and validate: `xcrun stapler staple "$DMG"` then `xcrun stapler validate "$DMG"`.
5. THE ACCEPTANCE CHECK — exactly what the updater runs, so it must pass here:
     spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature "$DMG"
   must exit 0. If not, the release is not shippable: fail loudly and print spctl's output.
6. On notarization FAILURE, fetch and print the log so the cause is visible:
     xcrun notarytool log <submission-id> ...
   A silent failure here is expensive to debug later.

CONSTRAINTS
- NEVER print, copy, commit, or transcribe key material, the Key ID, or the Issuer ID. Do not copy anything out of ../FlöDo/.env into this repo. Do not cat the .p8.
- Do NOT create a git remote, run gh, or push.
- Do not change signing behaviour from gateopener-sal.

DONE-CRITERIA
- ./scripts/notarize-dmg.sh takes a signed DMG through submit -> staple -> validate against the real service.
- `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature <dmg>` exits 0. Paste the output.
- Running with no credentials configured prints the helpful instructions, not a raw error.
- No secret is committed; `git status` clean of key material; grep the diff for the key id and issuer to confirm neither leaked.

title: Build a signed, distributable DMG
description:
INPUT: a signed .app produced by scripts/build-app.sh, with the version now read from a single source.

OUTPUT: scripts/make-dmg.sh producing a distributable DMG of the signed app.

DO
1. Write scripts/make-dmg.sh following the conventions of the existing scripts (set -euo pipefail, SCRIPT_DIR/REPO_ROOT derivation, header comment explaining purpose/inputs/output, clear failure messages). Read scripts/build-app.sh and scripts/generate-icon.sh first and match their style.
2. It must build the .app first (or require it and fail clearly if absent — pick one and say why), then produce GateOpener-<version>.dmg at a predictable path.
3. Keep the DMG simple: a read-only compressed image (hdiutil create -srcfolder ... -format UDZO or equivalent) containing the .app and an /Applications symlink so drag-to-install works. No custom background art, no fancy window layout — those are cosmetic and can come later if the operator wants them.
4. The DMG must be code-signed with the same Developer ID identity the app uses (codesign --sign "$CODESIGN_IDENTITY" on the .dmg). Reuse the identity-resolution logic from build-app.sh rather than duplicating it — factor it into a shared snippet or source it, and say what you did.
5. Verify the result: `codesign -dv` on the DMG, and confirm the .app inside the mounted image is intact and signed.

DO NOT
- Do NOT notarize here. Notarization is the NEXT bead and requires an operator-supplied credential this bead must not touch.
- Do NOT create a remote, run gh, or push.

EDGE CASES
- Fail clearly if no Developer ID identity is available: an ad-hoc-signed DMG can never be notarized, so this must be an explicit, explained failure rather than a silently unusable artifact.
- Clean up any temporary mount points and staging directories, including on failure.

DONE-CRITERIA
- ./scripts/make-dmg.sh produces GateOpener-<version>.dmg with the version taken from the built bundle.
- `codesign -dv` on the DMG shows the Developer ID identity.
- Mounting the DMG and launching the .app from it works.
- The script is idempotent — running it twice leaves no stale mounts or temp dirs.
- swift build; swift test; SELFTEST PASS.

title: Single authoritative app version, read back from the built bundle
description:
INPUT: scripts/build-app.sh, which currently hardcodes SHORT_VERSION="0.1.0" at ~:29 and writes it into Info.plist's CFBundleShortVersionString (~:96).

PROBLEM
The release process derives the git tag, the DMG filename, and the manifest's latestVersion from the app version. If the version lives in a shell variable while the bundle is built from that same variable, they agree today — but the reference design deliberately reads VERSION FROM Info.plist so the shipped bundle and the tag CANNOT disagree. Right now nothing enforces that, and a stale hardcoded value would silently publish a v1.2.0 tag containing a 0.1.0 bundle. The updater compares against Bundle.main.CFBundleShortVersionString, so a mismatch means users are told they are up to date when they are not.

DO
1. Establish ONE authoritative source for the version. Prefer a plain VERSION file at the repo root, or a single well-marked variable — pick one and justify it. build-app.sh reads it and writes it into Info.plist.
2. Provide a way for the release process to read the version back OUT of the BUILT bundle (e.g. `defaults read "$PWD/GateOpener.app/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleShortVersionString` or PlistBuddy), so downstream steps use what was actually built rather than what was intended.
3. CFBundleVersion (the build number) should also be sane — it must increase monotonically for macOS to treat a replacement as newer. Decide how it is derived (git commit count is a common, reproducible choice) and document it.
4. Add a guard: if the version string does not parse as 1-4 dot-separated integers, build-app.sh FAILS with a clear message rather than producing an unversionable artifact. This mirrors the updater's fail-closed SemanticVersion.
5. Update any docs/comments that reference the old hardcoded value.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT change signing behaviour. build-app.sh signs with a stable Developer ID (gateopener-sal); that must keep working exactly as-is, including the CODESIGN_IDENTITY override and the ad-hoc fallback for contributors with no certificate.
- Do NOT create a git remote, run gh, or push.
- The app must still build and run identically.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The version appears in exactly one authoritative place; grep proves no second hardcoded copy.
- ./scripts/build-app.sh produces a bundle whose CFBundleShortVersionString matches that source, verified by reading it back out of the built .app.
- An invalid version string makes the build fail loudly.
- swift build; swift test; GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.
- The app still launches from /Applications and opens the gate.

title: Make a stale previous-session frame structurally impossible
description:
ROOT CAUSE IS NOW ESTABLISHED (gateopener-f8w.1, with screenshot + millisecond log evidence). READ bd memory `gateopener-f8w-root-cause-gate-open-path-overlaywindowcontro`.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE — SIMPLER THAN THE EARLIER THEORY, WHICH WAS REFUTED
OverlayWindowController.handleOpening() (~:389-394) calls show() then startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled(), but NEVER calls setContent(_:). show() (~:192-208) merely re-fires overlayWillShow() on whatever content is ALREADY installed. startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled() (~:413-444) builds a fresh DoorVideoFrameView but only installs it later, in handleOpenVideoState's `.streaming` branch (~:466-468).
  - FIRST open of a process: content is still the canned GateOpenVideoView, so the animation plays fully (2.2s) and holds its last frame. `.streaming` arrives ~6s later, well after it finished.
  - ANY REOPEN in the same run: content is the PREVIOUS session's DoorVideoFrameView, still holding its decoded image. show() re-fires overlayWillShow() on that STALE view (log-proven: `imageView.image=SET`), and it remains the panel's only content for a measured 2.5-6.3s until the new session reaches `.streaming`. That is symptom 1. And because nothing re-installs the canned view, the animation is never shown again either — that is symptom 2.
BOTH SYMPTOMS ARE THIS ONE OMISSION.

EXPLICITLY REFUTED — do not implement against it: the earlier theory that the canned animation is "torn out mid-play" by a premature swap on `.streaming`. Measured: the 2.2s clip finishes long before `.streaming` at ~6s. The swap timing is not the bug; the MISSING setContent on .opening is.

VIEW DOOR PATH IS NOT AFFECTED and needs no fix: DoorVideoOverlayController.start() calls setContent(connecting) synchronously before every session, so each reopen resets content. Two clean reopens verified, zero stale frames. Do NOT restructure that path. (Its swap-to-frame-view gap is ~150ms and imperceptible.)

THE FIX DIRECTION: make handleOpening() install content explicitly — the canned animation view — before/when starting a new video session, mirroring what DoorVideoOverlayController.start() already does. Then the reopen shows the animation again (symptom 2 fixed) and can never show the prior session's frame (symptom 1 fixed).

INPUT: the root cause established by the diagnosis bead (read its bd memory and report before starting).

OUTPUT: the overlay never shows a frame from a previous session, on EITHER entry point.

DO
1. Fix the actual cause identified by the diagnosis bead. Do not invent a different theory; if the diagnosis turns out to be wrong or incomplete, STOP AND REPORT rather than improvising a second fix.
2. THE BAR IS STRUCTURAL, NOT COSMETIC. A stale frame must be IMPOSSIBLE, not merely unlikely or short-lived. Do not fix this with a timing tweak, a sleep, or by shortening the window in which the old frame is visible. Concretely, the intended shape:
   - From the moment a session starts until a frame decoded BY THAT SESSION is displayed, the panel shows the connecting placeholder.
   - Any image belonging to a previous session is cleared at session start, rather than left in place to be overwritten later.
   - A frame is only displayed if it can be attributed to the CURRENT session.
   Whether that is achieved by clearing imageView.image, by always installing the placeholder first, by tagging frames with a session identity, or by ensuring no view/page outlives its session, is your call — justify it.
3. FIX BOTH ENTRY POINTS unless the diagnosis proved only one is affected:
   - "View Door" -> DoorVideoOverlayController (currentFrameView, ~:85/:161)
   - gate open -> OverlayWindowController (openVideoSession/openVideoFrameView, ~:412-422)
   If a single shared change covers both, prefer that over two parallel fixes.
4. Consider whether captureFrameJpeg should ALSO refuse to return a frame from a page whose session has ended. Resources/door-video.html:188-196 currently guards only on video.videoWidth/videoHeight being non-zero, and a finished <video> KEEPS its dimensions while frozen on its last frame — so that guard cannot distinguish live from stale. Hardening it is likely worthwhile defence in depth; say what you decided and why.

THE CANNED ANIMATION MUST BE VISIBLE ON THE OPEN PATH — a first-class requirement, not a side effect
The user: "I kind of liked the 'slowly opening curtains' effect, that distracts the user from the delay for live video to appear, and I didn't see that either."
Today OverlayWindowController.handleOpenVideoState(_:) (~:466) swaps to the live view on `.streaming`, which fires when the SESSION has framesDecoded > 0 — before DoorVideoFrameView has decoded its own first JPEG. So the animation is cut off mid-play and replaced by an image-less view showing a "Connecting..." label.
REQUIRED: swap to the live view only when a frame FROM THAT SESSION is decoded and ready to DISPLAY — not merely when the session reports `.streaming`. That single change plausibly fixes both symptoms: the curtains play through the whole connect delay, and there is never a window where the panel shows an image-less or stale view.
DONE-CRITERION FOR THIS: screenshot the panel DURING the connect window on a gate open and confirm the canned gate animation is visibly playing — not a "Connecting..." label, not a blank panel, not an old frame.

CONSTRAINTS — none of these may regress
- The overlay must NEVER take keyboard focus: orderFrontRegardless() only, never makeKeyAndOrderFront, never NSApp.activate. Verify by typing into another app while the panel is visible and report the observation.
- Keep the canvas-capture architecture; do NOT display the <video> element (it needs a key window the panel can never be).
- Keep the byte-comparison plateau detector: identical JPEG bytes must not count as a new frame, or session-end detection breaks.
- Keep streaming detection on framesDecoded > 0.
- Panel content view stays wantsLayer = true.
- Rapid repeated opens must still produce ONE panel and ONE session, not stacked ones.
- rtc/offer ONLY; never the power/open endpoint.
- Build with ./scripts/build-app.sh UNMODIFIED; add no codesign step.

VERIFY BY OBSERVATION, NOT ARGUMENT
Reproduce the ORIGINAL bug scenario and prove it is gone: run a full session to natural end, then start a second one, and screenshot the panel rect within the first 1-2 seconds. It must show the connecting placeholder or nothing — NOT the previous session's scene. Do this for BOTH entry points and report each separately, with the images described.
Then confirm the second session goes on to show live video normally and disappears at ~28-30s via the plateau detector.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Screenshot evidence that the second run shows no stale frame, for both entry points.
- Second run still streams live video and still ends via the plateau detector (not the hard timeout).
- Typing in another app is unaffected while the panel is visible.
- swift build; swift test (130 at filing, plus any tests you add); GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.
- git status --short shows only intended files; no leftover instrumentation.

title: Diagnose the stale-frame-on-reopen bug with reproduction evidence
description:
INPUT: the installed, working app on main (783a6b2). The user reports that opening the video overlay a SECOND time briefly shows the LAST frame of the PREVIOUS session.

OUTPUT: a definitive, evidence-backed root cause. NO FIX in this bead — diagnosis only, so the fix lands with the cause understood rather than guessed.

WHY DIAGNOSIS IS ITS OWN BEAD
Preliminary tracing RULED OUT the two most obvious explanations: DoorVideoOverlayController builds a fresh DoorVideoFrameView per session (~:85), OverlayWindowController builds a fresh one per open (~:422), and DoorVideoSession builds a NEW WKWebView per session (:174) loading the page fresh (:242). So this is NOT simply "the view was reused". Guessing at a fix without finding the real path risks papering over it.

DO
1. REPRODUCE IT FIRST, on the real app against real hardware, and CAPTURE IT. Trigger the overlay, let it stream, let it end (~28-30s). Then trigger it AGAIN and screenshot the panel rect in the first ~1-2 seconds of the second run, before the new session's first frame can arrive (~6s). Compare that image against a frame from the FIRST run. LOOK at both with the Read tool. You must be able to say "this pixel content is from the previous session" with evidence, not impression.
   Both entry points must be checked, and they use DIFFERENT code paths — report each separately:
     - "View Door" menu item -> DoorVideoOverlayController
     - opening the gate -> OverlayWindowController's openVideoSession/openVideoFrameView path
   Harnesses exist: GATEOPENER_VERIFY_VIEW_DOOR_MENU=1, and GATEOPENER_VERIFY_OPEN_VIDEO=1 with GATEOPENER_VERIFY_OPEN_VIDEO_TRIGGER=leftclick|menu|hotkey. The panel rect is printed by the harness; capture exactly that rect, never the full screen (the user is at the machine).
2. INSTRUMENT to find the path. Log, with timestamps: every setContent(_:) call and which view instance it installs; every DoorVideoFrameView init/deinit (use ObjectIdentifier so instances are distinguishable); every imageView.image assignment and whether the decoded bytes differ from the previous poll; every captureFrameJpeg result (nil vs data-URL length); and the panel's current content view identity at the moment the second session starts.
2b. DIAGNOSE THE SECOND SYMPTOM TOO — the user also reports the canned "slowly opening curtains" animation is NOT seen on the gate-open path, and they explicitly value it for covering the ~6s connect delay.
STRONG HYPOTHESIS, verify or refute: OverlayWindowController.handleOpenVideoState(_:) ~:466 calls setContent(openVideoFrameView) on `.streaming`, but `.streaming` fires when the SESSION reaches framesDecoded > 0 — before DoorVideoFrameView has completed its own first captureFrameJpeg poll and decode. The frame view has NO image yet and shows its own "Connecting..." label (DoorVideoFrameView.swift ~:251-252). So the canned animation is torn out mid-play and replaced by an image-less view.
If confirmed, this is likely the SAME root cause as the stale frame: content is swapped in before it has a current-session image to show. Report whether the two symptoms share one cause — that materially changes the fix.
RECORD: how long the canned animation actually plays before being replaced, and what is on screen in the gap between the swap and the first decoded frame.

3. ANSWER THESE SPECIFICALLY:
   - At the instant the second session starts, what view is installed in the panel, and does it still hold an NSImage from the first session?
   - Is the connecting placeholder shown at all on the second run, or is the old frame view left installed until new frames arrive?
   - Does captureFrameJpeg ever return a frame belonging to the previous session (e.g. a page/web view outliving its session)?
   - Are currentFrameView (DoorVideoOverlayController) or openVideoFrameView (OverlayWindowController) retained across sessions in a way that matters?
4. Record the root cause with `bd remember` in this repo so the fix bead and any future reader inherit it.
5. REMOVE all instrumentation before finishing; confirm with git diff.

CONSTRAINTS
- Diagnosis only. Do NOT fix. Do NOT refactor.
- Do not regress or even touch: the never-steal-focus guarantee (orderFrontRegardless only), the canvas-capture architecture, the byte-comparison plateau detector, framesDecoded>0 streaming detection, wantsLayer on the content view.
- rtc/offer ONLY; never the power/open endpoint.
- Build with ./scripts/build-app.sh UNMODIFIED (stable Developer ID). Do NOT add a codesign step — the user must not get another keychain prompt.
- The user is AWAKE and using the machine. Do not steal focus; capture only the panel rect.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A screenshot pair proving the stale frame, described in your report.
- A named root cause with file:line references and log evidence, covering BOTH entry points (or an explicit statement that only one is affected, with proof).
- bd memory written.
- git status clean of instrumentation; swift build; swift test (130 at filing); GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.
close_reason: Root cause found with screenshot and log evidence: OverlayWindowController.handleOpening() never calls setContent(_:), so on a reopen the panel keeps the PREVIOUS session's DoorVideoFrameView (already holding a decoded image) and show() re-fires overlayWillShow() on it. Both symptoms trace to that one omission. Refuted the earlier 'animation torn out mid-play' theory: the 2.2s canned clip finishes long before .streaming arrives at ~6s, so on a FIRST open it plays fully; on a reopen it is never re-installed at all. View Door path is unaffected because DoorVideoOverlayController.start() calls setContent(connecting) synchronously every time. Recorded as bd memory gateopener-f8w-root-cause-gate-open-path-overlaywindowcontro. Diagnosis only, no production diff.

title: Sign the app with a stable Developer ID so keychain grants survive rebuilds
description:
DISCOVERED 2026-08-28 while working around an overnight keychain-prompt problem for the gateopener-yjn spike.

PROBLEM
scripts/build-app.sh:111 signs the app AD-HOC:
    codesign --force --deep --sign - "${APP_BUNDLE}"
An ad-hoc signature has NO stable code identity — the binary's identity is derived from its own hash, so it CHANGES ON EVERY REBUILD. macOS grants keychain access per code identity, so:
- Every reinstall invalidates the user's previous "Always Allow" grant for the Comelit credentials in the keychain (service "ie.boboco.GateOpener", account "credentials").
- The user is therefore re-prompted for keychain access after every single rebuild+install cycle, forever.
The install script already half-acknowledges this, printing "because the app is ad-hoc signed and just moved to a new path, macOS may prompt for Keychain access the first time it runs from here" — but the prompt is not actually a one-time path thing, it recurs on every rebuild.

THE FIX
The user HAS a real Developer ID certificate. `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` reports three identities; the relevant one is:
    "Developer ID Application: Eric Bowman (Y5SB82BPYL)"
VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY (2026-08-28): signing with that identity produces a designated requirement keyed on the IDENTIFIER + TEAM, not on the binary hash. A probe binary was signed, its source COMPLETELY REWRITTEN, then rebuilt and re-signed — the designated requirement was byte-identical across both:
    designated => identifier <id> and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = Y5SB82BPYL
So ONE "Always Allow" would persist across all future rebuilds.

DO
1. Change scripts/build-app.sh:111 to sign with the Developer ID rather than ad-hoc.
2. DO NOT hardcode the identity as the only option — this repo is intended for public release (see gateopener-4ub.13), and a hardcoded personal signing identity would break the build for anyone else and leaks a team id into the repo. Make it configurable and DEGRADE GRACEFULLY:
   - Read an override from the environment, e.g. CODESIGN_IDENTITY.
   - If unset, try to auto-detect a Developer ID Application identity via `security find-identity -v -p codesigning`.
   - If none is found, FALL BACK TO AD-HOC (`--sign -`) exactly as today, and print a clear note explaining that keychain prompts will recur on every rebuild without a stable identity.
   A contributor with no Apple certificate must still be able to build and run the app.
3. Consider adding `-i <stable-identifier>` so the identifier stays fixed even if the bundle name ever changes.
4. Update the message printed by scripts/install.sh (~line 26 region prints the keychain caveat) so it matches the actual behavior in each case — stable-identity builds should NOT claim a prompt is expected on every rebuild.
5. Check whether `--deep` is still appropriate; it is deprecated by Apple for signing nested code and may warrant signing nested components explicitly. Do not change this speculatively — investigate and report, only change it if it is actually wrong for this bundle.

EDGE CASES / HAZARDS
- Do NOT enable hardened runtime or notarization as part of this bead. Those change Gatekeeper behavior and entitlements handling and deserve their own decision; this bead is only about a STABLE identity for keychain-grant stability.
- Signing with a Developer ID does NOT make the app notarized. First launch from /Applications may still show Gatekeeper UI depending on quarantine attributes. Do not claim otherwise in any user-facing message.
- Verify the existing keychain item is still readable after the identity change. NOTE: the user will likely get ONE more prompt after the first Developer-ID-signed build, because the identity genuinely changed from ad-hoc. Say so plainly in the report so it is not mistaken for a regression.

DONE-CRITERIA
- scripts/build-app.sh signs with a stable Developer ID identity when one is available, and still builds successfully with ad-hoc when none is.
- `codesign -d -r-` on two builds made from DIFFERENT source states produces the SAME designated requirement.
- The app still launches from /Applications and can read its keychain credentials.
- swift build, swift test (126 at time of filing), and GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 (SELFTEST PASS) all still green.
- No signing identity, team id, or certificate is committed to the repo.

title: SPIKE: does any Swift-side WebRTC stack receive RTP from the door?
description:
RESEARCH SPIKE with a single binary outcome. Time-boxed to ONE working session. It gates whether gateopener-12h (live door camera) is buildable at all.

THE QUESTION
Does a native macOS client receive actual RTP VIDEO PACKETS from the Comelit door station?

STACK CHOICE IS DELEGATED TO YOU. The user said "no preference, just figure it out." Test in this order, stopping as soon as one arm gets packets:
  ARM 1 — WKWebView. Cheap (~1 hour), and reuses ../comelit/comelit/webrtc_page.html almost verbatim.
