PROCEDURE
1. With autoShowDoorVideoOnOpen enabled, click the menu-bar item once, then click it again ~3s later (after the gate open has resolved, before video appears). Expect: the overlay does not flicker back to the canned animation, the video appears at roughly the same moment it would have with a single click, and the unified log (Console.app, subsystem for GateOpener) shows a "retaining it" line, NOT "replacing it". Note the time from first click to first frame.
2. Repeat with the second click during streaming (e.g. 10s in). Expect: video continues uninterrupted, "retaining it" logged, overlay auto-hides at roughly the FIRST session's ~30s mark (not extended).
3. Repeat with a second click within ~1s of the first. Expect: coalesced (no second .opening, existing behaviour); video unaffected.
4. Let a session run to its natural end, then click again after the overlay hides. Expect: a new session starts normally ("replacing" or no prior-session log is fine here).
5. Menu "View" twice, ~3s apart. Expect: single session, "retaining it".
6. Record results as a comment on this bead: timings for step 1 vs a single-click baseline, and any case where video restarted or the overlay flickered.

DONE WHEN: steps 1-5 behave as expected on real hardware and the observations are recorded on the bead. Any deviation -> file a follow-up task under the epic with the exact log excerpt.

title: DoorVideoOverlayController: repeated View clicks retain a connecting/streaming session
description:
INPUT: Sources/GateOpener/DoorVideoOverlayController.swift start() (~:72-76 currently: `if currentSession != nil { log "replacing it"; teardown() }`), teardown() (~:183-188). The retain/replace policy from the Core task and the DoorVideoSessionState -> DoorVideoSessionPhase mapping from the OverlayWindowController task.

STEPS
1. In start(): compute the retention decision from currentSession?.phase. If .retain: log at notice "View door selected while a session is <phase>; retaining it" and return without teardown() and without creating a new session or hiding/re-showing the overlay. If .replace: existing behaviour.
2. Confirm the overlay stays visible and its content is untouched on the retained path (do not call overlay.hide()/show() or setContent).
3. `swift build` and full `swift test` pass.

EDGE CASES: a session in .ended or .failed is replaced (this is the user's retry). nil currentSession behaves exactly as today.

DONE WHEN: clicking View twice while the first session is connecting/streaming leaves the first DoorVideoSession instance running; the log line says "retaining"; ended/failed/nil still replaces; build + tests green.

title: Retain RTP-counter baseline across getStats() gaps so a dead stream cannot re-arm the plateau clock
description:
PROBLEM (minor, found in a24bcb7 review): in DoorVideoFrameView.pollOnce(), when a poll cannot obtain RTP counters (page returned video:null), lastRTPCounters is reset to nil. On the NEXT successful poll, rtpCountersShowProgress(previous: nil, current:) returns true whenever current shows ANY nonzero cumulative traffic — and a DEAD stream's cumulative counters are nonzero forever. So each getStats() gap lets a dead stream count 'progress' once, extending the 2.5s plateau by up to one plateauInterval per gap. Bounded by the 35s hardTimeout, so impact is small — but the semantics are wrong.

PREREQUISITE: gateopener-v6t.2 has moved RTPCounters/rtpCountersShowProgress into GateOpenerCore with tests. Build on that.

FIX (numbered):
1. In DoorVideoFrameView.pollOnce(): when RTP counters are unavailable for a poll, KEEP lastRTPCounters as-is instead of setting it to nil. Update the property's and pollOnce()'s doc comments, which currently justify the nil-reset ('do not compare a FUTURE available sample against a stale baseline').
2. Justify safety in the updated comment: comparing across a gap is safe because (a) a mid-session stats RESET presents as a counter DECREASE, which rtpCountersShowProgress already treats as no-progress and then re-baselines on the assignment that follows; (b) a live stream's counters strictly increase across the gap and correctly count as progress; (c) a dead stream's counters are flat across the gap and correctly do NOT count.
3. Verify the session-start reset path still nulls the baseline: startSession() sets lastRTPCounters = nil — that must remain, it is the intended fresh-baseline point.
4. Add test(s) in Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/DoorVideoLivenessTests.swift capturing the gap scenario at the pure-function level: sequence [counters C, gap, C again] must yield no progress when the baseline is retained (i.e. assert rtpCountersShowProgress(previous: C, current: C) == false — trivially true today, so ALSO add a comment-anchored test documenting that the nil-baseline + nonzero-current == true behavior is exactly why the caller must not nil the baseline mid-session). If the implementer finds a cleaner way to encode the caller contract as a pure function (e.g. a small reducer taking Optional current), that refactor is IN scope provided v6t.2's existing tests still pass.

AMBIGUITY FLAG: the poll-loop side (pollOnce) remains untestable until gateopener-4ub.22 lands an app test target; this task only guarantees the pure-logic level. That residual gap stays with 4ub.22 — do not attempt an app test target here.

DONE-CRITERIA: swift build && swift test pass; lastRTPCounters is no longer nulled on an unavailable poll (only at session start); doc comments updated to the new rationale; new pure-level test(s) present and passing.

title: Cover the verify-before-install ordering against real code, not a mirror
description:
DISCOVERED during review of gateopener-c33.7. Not a bug — a test-coverage limitation worth closing before the updater ships to real users.

THE GAP
UpdateOrderingTests proves that nothing destructive runs when UpdateInstaller.verify() throws. But it proves it against a MIRROR of UpdateChecker.downloadVerifyAndInstall's control flow, re-implemented as a pure function in the test file, not against the real method. The reviewer read both and confirmed they currently correspond exactly.
The risk is drift: a future edit that hoisted launchSwap above verify() in the REAL UpdateChecker would not fail any test. The single most important safety property of the updater — verify before anything irreversible — is therefore protected by reviewer vigilance rather than by the suite.
This is a structural limit, not laziness: the test target links GateOpenerCore only, and UpdateChecker lives in the AppKit-dependent GateOpener target. The tests are honest about it in their doc comment.

DO
1. Make the ordering testable against the REAL path. Options, pick one and justify:
   a. Extract the download -> verify -> install sequence into a pure, injectable function in GateOpenerCore that UpdateChecker calls, so the test exercises the actual production code rather than a copy.
   b. Add an app-layer test target (see gateopener-4ub.22, which tracks the absence of one) and test UpdateChecker directly.
   (a) is likely cheaper and does not depend on 4ub.22.
2. The test must FAIL if launchSwap is moved before verify(), or if the verify-throws path stops deleting the temp download. Prove both by mutation and state how you confirmed it (see bd memory gateopener-vacuous-assertion-failure-mode).
3. Delete the mirrored test once the real path is covered — leaving both invites the mirror to drift silently.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT weaken verify() or change its semantics.
- Do NOT change the swap script's guards (empty/root install dir, bundle name with a path separator) added in c33.7.
- Keep the ordering guarantee exactly as it is: verify throws -> temp download deleted, app untouched, nothing destructive attempted.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The ordering property is asserted against production code, not a copy.
- Mutating the real UpdateChecker to hoist launchSwap above verify() makes a test fail.
- swift build; swift test; GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.

title: Tighten DMG URL pin from host-only to OWNER/REPO release path
description:
DISCOVERED during review of gateopener-c33.6. Not a defect — a deliberate interim that should tighten once the repo exists.

CURRENT STATE
UpdateInstaller pins the manifest's dmgURL host to the literal "github.com" (UpdateInstaller.swift ~:58-77). That correctly blocks the main attack: a malicious manifest naming an attacker-controlled host. Userinfo spoofing (https://github.com@evil.com -> host evil.com) and suffix spoofing (github.com.evil.com) were both probed during review and are rejected.

THE REMAINING GAP
A host-only pin still permits ANY GitHub user's release asset. Anyone can host a DMG at github.com, so a manifest that somehow reached the app could name https://github.com/attacker/repo/releases/download/v1/evil.dmg and pass the host check. The digest check does not help — the digest only proves the file matches what the MANIFEST said, and the manifest is what an attacker would control.
This was left as-is deliberately: no OWNER/REPO constant exists anywhere in the codebase yet, and hardcoding a placeholder would be either wrong or silently stale. The code comment already says exactly this.

DO — once a real OWNER/REPO is known (i.e. after the GitHub remote exists, gateopener-c33.4)
1. Introduce a single authoritative OWNER/REPO constant. Prefer deriving it the same way the release target does (from `git remote get-url origin`) if that is reachable at build time, else a clearly-marked constant next to the existing pinnedDMGHost.
2. Tighten validateManifestDMGURL to also require the release-download PATH SHAPE, not just the host: /OWNER/REPO/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>. Reject anything else.
3. Keep the existing host, scheme, userinfo and suffix protections exactly as they are — this is additive.
4. Add tests for the new rejections: right host but wrong owner, right owner but wrong repo, right repo but a non-release path, and a path-traversal attempt.
5. Each new assertion must be non-vacuous — it must fail if the corresponding guard is removed. State how you confirmed it (see bd memory gateopener-vacuous-assertion-failure-mode).

DONE-CRITERIA
- The URL check requires host AND the OWNER/REPO release-download path shape.
- A manifest naming a different GitHub owner or repo is rejected.
- Existing verify() behaviour is otherwise unchanged; all current tests still pass.
- swift build; swift test; GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.

title: Rapid reopen sometimes gets HTTP 200 but no frames; bound the wait
description:
OBSERVED during gateopener-f8w.2 verification (2026-08-28), on real hardware. NOT introduced by that change — flagging because it is user-visible and currently silent.

WHAT WAS SEEN
In 2 of 5 rapid reopen attempts, a second rtc/offer issued shortly after a previous session ended succeeded at the SDP level (HTTP 200, answer received) but NO video frames ever arrived. The session sat in .connecting indefinitely.
This is consistent with previously-documented door behaviour in ../comelit's memories (session liveness / rate-limiting around back-to-back sessions), not a defect in this app's code.

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR, which is safe but not great
Thanks to gateopener-f8w.2 the canned gate animation stays up and holds its final frame indefinitely rather than blanking or showing a stale camera frame. So nothing is WRONG on screen — but the user gets no indication that live video is not coming, and on the gate-open path the overlay is hidden only when the video session ends, so a session that never streams may leave the panel up until its hard timeout.

DO
1. Reproduce: trigger two sessions in quick succession (end one, immediately start another) and confirm the no-frames-after-200 case. Record how often it happens and whether a longer gap avoids it.
2. Decide and implement a bounded, honest fallback. Candidates:
   - Treat "SDP succeeded but no first frame within N seconds" as a failure and end the session, so the overlay resolves rather than waiting for the hard timeout. There is already a first-frame timeout concept in ../comelit (FIRST_FRAME_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10s) worth mirroring.
   - Optionally show a brief honest message ("camera unavailable") before the overlay disappears, rather than silently showing only the canned animation.
   Do NOT add automatic retry/renegotiation — the epic explicitly descoped session continuation, and hammering the door is exactly what the rate-limiting appears to guard against.
3. Whatever you choose, the gate-open path must still degrade to canned-animation-only cleanly, with no stranded panel.

CONSTRAINTS
- Never take keyboard focus: orderFrontRegardless only.
- Keep the canvas-capture architecture, the byte-comparison plateau detector, and framesDecoded>0 streaming detection.
- rtc/offer only; never the power/open endpoint.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The no-frames case resolves within a bounded time rather than hanging until the hard timeout.
- No stranded panel in that case, on either entry point.
- Normal sessions still stream and still end via the plateau detector at ~28-30s.
- swift build; swift test; GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.

title: Regression test: no stale frame on overlay reopen
description:
INPUT: the committed fix from the previous bead. This bead adds the test that keeps it fixed.

WHY
The stale-frame bug is invisible to every existing signal: the session streams correctly, stats are right, the panel is visible, focus is preserved, and the plateau detector still ends the session. Only a human looking at the panel in the first ~2 seconds of a SECOND run can see it. That is exactly the class of bug this project has shipped before (gateopener-9kk.12 and gateopener-12h.5 both had working plumbing and wrong pixels), and exactly the class a future refactor would silently reintroduce.

CHECK THIS FIRST, AND STOP IF IT BLOCKS
The overlay/video types live in Sources/GateOpener, and per gateopener-4ub.22 there is currently NO test target covering the app layer — only GateOpenerCoreTests. Determine whether an app-layer test target exists yet.
IF IT DOES NOT: say so plainly, add a dependency on gateopener-4ub.22, and STOP. Do NOT restructure Package.swift as a side effect of a test bead.

DO (assuming a test target exists)
1. Add tests asserting the invariant the fix establishes, driving the presentation layer directly rather than through the network. The point is to test the VIEW/CONTROLLER lifecycle, not WebRTC:
   a. After a session ends and a new one starts, the panel does NOT display any image belonging to the prior session — the connecting placeholder (or empty content) is shown until a frame from the NEW session arrives.
   b. A frame delivered by a session that has already ended is NOT displayed.
   c. The normal path still works: a frame from the CURRENT session IS displayed.
   d. Both entry points are covered — the DoorVideoOverlayController ("View Door") path and the OverlayWindowController open-gate path — unless the fix genuinely unified them into one code path, in which case test that once and say so.
2. NON-VACUOUSNESS IS THE POINT. Each assertion must FAIL against the pre-fix behavior. Confirm by temporarily reverting the fix (or mutating the specific guard) and observing the test fail; state in your report exactly how you confirmed it. See bd memory gateopener-vacuous-assertion-failure-mode for why this repo insists.
3. Prefer a seam that does not require a live door: inject or simulate frame delivery and session-end rather than opening a real WebRTC session. If a small internal test seam is needed, keep it minimal and internal — do NOT widen the public surface, and do NOT expose show()/hide() further (gateopener-9kk.9 deliberately tightened those).

CONSTRAINTS
- Tests only. No production behavior change beyond a minimal justified test seam.
- Do not weaken the focus guarantee, the canvas-capture architecture, the plateau detector, or framesDecoded>0 streaming detection.
- Do not require real hardware to run the suite — swift test must stay hermetic and fast.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The assertions above exist and genuinely discriminate, with the confirmation method stated.
- swift test passes; GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.
- No new network or hardware dependency in the test suite.

title: Strip or DEBUG-gate the throwaway verification paths in GateOpenerApp
description:
DISCOVERED during the gateopener-12h live-video work. Cleanup, not a defect — but it ships in the release binary today.

PROBLEM
Sources/GateOpener/GateOpenerApp.swift accumulated several env-gated throwaway verification paths added to drive features against real hardware while building epic 12h:
  - GATEOPENER_VERIFY_DOOR_VIDEO (+ GATEOPENER_VERIFY_DOOR_VIDEO_DWELL_MS)
  - GATEOPENER_VERIFY_PANEL_CAPTURE
  - GATEOPENER_VERIFY_VIEW_DOOR_MENU
They were genuinely necessary — the only way to observe WebRTC behaviour against the real door — and they are inert unless their env var is set. But they are dead weight in a shipping app, and this repo is intended for public release (see gateopener-4ub.13).
Note there is precedent for caring about this: gateopener-3vq.6 tracks a test-only failure-injection hook shipping in release builds.

DO
1. Inventory every GATEOPENER_VERIFY_* / GATEOPENER_MEASURE_* path in Sources/ and list them with line references before changing anything.
2. Decide per path, and justify: DELETE it, or keep it behind a compile-time guard (e.g. #if DEBUG) so it cannot exist in a release build.
   Recommendation: keep GATEOPENER_VERIFY_DOOR_VIDEO in some form — it is the fastest way to check the door pipeline end to end when something breaks — but compile it out of release. Delete the narrower one-shot experiment paths whose questions are now answered (PANEL_CAPTURE especially: its finding is recorded in bd memory gateopener-live-video-architecture).
3. Do NOT remove the GATEOPENER_MOCK / GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST paths — those are the established self-test mechanism and are load-bearing for CI-style verification.
4. Whatever you keep must not change behaviour when its env var is unset.

DONE-CRITERIA
- No verification-only code path is reachable in a release build, or a clear justification is given for each one kept.
- swift build; swift test (126 at filing); GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.
- The real app still launches and opens the gate normally.

title: Regression tests for the fadeOutThenHide self-cancellation ordering
description:
DISCOVERED during review of gateopener-9kk.9. No bug today — this locks in a guarantee that currently rests on line ordering plus a comment.

THE GUARANTEE AT RISK
fadeOutThenHide() calls hide(), and hide() now calls cancelPendingResolve(), which cancels pendingResolveTask — the very task still executing. That is safe ONLY because fadeOutThenHide() contains exactly ONE Task.isCancelled check and it sits BEFORE the hide() call, with zero suspension points after it. Adding a second isCancelled check below hide(), or introducing an await in the tail, would silently reintroduce the stranding/invisible-overlay hazard. Nothing would catch it: there is no test, and the compiler cannot see the constraint.
There is a warning comment in the source, but a comment is not a test.

DO
1. FIRST check whether an app-layer test target exists. OverlayWindowController lives in Sources/GateOpener and per gateopener-4ub.22 only GateOpenerCoreTests exists today. This bead is blocked on that. If the target is still missing, SAY SO AND STOP — do not restructure Package.swift as a side effect.
2. Add regression tests covering:
   a. External hide() called while a resolve-fade is pending leaves isResolveFadePending == false and pendingResolveTask == nil.
   b. After that external hide(), a subsequent .idle via handle(_:) is HONORED rather than swallowed by the !isResolveFadePending guard.
   c. A normal .succeeded resolve completes its hold-then-fade and ends with alphaValue == 1, isResolveFadePending == false, and the panel hidden.
   d. A second .opening arriving mid-fade cancels the pending fade, restores alpha to 1, and leaves the panel visible — the invisible-overlay regression from 9kk.5.
3. Each assertion must be NON-VACUOUS: it must fail if the corresponding guard is removed, inverted, or if a second Task.isCancelled check is added after hide(). Confirm by temporarily mutating the source and observing the failure. See bd memory gateopener-vacuous-assertion-failure-mode for why this repo insists.
4. Timing: the resolve path uses a 1200ms hold plus a 250ms fade. Do NOT write tests that sleep for real. Prefer injecting the durations, or drive the state machine directly and assert on the synchronous state rather than on wall-clock outcomes. If injection requires a small production seam, keep it minimal and internal — do not widen the public surface.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The four cases above are covered and genuinely discriminate.
- swift test passes; each new assertion demonstrably fails against a deliberately broken variant.
- No production behavior change beyond any minimal test seam, which must be justified in the report.
- The focus guarantee (orderFrontRegardless only) and the handle(_:)-only contract are untouched.

title: Regression test for toggle-off-while-overlay-visible (no stranded panel)
description:
DISCOVERED during review of gateopener-9kk.7. The FIX is committed (020d301) and verified by code inspection; this bead adds the test that locks it in.

WHY THIS MATTERS
9kk.7 fixed a real stranding bug: handle(_:) previously opened with a blanket "guard appSettings.showOpenConfirmationOverlay else { return }", so flipping the setting OFF while an overlay was visible made the subsequent .succeeded/.idle return early and never call hide() — leaving the panel on screen permanently, with nothing able to dismiss it, since handle(_:) is the sole presentation driver. The fix narrows the gate to .opening only.
That behavior is currently protected by nothing but reviewer vigilance. It is exactly the kind of subtle guard a future "simplification" would revert.

WHY IT IS CHEAP
handle(_:) is synchronous, @MainActor, and takes AppSettings by injection, so a test can drive it directly with an isolated UserDefaults suite — no GUI, no window server, no timing.

DO
1. Note the constraint FIRST: OverlayWindowController lives in Sources/GateOpener, and per bead gateopener-4ub.22 there is currently NO test target covering the app layer — only GateOpenerCoreTests. Determine whether adding an app-layer test target is in scope here, or whether this bead should be blocked on 4ub.22. If it needs 4ub.22 first, SAY SO AND STOP rather than restructuring Package.swift as a side effect of a test bead.
2. Assuming a test target exists, add tests asserting:
   a. setting ON, .opening then .succeeded — panel shown then hidden, no stranded panel.
   b. setting ON, .opening, then setting flipped OFF mid-show, then .succeeded — panel is STILL hidden. This is the regression case; it must FAIL against the pre-fix blanket guard.
   c. setting OFF from the start, .opening — no panel created at all, proving the toggle genuinely suppresses.
   d. setting OFF from the start, .succeeded/.idle with no panel — no panel created as a side effect, no crash.
3. The assertions must be non-vacuous: each must fail if the corresponding guard is removed or inverted. State in your report how you confirmed that, e.g. by temporarily mutating the guard and observing the test fail. See bd memory gateopener-vacuous-assertion-failure-mode for why this repo insists on it.
4. Observing "panel shown/hidden" may need a seam, since the panel property is private. Prefer a minimal test-visible accessor, e.g. an internal read-only isPanelVisible, or @testable import, over widening the public surface. Do NOT expose show()/hide() further — bead gateopener-9kk.9 is separately tightening those.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The four cases above are covered by tests that genuinely discriminate.
- swift test passes, and each new assertion demonstrably fails against a deliberately reverted guard.
- No production behavior change — this bead adds tests only.
- The focus guarantee and the handle(_:)-only contract are untouched.

title: setContent while the overlay panel is visible never fires overlayWillShow
description:
DISCOVERED during review of gateopener-9kk.4. NOT a bug today — no caller does this — but it is exactly the trap the live-camera work will hit.

PROBLEM
OverlayWindowController.setContent(_:) installs the new view into the visible panel but does NOT invoke overlayWillShow() on it. The OverlayShowHideResponding hooks fire only from show() and hide().
Consequence: swapping content INTO an already-visible panel leaves that content un-started. For a GateOpenVideoView (or a future RTCMTLNSVideoView) that means it sits on frame zero — a black or frozen tile — until the next full show/hide cycle.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR gateopener-12h
The live door-camera feature is the likely first real caller of setContent(_:) against a visible panel: show the panel, then swap in the video view once the WebRTC session produces a first frame. That is precisely the ordering this gap breaks, and the symptom (a black tile that never starts) would look like a WebRTC failure rather than a lifecycle bug — expensive to misdiagnose given how much of that epic is already about debugging why no frames arrive.

DO
1. In OverlayWindowController.setContent(_:), if the panel exists AND is currently visible, invoke overlayWillShow() on the newly-installed content after installing it.
2. Do NOT fire it when the panel is not visible — show() will do that. Guard on the panel's isVisible.
3. Ensure the OUTGOING content gets overlayDidHide() when it is replaced, so a swapped-out player pauses rather than continuing to decode off-screen.
4. Preserve the existing focus guarantee exactly: no makeKeyAndOrderFront, no NSApp.activate, and do not reorder the panel as a side effect of swapping content.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Swapping content into a visible panel starts the new content (verifiable with the existing GateOpenVideoView: swap it in while visible and confirm playback begins from frame zero rather than freezing there).
- Swapping content OUT pauses the outgoing content.
- No change to behavior when setContent is called before show().
- swift build + swift test still green (126 tests at time of filing).
close_reason: Superseded by gateopener-12h.2, which covers the same setContent/overlayWillShow gap with fuller done-criteria as part of the live-video epic decomposition.

title: Operator check of the open overlay
description:
INPUT
The complete feature. This is a human-in-the-loop acceptance pass; the implementer's job is to prepare and drive it, not to declare it passed alone.

OUTPUT
A written verdict on the feature against the user's stated intent: 'non-obtrusive if you don't care, easy to see if you do'.

STEPS
1. Build and install the app the way the Makefile installs it, and launch it from /Applications (not from .build — several behaviors here are bundle-dependent).
2. Run through this checklist, recording PASS/FAIL and a one-line note for each:
   a. Hotkey while actively typing in another app (e.g. a text editor): overlay appears, and NOT ONE KEYSTROKE is lost or misrouted. This is the acceptance gate for the whole feature — if focus is stolen, the feature is wrong.
   b. Menu-item 'Open Gate': overlay appears.
   c. Left-click on the menu-bar item: overlay appears.
   d. Overlay duration visually matches the open sequence — it is up while the gate is being opened and gone shortly after it resolves.
   e. Failure case (use the existing MockGateOpening failure-injection hook to force a failure): overlay leaves promptly and does NOT read as success; the failure notification still posts.
   f. Slow open: the overlay keeps running for the whole attempt rather than timing out early.
   g. Over a full-screen app: the overlay is visible and does not force a space switch.
   h. On an external display / with the menu bar on a second screen: the overlay lands on a sensible screen. Note which. If no second display is available, say so rather than guessing.
   i. Rapid repeat triggers: no stacked panels, no visual corruption.
   j. Reduce Motion on: static, informative, no animation.
   k. Settings toggle off: no overlay, next open onward.
3. Report the results as a table. Any FAIL becomes a follow-up bead — file it, do not fix it in this task.

DONE CRITERIA
- All eleven checks recorded with an explicit verdict.
- Check (a) passes, or the feature is reported as NOT shippable.
- Any failures filed as new beads with reproduction steps.

title: Honor Reduce Motion and add the Settings toggle
description:
INPUT
A fully wired overlay (gateopener-9kk.6) and the showOpenOverlay setting (gateopener-9kk.1). Read Sources/GateOpener/SettingsView.swift and find the existing toggle-style control (e.g. Launch at Login) to copy its binding pattern.

OUTPUT
The overlay is accessible and user-controllable.

STEPS
1. Reduce Motion: in OverlayWindowController, check NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion at show()-time. When true, do NOT play the looping video — display a single static frame instead (seek to a representative time and pause, or render one frame as an image), and skip the fade animation, using a plain orderOut instead. The overlay still APPEARS — Reduce Motion means less motion, not less information.
2. Read the flag at show()-time rather than caching it at init, so a user changing the system setting does not need to relaunch.
3. Settings UI: add a toggle labelled 'Show overlay when opening the gate' bound to AppSettings.showOpenOverlay, placed near the other app-behavior controls in SettingsView.swift. Match the existing control's binding idiom exactly — do not introduce a different state-management approach.
4. Add explanatory secondary text under the toggle if the existing rows do so; if they do not, add none. Match the surrounding style.
5. Edge case: toggling the setting OFF while an overlay is currently on screen. Decide and implement — the reasonable behavior is that the current overlay finishes naturally and no future one is shown. Comment the decision. Do NOT leave a stranded panel visible forever.
6. Accessibility of the panel itself: because it is a non-interactive decoration that duplicates information already in the menu-bar icon and tooltip, mark the content view accessibilityElement = false / set an appropriate role so VoiceOver does not announce a focus-stealing element. Confirm the panel is not reachable by keyboard.

DONE CRITERIA
- 'swift build' succeeds and 'swift test' still passes.
- With System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Reduce Motion ON, an open shows a static overlay with no animation and no fade. Report this manual check.
- Unchecking the Settings toggle suppresses the overlay on the very next open, with no relaunch.
- Re-checking it restores it.
- The setting survives a quit and relaunch (this exercises gateopener-9kk.1 end to end).

title: 838 stray test plists accumulating in ~/Library/Preferences
description:
FOUND during the bead gateopener-3vq.4 re-review. Pre-existing and project-wide, NOT introduced by that bead.

PROBLEM
~/Library/Preferences now holds 838 stray 'ie.boboco.GateOpener.tests.<UUID>.plist' files, about 3.3 MB. Multiple test files create UUID-unique throwaway UserDefaults suites; removePersistentDomain(forName:) erases the CONTENTS but cfprefsd does not unlink the backing file, so every run leaves empty plists behind permanently.

This supersedes the narrower gateopener-4ub.16, which described the same root cause when the count was 570 and framed it as an AppSettingsTests-only issue. It is broader: several test files do this, and the count keeps climbing with every run.

SEVERITY: low individually (each file is empty, ~42 bytes, holds no data) but the growth is unbounded and it litters the operator's real Preferences directory.

DO
1. Add a shared test helper that creates a throwaway suite AND fully removes it — removePersistentDomain plus deleting the backing plist at ~/Library/Preferences/<suiteName>.plist, tolerating absence.
2. Route EVERY test that creates a UserDefaults suite through that helper (KeyboardShortcutTests, AppSettingsTests, and any others — grep for 'suiteName').
3. Clean up the existing 838 files as a one-off (the orchestrator has already deleted them once at 570; they came back).
4. Keep the existing guarantee intact: tests must never touch the real ie.boboco.GateOpener domain.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Count files matching ~/Library/Preferences/ie.boboco.GateOpener.tests.*.plist before and after a full 'swift test': the delta is 0.
- 'swift test' still passes twice consecutively.
- 'defaults read ie.boboco.GateOpener' is unchanged by a test run.

title: Test-only failure-injection hook ships in release builds
description:
FOUND by the bead gateopener-3vq.2 reviewer. Judged non-blocking (hygiene, not a live vulnerability) but should be closed out.

PROBLEM
GlobalHotkey.swift:388 declares:
    var forceNextRegistrationFailureForSelfTest = false
It has NO '#if DEBUG' guard and no environment guard. 'grep -rn "#if DEBUG" Sources/' finds none anywhere in the project. So a mutable backdoor that can force the global hotkey's registration to fail is compiled into RELEASE builds — including the .app installed at /Applications.

SEVERITY: low. The property is 'internal' (not public), and the only writer is the self-test block which runs solely under GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1. Nothing in normal operation flips it. So this is hygiene, not an exploitable hole.

WHY STILL WORTH FIXING: the hotkey is the operator's PRIMARY way to open the gate (the menu-bar icon is parked off-screen at x=-10329 because the menu bar is full). A production-reachable switch that can silently disable hotkey registration is exactly the wrong thing to ship, however unlikely it is to be flipped.

WORTH PRESERVING: the reviewer confirmed the hook is GOOD test design — it short-circuits inside registerHotKey, so registerWithFallback's real snapshot/retry/clear logic still runs. It does not shortcut to a canned answer. Do NOT replace it with a mock that bypasses the real path.

DO
1. Guard the hook so it cannot exist in release builds. Options: wrap the property and its use sites in '#if DEBUG'; or gate it behind the same GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST environment check the self-test already uses; or move it behind a protocol seam injected only by the self-test.
2. Keep the self-test's failure-preservation assertion working in debug builds — do not weaken it into proving only its own mock.
3. While there, consider whether any OTHER self-test-only affordance is similarly unguarded (e.g. simulateClickForSelfTest in StatusItemController). Report what you find; fix only what is genuinely test-only.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A release build ('swift build -c release') contains no path that can set forceNextRegistrationFailureForSelfTest.
- The debug self-test still asserts that a failed registration preserves the previous working chord, and still FAILS with a non-zero exit if that logic is broken (mutation-test it, do not assert it).
- swift test passes; zero warnings; SELFTEST PASS in debug.

title: Hotkey registration is not re-checked after launch
description:
FOUND by the bead gateopener-iif.2 reviewer. Non-blocking, but a real correctness gap.

PROBLEM
Carbon RegisterEventHotKey is first-come-first-served. GateOpener registers Cmd-Ctrl-Opt-G at launch and records the result in 'isRegistered'/'lastRegistrationError'. If ANOTHER app claims the same chord AFTER GateOpener has launched, GateOpener's registration can stop working — but nothing re-checks it. Settings would continue to display the shortcut as registered and working while the chord is actually dead.

WHY IT MATTERS
This is the affordance the operator relies on precisely BECAUSE the menu bar icon is unreachable (parked off-screen at x=-10329). Silently believing the hotkey works when it does not is worse than knowing it is broken — the operator would press it at the gate and nothing would happen.

DO
1. Re-verify hotkey registration when the Settings window opens, and refresh the displayed status.
2. Consider a lightweight periodic or event-driven re-check (e.g. on app activation). Do NOT poll aggressively — this is a menu-bar utility that should stay idle.
3. If the hotkey is found dead, surface it clearly in Settings and attempt re-registration once.
4. Distinguish honestly in the UI between 'registered and working', 'never registered (chord taken at launch)', and 'was registered, now lost'.

DONE-CRITERIA
- With a harness holding the chord, opening Settings shows the shortcut as unavailable rather than as working.
- Releasing the chord and reopening Settings shows it recovered (or offers a retry that succeeds).
- No busy-polling: demonstrate the re-check is triggered by an event, not a tight timer.
- swift test still passes; zero warnings; SELFTEST PASS.

title: Make the global hotkey editable (recorder UI)
description:
FOLLOW-UP promised by bead gateopener-iif.2, which shipped the shortcut as READ-ONLY by explicit permission ('If a full recorder UI is too large for this task... expose the current shortcut read-only and file a follow-up'). The .2 reviewer noted the follow-up did not yet exist. This is it.

CURRENT STATE
Cmd-Ctrl-Opt-G is hardcoded in GlobalHotkey.swift and displayed read-only in Settings' 'Keyboard Shortcut' section. If it collides with something the operator uses, they cannot change it without a rebuild.

DO
1. Add a shortcut recorder to the Settings 'Keyboard Shortcut' section: click to record, capture the next chord, display it.
2. Persist the chosen chord in AppSettings (NON-SECRET config — keyCode + modifier mask; do NOT put it in the Keychain).
3. On change: unregister the old hotkey, register the new one, and surface failure inline if the new chord is already taken — reverting to the previous working chord rather than leaving the app with no hotkey at all.
4. REJECT unsafe chords. This fires a REAL GATE. Require at least two modifiers; refuse a bare key or a single-modifier combination, with a clear explanation. A gate that opens on an accidental keypress is a genuine hazard.
5. Provide a 'Reset to default' action returning to Cmd-Ctrl-Opt-G.
6. Keep the read-only display working when no custom chord is set.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Recording a new chord re-registers the hotkey and it fires openGate() (verify with the mock self-test, NEVER by pressing it against a real build).
- A chord with fewer than two modifiers is rejected with a visible explanation.
- A collision with an already-registered chord surfaces inline and leaves the PREVIOUS hotkey working.
- The choice survives an app restart.
- swift test still passes; zero warnings; SELFTEST PASS.

title: Verify Launch at Login now works from /Applications
description:
WHY: bead gateopener-4ub.11 implemented Launch at Login via SMAppService.mainApp, but it could never be verified — the app was not in /Applications, and registering a real login item is a side effect no agent should perform unasked. Once the app is properly installed, this becomes testable.

ALSO: gateopener-4ub.11's review found and FIXED a real bug here — kSMErrorLaunchDeniedByUser is 11, not 1 (verified against SMErrors.h, where the enum starts at kSMErrorInternalFailure = 2). With the wrong constant, a genuine user denial was misreported as 'Move GateOpener to /Applications first', sending the operator to fix the wrong thing. This bead confirms the fix in the field.

THIS IS AN OPERATOR-ASSISTED TASK. The agent prepares and instructs; the OPERATOR performs the toggling and reports what they saw. Do not register login items on the operator's machine unprompted.

DO
1. Confirm the app is installed at /Applications/GateOpener.app and is ad-hoc signed (codesign --verify --deep --strict).
2. Provide the operator with a short, explicit checklist:
   a. Open Settings, toggle Launch at Login ON. Expect: no error, and the toggle stays on.
   b. Confirm it registered: 'sudo -u "ebowman" /bin/launchctl print gui/501 | grep -i gateopener' or check System Settings > General > Login Items for GateOpener.
   c. Toggle OFF and confirm it deregisters.
   d. THE IMPORTANT ONE: deny it — in System Settings > General > Login Items, disable GateOpener's entry, then toggle ON from within the app. Expect the message 'Launch at Login was denied. Enable it for GateOpener in System Settings > General > Login Items.' — and specifically NOT 'Move GateOpener to /Applications first'. That misattribution was the bug; this is the field confirmation.
   e. Confirm the toggle reconciles to the TRUE system state after a failure (it must not stay showing the attempted value).
3. Record the operator's observed results in the bead notes and via 'bd remember' if anything surprising turns up.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Operator confirms Launch at Login registers and deregisters cleanly from /Applications.
- Operator confirms a DENIAL produces the Login Items message, not the /Applications message.
- Operator confirms the toggle never displays a state the system does not actually have.
- Any discrepancy is filed as a new bead rather than silently fixed here.

title: No test target covers the app layer (Sources/GateOpener)
description:
STRUCTURAL GAP — this is why the LaunchAtLogin bug shipped.

PROBLEM
Package.swift declares exactly one test target, GateOpenerCoreTests, depending only on GateOpenerCore. NOTHING in Sources/GateOpener/ has any test coverage: LaunchAtLogin, GateIcon, StatusItemController, GateControllerObservable, NotificationPresenter, SettingsView.

WHAT IT COST
Bead .11's reviewer found 'case 1: // kSMErrorLaunchDeniedByUser' — the real value is 11 (SDK SMErrors.h: the enum starts at kSMErrorInternalFailure = 2). The constant appeared ONLY in a comment, so the compiler could not catch the drift and no test existed to catch it either. Consequence: a genuine user denial was misreported as 'Move GateOpener to /Applications first', sending the user to fix the wrong thing. A single unit test over the pure Error->message mapping would have caught it immediately.

The orchestrator verified the corrected mapping with a standalone script (denial=11 recognized; the old code 1 NOT treated as denial; code 11 in NSPOSIXErrorDomain not a false positive), but that verification is NOT part of the suite and will not run again.

DO
1. Add a test target for the app layer. Because the executable target cannot be imported directly, EITHER:
   (a) Extract the pure, UI-free logic into a small library target (e.g. GateOpenerAppSupport) that both the executable and a new test target depend on — LaunchAtLogin.from(), GateIcon's state->symbol/tooltip mapping, and the tooltip-escalation timing are all pure and testable; OR
   (b) Add '.testTarget(name: "GateOpenerTests", dependencies: ["GateOpener"])' if SwiftPM permits testing the executable target on this toolchain (verify — historically executable targets are not importable).
   Prefer (a); it is the standard workaround and keeps the executable thin.
2. Port the orchestrator's SMError verification into a real test: denial code 11 in an SM domain maps to the denial message; code 1 does NOT; code 11 in NSPOSIXErrorDomain does NOT; already-registered (12) and invalid-signature (3) map correctly.
3. Add tests for GateIcon: all five GateStates yield DISTINCT symbols and non-empty tooltips (a duplicate symbol would make two states visually indistinguishable in the menu bar).

DONE-CRITERIA
- 'swift test' runs app-layer tests as part of the normal suite.
- The SMError mapping test FAILS if 'case 11' is reverted to 'case 1' — prove it, do not assert it.
- No SwiftUI/AppKit is pulled into GateOpenerCore by this change (bead .1's headless constraint still holds).

title: Log records only coarse open events, not attempt/status/token/login/discovery detail
description:
REPORTED HONESTLY by the bead .10 implementer rather than concealed. Not a defect in .10's own scope — a structural limit.

WHAT IS RECORDED TODAY
The app layer observes GateController.onStateChange, so it can only log what GateState carries:
 - logOpenAttempt on .opening — always recorded as 'attempt 1 of 1'
 - logOpenSucceeded on .succeeded
 - logOpenFailed(reason: .unknown) on .failed — always .unknown

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
 - the REAL attempt count and HTTP status per retry (logOpenFailed(status:))
 - logTokenRefreshed, logLoginPerformed, logDiscoveryPerformed
Reason: that detail lives inside GateClient.open's internal retry loop and inside TokenManager/ComelitAPI. GateState carries only a short human message, so the app layer cannot see it. The .10 brief explicitly forbade restructuring committed core types.

WHY IT MATTERS
This log exists so the operator can diagnose a gate that misbehaves. 'attempt 1 of 1 / unknown' is materially less useful than 'attempt 2 of 3 failed with HTTP 500'. Given the cloud transiently 500s (which is exactly why retry is mandatory), the retry detail is the single most valuable thing the log could show — and it is the part currently missing.

DO (requires a scoped core change, hence a separate bead)
1. Give GateOpenerCore a way to surface per-attempt detail. Options, in preference order:
   (a) Inject the EventLog (or a small logging protocol) into GateClient so its retry loop records each attempt and status directly at the source — cleanest, keeps GateState simple.
   (b) Add a callback/delegate on GateClient (e.g. onAttempt(attempt:of:status:)) that the app layer subscribes to.
   (c) Enrich GateState.failed with structured detail — least preferred, it complicates a type whose simplicity the UI depends on.
2. Wire TokenManager/ComelitAPI similarly for token-refresh, login, and discovery events.
3. Keep the no-secrets guarantee absolutely intact: whatever seam is added must NOT be able to carry a token, password, or Authorization header. Reuse the typed-method/closed-enum discipline already established in EventLog.
4. Update the no-secrets test to cover any new logging path.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A forced 500-then-202 sequence produces log entries naming attempt 1 failed with status 500 and attempt 2 succeeded.
- Token refresh, login, and discovery each produce an entry.
- A test proves no secret can traverse the new seam.
- swift test fully passes.

title: No-secrets log test does not exercise the one channel that can leak
description:
FOUND by the orchestrator while verifying gateopener-4ub.10. Modest gap, not a live leak — filed rather than blocking.

CONTEXT
EventLog's API is deliberately built so secrets cannot be passed: every method is typed with non-secret parameters (logOpenAttempt(attempt:of:), logTokenRefreshed(expiresIn:), logDiscoveryPerformed(endpointCount:), ...). There is NO free-form log(String). That design is good and should be preserved.

THE ONE EXCEPTION
'logOpenFailed(attempt:of:reason: String)' (EventLog.swift:91) takes an arbitrary String. That is the only channel through which a secret could reach the log — e.g. if a caller ever passes an underlying error's description that happens to embed a token, a URL with a query-string credential, or an Authorization header value.

THE TEST GAP
The no-secrets test (EventLogTests.swift:112) feeds secrets past all the typed methods, but calls the reason: channel with the SAFE literal "unauthorized" (line 136). So it proves the safe methods are safe and never exercises the only genuinely risky path. The test's own comment even asserts 'there is no call here that could even syntactically pass the secret through' — which is true of the other methods but NOT of reason:.

DO
1. Extend the no-secrets test to call logOpenFailed(attempt:of:reason:) with a hostile string containing the fake access token, refresh token, and password, then assert those substrings do NOT survive into formattedText()/LogEntry.message.
2. That test will FAIL against today's implementation (the reason string is stored verbatim) — that is the point. Then make it pass by choosing ONE of:
   (a) Sanitize/redact inside logOpenFailed: strip anything resembling a bearer token/JWT/long opaque string (e.g. redact runs of 20+ base64url chars, and anything after 'Bearer '), OR
   (b) Replace the free-form reason: String with a closed enum of known failure reasons (timeout, unauthorized, serverError, transport, ...), eliminating the channel entirely — most in keeping with the rest of the design, and preferred if the call sites allow it.
3. Whichever you choose, keep the existing typed-method design and the 100-entry cap intact.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A test passes a token/password-bearing string through the reason: channel and asserts it does not appear in any log output.
- That test demonstrably fails if the sanitization/enum is removed (prove it, don't assert it).
- 'swift test' still fully passes.
close_reason: Resolved inside bead .10's fix pass: logOpenFailed(reason:) now takes the closed OpenFailureReason enum (no associated String, no ExpressibleByStringLiteral), so a secret cannot syntactically reach the log. Verified by the .10 reviewer, who could not route a secret through any public EventLog API.

title: Flaky test: autoResetUsesInjectedDelayNotRealSleep asserts wall-clock
description:
OBSERVED during parallel work on 2026-08-27: GateControllerTests.swift:302 failed at 0.66s against a 0.5s threshold, purely because three agents were building/testing concurrently on the same machine. It passed immediately on retry. This is a flaky TEST, not a product defect — nothing in GateController changed.

ROOT CAUSE
The test makes two assertions:
  #expect(elapsed < .milliseconds(500))                       // line 302 — WALL CLOCK
  #expect(recordingSleep.requestedDurations == [.seconds(3)]) // line 303 — the real proof
Line 303 is the assertion that actually proves the property: the 3s auto-reset delay was REQUESTED FROM THE INJECTED SLEEP rather than really slept. If the code regressed to a real Task.sleep, requestedDurations would be empty and line 303 would fail.
Line 302 measures wall-clock elapsed time on a shared machine and can fail under any unrelated CPU load (a parallel build, Spotlight, a test run in another checkout). It adds flakiness without adding proof.

DO
1. Either DELETE the wall-clock assertion at line 302, or raise its threshold substantially (e.g. 5s) so it only catches a genuine real-3s-sleep regression rather than incidental load. Deleting is cleaner: line 303 already fully covers the property, and a 5s threshold on a 3s sleep is a weak signal.
2. Scan the rest of the suite for other wall-clock-threshold assertions and apply the same reasoning. Timing assertions that gate on machine speed are a recurring source of false failures.
3. Do NOT weaken line 303 — that is the assertion carrying the meaning.

DONE-CRITERIA
- 'swift test' passes with the suite under artificial load (e.g. run it while a 'swift build' of a clean .build runs concurrently, or under 'nice -n 20' alongside a busy loop) — no timing failures.
- A deliberate regression (swap the injected sleep for a real Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3))) still FAILS the test, proving the remaining assertion has teeth.

title: Mock mode pollutes the real UserDefaults domain (happening now, not latent)
description:
DISCOVERED by the orchestrator while verifying gateopener-4ub.8 (latent, not yet biting).

CURRENT STATE (harmless today)
GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 substitutes MockGateOpening / MockTokenResolving / MockCredentialStore, so mock mode cannot reach the network or the keychain — verified. BUT it still constructs a plain 'AppSettings()' (GateOpenerApp.swift:138), which is backed by STANDARD UserDefaults, and it WRITES to it (sets selectedEndpointId / selectedEndpointName to the fake mock endpoint).
Today this leaves no trace: run under 'swift run' / '.build/debug/GateOpener' the binary has no proper bundle identifier, so those writes land in a transient domain. Verified after a self-test run: 'defaults read ie.boboco.GateOpener' reports 'Domain does not exist', and no stray GateOpener plist exists in ~/Library/Preferences.

THE LATENT BUG
Bead gateopener-4ub.11 packages a real .app with CFBundleIdentifier 'ie.boboco.GateOpener'. From that point on, running mock mode FROM THE BUNDLE would write the FAKE endpoint id/name into the OPERATOR'S REAL preferences domain — silently repointing the app at a non-existent gate, or masking a real selection. That is a genuinely confusing failure: the app would look configured and the gate would never open.

DO
1. In mock mode, inject a THROWAWAY UserDefaults suite rather than .standard — e.g. AppSettings(defaults: UserDefaults(suiteName: "ie.boboco.GateOpener.mock")!) — so mock runs can never touch real settings. AppSettings already supports an injectable suite (init(defaults:)), so this is a small change.
2. Ensure the mock suite is removed (removePersistentDomain) on exit, or at least never read by the real app path.
3. Add a check that running mock mode leaves 'defaults read ie.boboco.GateOpener' unchanged.

DONE-CRITERIA
- After running mock mode FROM A BUILT .app bundle, the real ie.boboco.GateOpener domain is byte-identical to before (or still absent).
- The self-test still passes.
- Real (non-mock) mode still persists to the real domain as normal.

DEPENDENCY: only becomes testable once bead .11 produces the .app bundle, but the fix can and should land before then.
notes: REVIEW: PASS (2026-08-27). Empirically proven across 6 mock runs: BOTH real domains ('GateOpener' and 'ie.boboco.GateOpener') report 'does not exist' before AND after; neither contains MOCK_APT_MOCK#OD#MOCKGATE nor 'Mock Gate (verification mode)'. Mock keys are quarantined in the throwaway ie.boboco.GateOpener.mock suite, which is wiped per run via removePersistentDomain (GateOpenerApp.swift:227) and was cleaned up by the reviewer afterwards. Suite-creation failure fails LOUDLY via fatalError (:224-226) — no silent .standard fallback, which would have reintroduced the original bug. The real (non-mock) path still uses AppSettings() with .standard, unchanged, and now lives only after the isMock early return.

title: Validate the returned OAuth state parameter (dropped in the Swift port)
description:
DISCOVERED during review of gateopener-4ub.2 (reviewed as a follow-up, explicitly NOT pass-blocking).

PROBLEM — empirically confirmed, not merely suspected
ComelitAPI.swift generates a random state (:71), threads it as a parameter (:88), and sends it in the auth body (:101) — then NEVER reads it again. extractCode(fromBodyData:response:) (:144) cannot possibly validate it because the sent state is never passed in. The reviewer proved this on the wire: a stub echoing 'state=TOTALLY-WRONG-STATE' still produced a successful login.

The validated Python reference DOES check it and aborts (comelit/auth.py:136-138):
    returned_state = qs.get('state', [None])[0]
    if returned_state != state:
        raise RuntimeError('login step 1 state mismatch — aborting for safety.')

WHY IT WAS NOT PASS-BLOCKING
This is a resource-owner-password-style flow over TLS: the client posts credentials and receives the code in the SAME response body. There is no browser, no user-agent redirect, and no third-party-controlled entry point, so the code-injection/CSRF threat model that 'state' defends against has no delivery path here. It is a port-fidelity gap rather than an exploitable hole — but the reference deliberately checks it, so close it.

DO
1. Thread the sent state into the code-extraction path so it can be compared (e.g. pass it to extractCode, or return both code and state from extraction and compare in login()).
2. When the response DOES carry a state, compare it to the one sent; on mismatch throw a distinct error (e.g. ComelitError.stateMismatch) and abort — matching auth.py's fail-closed behavior.
3. CRITICAL EDGE CASE, do not skip: the extraction path must TOLERATE AN ABSENT STATE. ComelitAPI.swift:189 handles a JSON body carrying only a 'code' with no state at all; unconditional validation would break that legitimate route. Validate only when a state is actually present.
4. UPDATE THE EXISTING TESTS: ComelitAPITests.swift:144 and :173 currently stub 'state=xyz', which can never match the random UUID the client sends. Those tests pass today precisely BECAUSE no validation exists — they will fail once it lands. Make the stubs echo back the state the client actually sent.
5. Add tests for: matching state succeeds; mismatched state throws .stateMismatch; ABSENT state still succeeds (the :189 route).

DONE-CRITERIA
- A stub echoing a deliberately wrong state now FAILS login with the distinct error (the exact scenario the reviewer used to prove the gap).
- A response with no state at all still logs in successfully.
- Full 'swift test' passes; no test still relies on an unmatchable hardcoded state.
- No secret or state value is logged.

title: Prepare the repo for public GitHub release (do not push)
description:
INPUT: a working, verified app.

The operator will push this to GitHub LATER, by hand. This task PREPARES the repo only. DO NOT create a remote, DO NOT push, DO NOT run 'gh repo create'.

DO
1. Audit the entire git history and working tree for secrets: the operator's password, any access/refresh token, the .comelit_token.json cache, and any real credential. 'git log -p' grep, not just the current tree. Report findings; if anything is found, STOP and report rather than silently rewriting history.
2. Decide and document the aptId question: the operator's aptId (577fcdbf-...) is account-specific. It must NOT be committed as a default. Confirm it is only ever user-supplied or discovered.
3. Write a real README: what it does, a screenshot placeholder, install instructions, build-from-source instructions, macOS 14+ requirement, MIT license, and a SECURITY note saying credentials live in the macOS Keychain and never leave the machine except to api.comelitgroup.com.
4. Add a DISCLAIMER: this is an unofficial third-party client, not affiliated with or endorsed by Comelit; it uses the same cloud API the official app uses; use at your own risk.
5. Add a CONTRIBUTING.md stub and a .github/workflows/ci.yml running 'swift build' and 'swift test' on macos-latest.
6. Add a docs/PROTOCOL.md documenting the reverse-engineered API (endpoints, PKCE flow, the 202/500-retry behavior, the Generic Actuator trap) so the knowledge is not trapped in beads. Cite that this was derived from observing the operator's own account's traffic on their own network.
7. Print the exact 'git remote add' and 'git push' commands for the operator to run themselves — as a PROPOSED command block, not executed.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A secrets audit over full history reports clean (or explicitly reports what was found, having changed nothing).
- CI workflow is syntactically valid.
- README, LICENSE, DISCLAIMER, PROTOCOL.md all present.
- 'git remote -v' is EMPTY — nothing was pushed.

title: Package as a real .app bundle with Launch-at-Login
description:
INPUT: a working app from .8/.9.

WHY: 'swift run' is not a deliverable. This must be an app the operator can drag to /Applications, that starts on login, and that a future task can sign and ship to other Macs.

DO
1. Add a build script (Makefile target or scripts/build-app.sh) that assembles GateOpener.app: correct bundle layout, the SwiftPM-built binary in Contents/MacOS/, and a generated Info.plist with CFBundleIdentifier ie.boboco.GateOpener, CFBundleName GateOpener, a version, LSMinimumSystemVersion 14.0, and LSUIElement=true (menu-bar only, no Dock icon).
2. Add an app icon (AppIcon.icns). A simple generated gate/lock glyph is fine; generate it from an SF Symbol or a small SVG via a scripted iconutil step so it is reproducible, not a hand-placed binary blob.
3. Implement Launch-at-Login using SMAppService.mainApp (ServiceManagement, macOS 13+), exposed as a toggle in Settings that reflects the true current registration status.
4. Ad-hoc codesign the bundle in the build script (codesign --force --deep --sign -) so keychain access and SMAppService behave sanely locally. Note in the README that a Developer ID signature and notarization are required before distributing to other Macs, and that this is tracked separately.
5. README gets a 'Build and install' section with the exact commands.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The build script produces GateOpener.app that launches by double-click from Finder, shows only a menu-bar icon (no Dock icon), and opens the gate on left-click.
- Toggling Launch-at-Login ON then relaunching the login session registers it; the toggle reflects SMAppService.mainApp.status accurately after an app relaunch.
- The script is idempotent and runs from a clean checkout.

EDGE CASES
- SMAppService registration can throw if the bundle is unsigned or in an unexpected location — catch it and surface a clear message ('Move GateOpener to /Applications first') rather than crashing.
- Do not commit the built .app or the .build directory.
close_reason: Reviewed FAIL then fixed and re-verified by the orchestrator. All done-criteria met: idempotent build-app.sh, correct Info.plist (LSUIElement=true, ie.boboco.GateOpener, macOS 14 floor), valid ad-hoc signature under --verify --deep --strict, no Dock icon (lsappinfo type=UIElement), reproducible icon (byte-identical .icns on regeneration, generator degrades gracefully without librsvg), README build/install section, artifacts gitignored, zero secrets. CRITICAL: the bundled app leaves both real UserDefaults domains absent — the first true test of bead .17's fix. The one blocking defect (kSMErrorLaunchDeniedByUser = 11, not 1) is fixed and verified against the SDK header, now matched with its error domain to avoid false positives. Test-coverage gap that allowed it filed as gateopener-4ub.22.

title: Failure notifications and a diagnostic log that never leaks secrets
description:
INPUT: GateController (.7), app shell (.8).

WHY: the operator needs to know, without looking at the menu bar, when the gate genuinely did NOT open — because someone is standing outside waiting.

DO
1. On a .failed outcome post a UserNotifications notification: title 'Gate did not open', body = the controller's short message, plus an action to retry. Request notification authorization lazily on first failure, and degrade silently (icon-only feedback) if the user denies it.
2. Do NOT notify on success — that would be noise. Success is conveyed by the icon only.
3. Add a small in-memory ring buffer (last ~100 entries) of timestamped events: open attempted, attempt N failed with HTTP status, succeeded, token refreshed, login performed. Expose it in Settings behind a 'Show Log' disclosure with a 'Copy' button.
4. HARD REQUIREMENT: no access token, refresh token, password, PKCE verifier, or Authorization header value may ever enter the log or a notification. Log token events as 'refreshed token (expires in Ns)' with no value. Add a unit test that feeds a TokenSet and credentials through the logging path and asserts the secret substrings do not appear in the emitted text.
5. Use os.Logger with a privacy-preserving category for anything that goes to the system log.

DONE-CRITERIA
- 'swift test' passes including the no-secrets-in-log test described above.
- Triggering a forced failure produces exactly one notification, and a success produces none.
- The log view renders and Copy puts plain text on the pasteboard.

EDGE CASES
- Notification authorization denied must not throw or block the open path.
- The ring buffer must be bounded — assert it never exceeds its cap under 1000 appends.
notes:
REVIEW 2: FAIL — STOP CONDITION REACHED (2026-08-27). Bead left OPEN/in_progress; no third fix pass was attempted, per the run's stop conditions.

THREE OF FOUR DEFECTS ARE GENUINELY FIXED AND VERIFIED AT RUNTIME:
 - Defect 1 FIXED: EventLog instantiated (GateOpenerApp.swift:70-72), state transitions logged (:86-108). Self-test 3/3 printed 'entry count: 2', 'recorded open attempt: true', 'recorded open success: true'.
 - Defect 2 FIXED: SettingsView.swift:514-563 renders real formattedText(); placeholder gone; Copy does clearContents()+setString(forType:.string) at :559-561; read-only.
 - Defect 4 FIXED: NotificationPresenter conforms to UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate (:35), routes retryActionIdentifier to handleRetryAction() (:236-248), and the delegate assignment at :125 is strictly AFTER the Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier guard at :109 — the launch-crash fix is NOT regressed (verified: plain unbundled launch alive past 6s).
 - No-secrets guarantee HOLDS: OpenFailureReason is a closed String-raw enum with no associated values and no ExpressibleByStringLiteral; all 11 public logging methods take only Int/TimeInterval/OpenFailureReason; LogEntry.init is internal; a hostile attempt to route a secret through any public API failed.
 - 102/102 tests pass; zero build warnings.

THE ONE REMAINING DEFECT (one line):
EventLog.swift:167
    guard expiresIn >= Double(Int.min), expiresIn <= Double(Int.max) else { return "unknown" }
    return String(Int(expiresIn))          // :168 traps
Double(Int.max) rounds UP to 9223372036854775808.0 == Int.max + 1, which is NOT representable as Int. The '<=' therefore ADMITS it and Int(expiresIn) on the next line traps. Independently confirmed by the orchestrator: Int(exactly: Double(Int.max)) == nil, yet 'd <= Double(Int.max)' is true.
Reachable from the intended call site (expiresAt.timeIntervalSinceNow with a corrupt/absurd stored expiry). .nan/.infinity/-.infinity/1e300 ARE handled correctly; the existing test passes only because it stops at 1e300.

EXACT FIX FOR WHOEVER RESUMES (do NOT let this bead be closed without it):
 1. Use a strict bound or exact conversion, e.g.:
      guard let seconds = Int(exactly: expiresIn.rounded()) else { return "unknown" }
      return String(seconds)
    (or 'expiresIn < Double(Int.max)' with a matching strict lower bound, or clamp).
 2. Extend Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/EventLogTests.swift:57 to include Double(Int.max) AND Double(Int.min) alongside the existing .nan/.infinity/-.infinity/1e300 cases.
 3. Verify the new test FAILS against the current ':167 <=' code before the fix, then passes after — the current test does not catch this.

title: Notarization polish: skip re-submission, settle the DMG timestamp
description:
DISCOVERED during review of gateopener-c33.3. Both are polish, neither is a defect. Low priority — do not let these block release work.

1. RE-NOTARIZATION IS WASTEFUL, NOT WRONG
scripts/notarize-dmg.sh has no pre-flight check, so running it against an already-notarized-and-stapled DMG submits it to Apple again. Apple accepts duplicate submissions of identical bits and re-stapling is idempotent, so the OUTCOME is correct — it just costs a needless multi-minute round trip.
DO: add a `xcrun stapler validate "$DMG"` short-circuit near the top that skips submission when the DMG is already stapled, with a clear message saying so and an env override (e.g. FORCE_NOTARIZE=1) to submit anyway. Keep it a fast local check — do not call the network to decide.

2. THE DMG CONTAINER IS SIGNED WITH --timestamp=none
scripts/make-dmg.sh (~:41) signs the DMG itself without a secure timestamp. This notarizes fine today because Gatekeeper reads the STAPLED ticket for a DMG, not the container's own timestamp — so this is genuinely working, not latent breakage.
DO: decide deliberately rather than leaving it accidental. Either add `--timestamp` to the DMG signing call for conventionality, or add a comment at that line explaining why the container deliberately omits it. Note that build-app.sh's Developer ID path DOES use `--timestamp --options runtime`, because Apple hard-requires both for the app inside — the asymmetry between the two is exactly what will confuse a future reader.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT touch identity resolution (scripts/lib/resolve-codesign-identity.sh) or the designated requirement. Identity stability is what stopped the operator's repeated keychain prompts (gateopener-sal).
- Do NOT add hardened runtime to the ad-hoc fallback path — it is not required there and would surprise a contributor without a certificate.
- Do not create a git remote, run gh, or push.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Re-running notarize-dmg.sh on a stapled DMG skips submission, and FORCE_NOTARIZE=1 still submits.
- The DMG timestamp question is resolved one way or the other, with the reasoning written down at the call site.
- A fresh end-to-end run still ends with `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature` exiting 0.
- swift build; swift test; GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.

title: SPIKE: is AI face-recognition data retrievable for a video overlay?
description:
LOW PRIORITY — the user called this out explicitly as "nice ... but that's low priority". Do NOT let it block or delay the video work.

THE ASK: overlay text on the live video naming the AI-determined face, if available.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY KNOWN (do not assume more)
The door DOES advertise a face-recognition capability. In ../comelit/docs/ring-capture-2026-08-27/discovery.json there is an endpoint:
  endpointId: _DA_577fcdbf-...-00001_VIP#AP#SB000001
  friendlyName: SB000001
  capabilities: ["FaceRecognitionController", "ConfigurationController"]
That is the ENTIRETY of what is known. NO request shape, NO response shape, NO idea whether it is poll or push, NO captured traffic exercising it, and NO evidence any face data is available to a client at all. ../comelit never used it.

THIS IS A SPIKE, NOT A FEATURE. Do not build UI.
1. Search ../comelit thoroughly first: `bd memories --json` for anything face/recognition/AP#SB000001 related, plus its captures (docs/ring-capture-2026-08-27/, captures/) for any traffic touching that endpoint. Report what exists.
2. Probe the endpoint READ-ONLY against real hardware. GET-style/state-read requests only, mirroring how other controllers are read in ../comelit/comelit/client.py. DO NOT issue writes, DO NOT call power/open, DO NOT attempt to enroll/modify faces or configuration. If a call's effect is not obviously read-only, DO NOT MAKE IT.
3. Determine whether a client can retrieve a recognised-face identity, and if so: the exact request, the response shape, and crucially the TIMING — is it available during a live video session, or only after a ring event? A name that arrives after the video ends is useless for an overlay.
4. TIME-BOX to a short session. If the API shape cannot be established quickly, that is a perfectly good result: report "not discoverable without further reverse-engineering" and stop.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A written finding: either the concrete API shape and whether it is usable during a live session, or a clear statement that it is not discoverable within the time-box.

title: Tighten OverlayWindowController show()/hide() visibility to enforce the handle(_:)-only contract
description:
DISCOVERED during review of gateopener-9kk.6. NOT blocking; nothing calls these today.

PROBLEM
OverlayWindowController.show() (~:113) and hide() (~:133) are internal (non-private), but the type's design contract is that handle(_:) is the SOLE driver of presentation. Calling hide() externally while a resolve-fade is pending does not reset isResolveFadePending or cancel pendingResolveTask, so a subsequent .idle would be silently ignored and the overlay could be stranded on screen.
Today criterion-4 of bead 9kk.6 ('driven only via handle(_:)') is enforced only by grep and by reviewer vigilance, not by the type system.

DO
1. Make show() and hide() private if nothing outside the type needs them.
2. If a test or a future caller genuinely needs them, keep them internal but document them explicitly as not-for-production-use and state the pending-fade hazard on each.
3. Alternative worth considering instead of (1): have hide() itself cancel any pending resolve work and clear isResolveFadePending, making external calls SAFE rather than merely discouraged. This may be preferable, since gateopener-12h's 'View door' feature is likely to want a real user-initiated dismiss. Pick one approach and say why.
4. Do not change handle(_:)'s behavior or the focus guarantee (orderFrontRegardless only).

DONE-CRITERIA
- Either the methods are private, or they are safe to call externally (pending work cancelled and flags cleared) — not the current middle state.
- swift build + swift test still green (126 tests at time of filing).
- The self-test (GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1) still reports SELFTEST PASS.

The fix DID buy something real: the semantic now has a single named home with the rationale attached, and the dangerous half of the failure mode (someone 'simplifying' .unset into .custom(defaultChord) at the definition, where the reasoning is not visible) IS caught. The remaining mutation requires deliberately editing a line whose adjacent comment explains why not to.

2. Assert that invoking the reset action produces .unset — and that the mutation described above then FAILS. Prove it, do not assert it.

title: GateController exposes no read accessor for display state
description:
DISCOVERED during the bead .9 review; judged NON-BLOCKING there.

PROBLEM
GateController exposes no public read accessor for the signed-in username or the selected gate name, so SettingsView reads them DIRECTLY:
  SettingsView.swift:216 — KeychainCredentialStore().loadCredentials()?.username
  SettingsView.swift:220 — AppSettings().selectedEndpointName
  SettingsView.swift:381 — AppSettings().selectedEndpointId (picker getter)
All three are strictly read-only (verified — no writes through either object), and all MUTATIONS correctly route through the controller.

WHY IT MATTERS (cosmetic today)
Under GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 the controller uses a throwaway UserDefaults suite while these display paths read .standard, so the Settings window can show a blank or stale gate name in mock mode. It CANNOT cause the wrong gate to open — openGate() uses the controller's own settings — so this is a display inconsistency, not a safety issue.

DO
1. Add read-only accessors to GateController, e.g. 'public var signedInUsername: String?' and 'public var selectedGateName: String?', sourced from the controller's OWN injected credential store and AppSettings instance.
2. Repoint SettingsView at those accessors and delete the direct KeychainCredentialStore()/AppSettings() constructions from the view.
3. Verify in mock mode that Settings then reflects the controller's actual (mock-suite) state rather than .standard.

UPDATE (2026-08-27, from the gateopener-9kk.7 review) — SCOPE HAS GROWN, AND IT NOW INVOLVES A WRITE
The overlay Settings toggle added in gateopener-9kk.7 follows this same fresh-AppSettings() precedent, at SettingsView.swift ~:170-171:
    get: { AppSettings().showOpenConfirmationOverlay }
    set: { AppSettings().showOpenConfirmationOverlay = $0 }
This is the first case that WRITES through a freshly-constructed AppSettings rather than only reading. Under GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 the write lands in `.standard` while the running app reads the throwaway suite, so the toggle would appear to do nothing in mock mode. Harmless in production (both are `.standard`) and harmless for the self-test (it never opens Settings), but it is a strictly worse failure mode than the read-only cases already listed above: a silently ineffective control rather than a stale label.

So when fixing this bead, cover the WRITE path too:
- Add the accessor(s) as described below, and repoint the overlay toggle at the shared instance as well as the read-only display paths.
- Whatever mechanism is chosen must support both reading AND writing showOpenConfirmationOverlay through the controller's own AppSettings instance.
- Note that OverlayWindowController already takes AppSettings via injection (init(appSettings:ignoresMouseEvents:)), so the app-side half of this is already done correctly — it is only the SettingsView side that constructs its own.

DONE-CRITERIA
- SettingsView constructs neither KeychainCredentialStore nor AppSettings.
- Under GATEOPENER_MOCK=1, the Settings window shows the mock gate name.
- Real mode still shows the real gate name.
- swift test still fully passes.

title: AppSettings tests leave an empty plist per run in ~/Library/Preferences
description:
DISCOVERED during review of gateopener-4ub.6 (explicitly NOT pass-blocking; the bead passed).

PROBLEM
AppSettingsTests uses UserDefaults(suiteName:) with UUID-unique names and calls removePersistentDomain(forName:) in teardown. That is the documented API and it DOES erase the contents — but cfprefsd does not unlink the backing file. Measured precisely by the reviewer: BEFORE=180, AFTER=186 files in ~/Library/Preferences/, i.e. exactly +6 (one per AppSettings test) on every single run.

This is filesystem litter, not state leakage. But it grows unboundedly across dev and CI runs.

DO
1. After removePersistentDomain(forName:), also remove the backing plist file directly at ~/Library/Preferences/<suiteName>.plist, tolerating absence (the file may legitimately not exist).
2. Alternatively/additionally consider CFPreferencesAppSynchronize before removal.
3. Keep the existing UUID-unique suite names and the defer-based teardown — both were verified correct.
4. Do NOT weaken the existing guarantee: the standard UserDefaults domain must remain untouched by tests (this was explicitly verified and must stay true).

DONE-CRITERIA
- Count files in ~/Library/Preferences/ before and after a full 'swift test' run: the delta attributable to AppSettings tests is 0.
