title: Keychain tests report as passed when silently skipped
description:
DISCOVERED during review of gateopener-4ub.3 (not blocking; the bead passed).

PROBLEM
The 5 KeychainCredentialStore tests in Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/CredentialStoreTests.swift (around lines 209, 229, 246, 268, 285) self-skip by returning early via a bare 'return' when the keychain is unavailable (errSecMissingEntitlement / errSecNotAvailable / errSecInteractionNotAllowed). swift-testing then reports those tests as PASSED rather than SKIPPED.

WHY IT MATTERS
On a CI runner or any keychain-less environment, real keychain coverage would silently stop running while the suite still reports all-green. Nobody would notice coverage had evaporated. This is a CI-visibility gap, not a correctness bug — the skip logic itself was reviewed and is correct.

DO
1. Replace the bare early-return skip with a mechanism that is VISIBLE in test output. Options, in preference order: (a) swift-testing's withKnownIssue with a clear comment, (b) a recorded Issue/warning, (c) at minimum a distinctive printed marker line naming the OSStatus that caused the skip.
2. Whatever mechanism is chosen must still satisfy the original hard constraint from bead .3: a headless 'swift test' must NEVER hang on a keychain prompt and must NEVER fail the suite merely because the environment lacks keychain access.
3. Keep the UUID-unique service strings and the defer-based cleanup exactly as they are — both were verified to leave zero residue.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Running 'swift test' on this machine (keychain available) still executes all 5 keychain tests for real and passes.
- Simulating unavailability (e.g. temporarily forcing the probe to report a sentinel status) produces output that a human or CI log scan can distinguish from a genuine pass.
- No hang, no suite failure, in either mode.

value: Comelit discovery does NOT require aptId (verified live 2026-08-27, read-only GET). GET /servicerest/devicecom/endpoints/discovery with NO aptId query param returns HTTP 200 and the IDENTICAL 8-endpoint set as passing aptId explicitly (byte-identical endpointId sets). So a client never needs the user to supply an apartment id. If aptId is ever needed it is PARSEABLE from any endpointId: format is _DA_<aptId>_<deviceUuid>-00001_VIP#..., i.e. endpointId.split('_')[2]. There is NO user/apartment-list API: /servicerest/user/me, /users/me, /user/profile, /apartments, /devicecom/apartments, /installations all 404. ALSO: the useless 'Generic Actuator' (VIP#OD#SBIO0255.0) has displayCategories=['VIP_ACTUATOR'] while the real gate 'Entrance lock' (VIP#OD#SB100001.1) has ['LOCK_GENERIC'] — so filtering on displayCategories contains LOCK_GENERIC is a cleaner discriminator than excluding the id suffix, though doing BOTH is safest.

Comelit cloud NORMAL latency measured live 2026-08-27 (read-only GET discovery, 6 samples, on-LAN, good network): min 1562ms, median 1702ms, max 1939ms — i.e. ~1.6-1.9 SECONDS per call is NORMAL, not slow. This is a cloud round-trip, not a LAN call. CONSEQUENCE FOR TIMEOUT TUNING: GateClient's default RetryPolicy.requestTimeout of 3s leaves only ~1.1s of headroom over the observed median. DO NOT tighten requestTimeout to ~2s (a tempting 'improvement' to cut the 15s worst case) — that would sit barely above normal latency and would spuriously time out healthy requests, triggering unnecessary retries on a PHYSICAL GATE. If the ~15s worst case (3 attempts x 3s + ~6s backoff) needs reducing, reduce maxAttempts or maxTotalDelay instead, NOT requestTimeout. Better still: leave it and have the UI show progress during .opening, since a real open normally completes in ~2s and the 15s path only occurs when the cloud is genuinely failing.

Comelit gate selection — BOTH discriminators are independently sufficient on real data (verified against the live 8-endpoint discovery response, 2026-08-27). Of the 8 endpoints only TWO carry PowerController: 'Entrance lock' VIP#OD#SB100001.1 displayCategories=['LOCK_GENERIC'] (the REAL gate) and 'Generic Actuator' VIP#OD#SBIO0255.0 displayCategories=['VIP_ACTUATOR'] (returns HTTP 202 but has NO physical effect — inert). So filtering by id-suffix OR by displayCategories each selects correctly in isolation; using both is genuine redundancy, not nominal. DESIGN DECISION for untested sibling actuators (e.g. a hypothetical SBIO0299.0): do NOT blanket-exclude all SBIO* ids — that could hide a legitimate gate on someone else's install. Exclude only the known-bad SBIO0255.0 (matched robustly: trim whitespace, split on '_', case-insensitive compare of the LAST component), and rely on the VIP_ACTUATOR category exclusion to catch inert siblings, since inert actuators legitimately carry that category. A plain hasSuffix check is NOT sufficient — it is defeated by case variation, trailing whitespace, and mid-string occurrences.

Comelit rtc/offer HTTP 500 = DOOR BUSY, not a network fault (confirmed from chedda's unified log 2026-09-09 11:12, build 0.1.4/142, on-LAN, endpoint VIP#EN#SB100001). Timeline: View-door session B streaming from 11:12:22; a gate-open-path session C PUT rtc/offer at :32.69 -> 500 (B still streaming); B plateaued/ended :33.29; C attempt 2 at :33.65 -> 500; View-door session D at :42.97 and :43.90 (9-10s after B ended) -> 500, 500; session E at :52.38 (19s after B ended) -> 200 and streamed normally. So the door accepts ONE rtc/offer session at a time and keeps refusing with 500 for roughly 10-15s after the previous session's media stops (consistent with ICE lingering ~10s before 'failed' per gateopener-live-video-architecture). CONSEQUENCES: (1) DoorVideoSession's retry policy (2 attempts ~1s apart, 500 = retryable) can never succeed against a busy door -- it needs a ~15s cooldown or a single delayed retry; (2) any second client (the iOS app, a widget, a second Mac, or this Mac's own gate-open path racing a View-door session) makes the other one fail with 'Could not reach door camera'; (3) 'intermittent remote failure' reports must first be checked for a 500 in the log before blaming NAT/STUN. NOTE: DoorVideoOverlayController (View door) and OverlayWindowController (gate-open path) each own a SEPARATE panel (two 240x180 windows at the same screen position); they do NOT tear each other down -- an earlier draft of this memory claimed they did, which was wrong. The gate-open panel ignores mouse events, so if it is stranded nothing but the next open hides it.

Double-click during door-video warm-up: the delay is NOT in GateController (openTask joins concurrent opens; sequential re-open after .succeeded already works). It is OverlayWindowController.startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled() unconditionally calling teardownOpenVideoSession() on every .opening, which runs DoorVideoSession.stop() -> resumes pageLoadContinuation, blanks the WKWebView, and discards the in-flight rtc/offer. Fix pattern (epic gateopener-ufk): retain a session whose state is connecting/streaming, replace only ended/failed/nil; keep the frame view so the ~30s window stays anchored to the first session.

gateopener-12h.4 MEASUREMENT RESULT (2026-08-28, WKWebView, 3 runs to natural expiry, never stopped early): the ~28-30s Chromium-inherited figure is CONFIRMED for WKWebView, not just inherited -- and it is remarkably stable. Method: a temporary env-gated harness (GATEOPENER_MEASURE_DOOR_VIDEO_EXPIRY=1, removed after measurement -- git diff clean in Sources/) ran ONE DoorVideoSession per run with a 60s dwell (so the DOOR ends the session, never the harness) and polled pc.getStats()/getState() every ~500ms from the moment .streaming was reached, logging wall-clock elapsed time, framesDecoded, packetsReceived, iceConnectionState, and connectionState.

RESULTS (elapsed time measured from first .streaming, i.e. from first decoded frame):
Run 1: framesDecoded plateaus (stops increasing) at t+28.3s (last new frame in the 27.8-28.3s poll window, final value 425). iceConnectionState connected->disconnected at t+38.25s (~10s after media stopped). disconnected->failed at t+48.23s (~20s after media stopped).
Run 2: framesDecoded plateaus at t+28.87s (final value 463). connected->disconnected at t+37.77s. disconnected->failed at t+47.70s.
Run 3: framesDecoded plateaus at t+28.69s (final value 457). connected->disconnected at t+38.59s. disconnected->failed at t+48.56s.

So: media-stop time is 28.3-28.9s across all 3 runs (spread well under 1s -- very stable), matching ../comelit's Chromium-documented ~28-30s almost exactly. This is CONFIRMATION, not just an inherited assumption anymore -- the WKWebView figure and the Chromium figure agree.

WHAT HAPPENS AT EXPIRY: media stops (framesDecoded plateaus) WHILE the connection stays 'connected'/'connected' for roughly another ~9-10s, THEN transitions to 'disconnected' (~t+37.8-38.6s), THEN to 'failed' about 10s after that (~t+47.7-48.6s). This is exactly the pattern ../comelit documented for Chromium: the door simply stops sending RTP: it does not tear down the ICE/DTLS session immediately. packetsReceived (RTP packet count) keeps ticking up for a few seconds after framesDecoded plateaus (e.g. run 1: packetsReceived plateaus at t+32.0s, ~3.7s after framesDecoded plateaus at t+28.3s) -- likely non-frame-completing packets/retransmits arriving briefly after the last full frame, not new video content. DoorVideoSession.state itself (Swift's .streaming/.ended) does NOT auto-detect any of this -- the session enum stays .streaming until stop() is explicitly called; only JS-side getStats()/getState() polling reveals the plateau or the ICE state changes.

RECOMMENDATION FOR gateopener-12h.6: use framesDecoded-plateau detection as the PRIMARY trigger, not the ICE state and not a bare timer. Concretely: poll getVideoStats() on the same ~500ms cadence already used here, and treat the session as 'over' once framesDecoded has not increased for ~2-3s (6 consecutive samples at 500ms is a safe, obviously-not-a-real-stall threshold given each run's steady climb was mid-hundreds of ms per new frame). This is reliable because the plateau is the FIRST and most immediate signal (it appears text seconds before any ICE state change, and 10-20s before 'failed') and directly reflects the user-visible fact ('no new video is arriving') that should make the overlay disappear per the user's ruling -- waiting for iceConnectionState to leave 'connected' would leave the overlay showing a frozen last frame for another ~10-20s after video actually stopped, which is wrong. A hardcoded ~29s timer alone is a reasonable FALLBACK/backstop (the spread across 3 runs was under 1s, so it is not unstable) but should not be the primary signal, in case some future session runs meaningfully shorter or longer than this sample of 3 -- a plateau-detector adapts to whatever actually happens on a given call, a timer does not. Recommend: plateau-detector primary (framesDecoded unchanged for ~2-3s after having been increasing), with a ~35s hard timeout as a safety net in case the plateau-detector itself misfires (e.g. getStats() call failures) so the overlay is guaranteed to eventually disappear even if the primary signal never fires.

gateopener-12h.8 EXPERIMENT RESULT (option c, verified live 2026-08-28): canvas frame-grabbing (captureFrameJpeg, ported from ../comelit/comelit/webrtc_page.html into Resources/door-video.html) produces REAL PIXELS from DoorVideoSession.contentView even when hosted in a panel configured EXACTLY like OverlayWindowController's -- styleMask [.borderless, .nonactivatingPanel], isFloatingPanel=true, level=.statusBar, shown ONLY via orderFrontRegardless(), NEVER makeKeyAndOrderFront/NSApp.activate. Live run: video.videoWidth=320, video.videoHeight=240, framesDecoded=14, hasVideoFrame=true, and window.captureFrameJpeg(0.85) returned a valid JPEG data URL decoded to a 320x240 PNG showing the real door camera scene (driveway, cobblestones, railings, hedges, wet road) -- visually confirmed by looking at the decoded file, not inferred from stats. THIS CONTRADICTS THE EARLIER 'must become key once to composite' CORRECTED FINDING (memory gateopener-12h-8-root-cause-wkwebview-refuses-to) INSOFAR AS videoWidth/videoHeight AND hasVideoFrame populated too, in a panel that never became key at any point in this run. Possible reconciliation, NOT yet proven: the earlier finding may have been specific to a plain NSPanel/NSWindow without a WKWebViewConfiguration difference, OR the WKWebView in this run simply happened to receive layout/compositing ticks the way DoorVideoSession.contentView is now constructed (it is added to a layer-backed content view via addSubview + autoresizingMask, same as the panel-hosted production path) that an earlier isolated test did not use. RECOMMENDED PRODUCTION APPROACH for gateopener-12h.5: keep contentView.frame reasonably sized and installed into the panel's real (layer-backed) view hierarchy as done here; poll captureFrameJpeg via callAsyncJavaScript on a timer at ~8-10fps (matching the reference's 125ms interval) once state==.streaming; draw the decoded JPEG into a plain NSImageView/CALayer.contents that the non-activating panel hosts, discarding the <video> element from the visible tree entirely (canvas stays hidden, exactly as door-video.html already has it). CONCERNS to weigh in 12h.5: (1) JPEG encode+base64+decode round trip per frame is nontrivial CPU/allocation churn at 8-10fps for a 240x180 panel -- likely fine at this small size but should be profiled; (2) callAsyncJavaScript has per-call dispatch overhead, so 8-10fps (100-125ms interval) is a reasonable starting point rather than trying for smoother video; (3) frame pacing/jitter from the JS side (canvas draw + toDataURL) is unmeasured here and should be checked under sustained polling, not just a single one-off capture like this experiment ran.

SUPERSEDED — READ gateopener-live-video-architecture INSTEAD. This entry is kept only so its earlier, WRONG conclusion is not rediscovered as if new.

WHAT THIS MEMORY ORIGINALLY CLAIMED: that a WKWebView refuses to paint unless its host window is/becomes KEY, and therefore that live video could not coexist with OverlayWindowController's never-steal-focus guarantee.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, established later the same day and shipped:
1. DISPLAYING the <video> element does require a window that becomes key at least once. That part holds, and it is why the video element is never shown to the user.
2. But CANVAS CAPTURE DOES NOT. window.captureFrameJpeg() draws the frame to a hidden canvas and returns a JPEG; this works fine in a fully non-activating panel shown only via orderFrontRegardless(). Verified against real hardware: a 320x240 frame of the actual door scene was captured and confirmed by eye, and the shipped feature now streams live video into the HUD panel with the focus guarantee intact.
3. The web view DOES still need to be IN THE VIEW HIERARCHY to composite at all — omitting that was a real bug (captureFrameJpeg returned nil forever and the panel sat on 'Connecting...'). It is added as the bottom-most subview behind the opaque image view.
So the tradeoff this memory implied — live video OR keyboard focus — turned out to be FALSE. Both are had at once.

CONSEQUENCE: do not design around 'the panel must become key'. The settled architecture is: WKWebView as an offscreen media engine, frames polled at ~8fps via captureFrameJpeg through callAsyncJavaScript, decoded and drawn into a plain layer-backed NSImageView the non-activating panel hosts. See gateopener-live-video-architecture for the full recipe, the measured timings, and the plateau-detector trap.

On a REOPEN within the same run, the panel's installed content is the PREVIOUS session's DoorVideoFrameView (still showing its last decoded frame, imageView.image=SET), and handleOpening()'s show() re-fires overlayWillShow() on THAT STALE VIEW -- confirmed by log: overlayWillShow id=0xb92d93000 at 1787917520.358920 imageView.image=SET, one more captureFrameJpeg for the OLD session lands 9ms later (bytes=28744, a session-1 frame) via a poll that was already in flight, then the old view's polls go nil (session 1's WKWebView is being torn down concurrently) while it remains the panel's ONLY content -- no canned animation, no connecting placeholder -- for the ENTIRE reconnect window (measured 2.5-6.3s across three runs, ending only when the NEW session's .streaming finally arrives or fails) before any swap happens. Screenshot evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ebowman-src-gateopener/9297301e-7e87-408b-801f-0fc672fd42b2/scratchpad/f8w/open_run2_immediate.png taken 0.19s after the second .opening fired shows the live outdoor scene frozen from session 1, byte-matched via log to the imageView.image assignment at 1787917520.368535 (9ms after reopen). GATEOPENER LIVE DOOR VIDEO — SETTLED ARCHITECTURE (2026-08-28, all verified against real hardware). Read this before touching any video code.

THE CORE CONSTRAINT AND HOW IT IS SOLVED: a WKWebView only begins compositing when its host window becomes KEY at least once. OverlayWindowController's panel is .nonactivatingPanel and can NEVER become key — that is deliberate and load-bearing, because the gate is opened by global hotkey while the user types in another app and must not lose a keystroke. So the <video> element can NEVER be displayed in that panel; it would stay permanently blank.
THE SOLUTION, PROVEN: never show the <video> element at all. The WKWebView is a PURE MEDIA ENGINE. window.captureFrameJpeg(quality) in Resources/door-video.html draws the frame to a hidden canvas and returns a JPEG data URL; Swift polls it at ~8fps via callAsyncJavaScript, decodes off the main actor, and draws into a plain layer-backed NSImageView the panel hosts. Canvas capture does NOT require key status. This is the same approach ../comelit used to serve MJPEG, which is why it was already proven against this hardware.
BUT: the web view MUST still be IN THE VIEW HIERARCHY to composite at all — it is added as the bottom-most subview behind the opaque image view. Omitting that was a real bug: captureFrameJpeg returned nil forever and the panel sat on 'Connecting...'.
ALSO: the panel's content view must be wantsLayer = true or NOTHING renders while still reporting isVisible=true (gateopener-9kk.12).

MEASURED FACTS (do not re-derive):
- Time to first frame: ~6s, dominated by the cloud rtc/offer round trip. NOT reducible by changing WebRTC stack — a native libwebrtc client pays the same round trip. This is why the canned animation covers the gap on the gate-open path.
- Session length: 28.30s / 28.87s / 28.69s across three runs to natural expiry under WKWebView (<1s spread). Confirms the ~28-30s figure previously only inherited from ../comelit's Chromium work.
- At expiry framesDecoded plateaus, but ICE stays 'connected' for ANOTHER ~10s and only reaches 'failed' at ~48s. NEVER use ICE state to detect session end — it would leave a frozen picture on screen for 10+ seconds.
- Sustained ~8fps polling costs roughly 9-10% of one core across the WebContent, GPU and main processes.

THE PLATEAU-DETECTOR TRAP, worth knowing: a stalled <video> element does NOT blank or zero out — it FREEZES on its last decoded frame. So captureFrameJpeg keeps succeeding forever on identical bytes. A naive 'no frame for N seconds' detector therefore NEVER fires. The working detector compares each poll's raw JPEG bytes to the previous poll's and only counts a genuinely NEW frame. Without this every session runs out its hard-timeout backstop instead of ending at ~28-30s.

STACK FINDING: WKWebView (WebKit's own WebRTC, NOT libwebrtc) receives RTP from this door fine. The '../comelit' conclusion that the door only streams to genuine libwebrtc does NOT generalize — it was an inference by elimination from aiortc's failure and the discriminator was never isolated. No Google WebRTC.framework xcframework is needed.
OTHER GOTCHA: plain evaluateJavaScript(_:) fails with WKErrorDomain code 5 on ANY Promise-returning expression. Always use callAsyncJavaScript(_:contentWorld:) with an explicit 'return await ...;' body.

The logs show the dominant cost is THE CLOUD rtc/offer ROUND TRIP, not WebKit: run2 offer-PUT->200 took 1896ms (8863->10759ms) and run3 took 2864ms (1482->4346ms). After the answer is applied, first decoded frame follows in roughly 2.2s (run2: 10766->12970ms). So the realistic budget is ~2-3s cloud signaling + ~2s ICE/DTLS/first-frame = ~4-6s total, and it is NOT reducible by changing WebRTC stacks — a native libwebrtc client would pay the same cloud round trip. Cold-token runs add up to ~8s more for keychain + token refresh + endpoint discovery (run2: 82ms->8279ms before signaling even began); a warm token removes nearly all of that.

It is a harness artifact, NOT a fast path. Same caveat applies to any 'second immediate run got 0 packets' reading — ICE/DTLS connected fine there; RTP simply had no time to arrive before polling stopped.

USER RULING (2026-08-28), binding on the overlay/live-video work: if closeability and never-stealing-keyboard-focus ever genuinely conflict, FOCUS WINS. The user's words: 'If we have to choose between being able to close the video window, and having it steal keyboard focus, I'll choose not having it steal keyboard focus.' Rationale: the gate is routinely opened by global hotkey while the user is typing in another app, so a panel that grabs focus loses keystrokes and is worse than a panel that is awkward to dismiss.

IMPORTANT TECHNICAL NOTE: this tradeoff is very probably FALSE and should not be accepted without testing. An NSPanel can accept mouse clicks WITHOUT ever becoming key. OverlayPanel already overrides canBecomeKey and canBecomeMain to return false, and the panel is shown with orderFrontRegardless() (never makeKeyAndOrderFront, never NSApp.activate). Mouse-event delivery is governed by ignoresMouseEvents, which is a SEPARATE, independent constructor parameter on OverlayWindowController — set it false and the panel receives clicks while still never taking keyboard focus. So a click-to-dismiss button, or click-anywhere-to-dismiss, should work with the focus guarantee fully intact.
Other dismissal routes that need no mouse at all and no focus: the session ending naturally (~28-30s, the user's chosen behavior is that the overlay simply DISAPPEARS), a menu item, or the existing global hotkey.
So: try click-to-dismiss with ignoresMouseEvents=false FIRST and verify empirically that typing in another app is unaffected while the panel is visible. Only if that is proven impossible does the user's ruling bite — and then drop closeability, not the focus guarantee.
